+`--os-events` is not a config. It adds the checked-in `linux.ftrace` and
+`linux.sys_stats` sources on a dedicated 256 MiB ring buffer.
+`--os-buffer-kb` resizes that buffer. The option keeps the base config's
+duration and file streaming settings. An event covered by the base's unnamed (default)
+ftrace instance stays on its original buffer. The added source omits that event.
+Named ftrace instances do not affect the added source. Conflicting
+ftrace settings or overlapping `linux.sys_stats` polling fail before the
+daemons start. The generator preserves settings and source routing that no option
+changes.
+The OS ring holds both ftrace and system-stat samples; it does not isolate
+kernel readers or probe CPU cost. See `README.perfetto.md` for the supported
+overlap selectors and all tuning options.
+
+The six `malloc_*` application counters use TrackEvent category `sys`.
+The default `*` includes them. A finite `--categories` list disables unlisted
+categories, so keep either `*` or explicit `sys` to record them.
+`--os-events` independently adds `linux.sys_stats`. It does not enable
+malloc counters. `--trace-passes` gates malloc counters together with the
+other application TrackEvent data.

+### Capture configuration tuning
+
+Both launchers call `perfetto/generate-config`. It reads the selected protobuf
+text (PBtxt) config with the pinned schema. It changes only the requested settings
+and passes a temporary binary `TraceConfig` to the client. The launcher removes

+
+| Option | Effect |
+|---|---|
+| `--categories LIST` | Select TrackEvent categories. A finite list disables unlisted categories. Prefix the list with `+` to add exact names to the base selection instead. |
+| `--exclude-categories LIST` | Replace exact category exclusions. An empty value clears the base list. Prefix the list with `+` to add exclusions instead. |
+| `--buffer-kb N` | Set the TrackEvent buffer size in KiB. |
+| `--fill ring\|discard` | Choose what to keep when the TrackEvent buffer fills. `ring` keeps the newest data. `discard` keeps the oldest. |
+| `--duration-ms N` | Set the external trace duration. `0` removes the duration limit. In `wrapper`, this option waits for the client, so `0` requires a manual stop. |
+| `--write-period-ms N` | Set the file streaming interval. `0` disables file streaming in the generated config. Positive values must be at least 100 ms and require ring buffers. |
+| `--os-events` | Add the checked-in `linux.ftrace` and `linux.sys_stats` sources. Added sources use a dedicated ring buffer. |
+| `--os-buffer-kb N` | Set the OS-event buffer size in KiB. Requires `--os-events`. |
+| `--perfetto-config FILE` | Select a custom PBtxt base config. |
+
+`--perfetto-config` overrides tronperf's `TRON_PERFETTO_CONFIG` default. Invalid
+options, malformed configs, and ambiguous TrackEvent routing fail before the
+daemons start. The generator preserves fields and source routing that no option
+changes. See the OS-event overlap rules below.
+
+Keep either the standalone `*` selector or explicit `sys` in `--categories`
+to record the six application-side `malloc_*` counters.
+`--os-events` independently adds `linux.sys_stats`. It does not enable those
+malloc counters. `--trace-passes` gates the malloc counters along with the
+other application TrackEvent data.
+
+The external duration clock starts when Perfetto opens the capture session. It
+may start before the client reports readiness. Tron initializes its producer
+later. The application and malloc event gates open after that. Leave startup
+time in short phased captures. For a wrapper target, allow for Tron's ten-second
+SIGUSR1 trace window plus startup time.

+It parses the file with the pinned `TraceConfig` schema. It changes only the
+requested settings and writes the result to standard output.
+
+Enter the Nix shell, which supplies the schema and Python protobuf runtime:
+
+```bash
+nix develop --accept-flake-config
+perfetto/generate-config runtron \
+  --categories driver,sys --buffer-kb 1048576 --duration-ms 60000
+```
+
+A finite unsigned `--categories` list disables unlisted C++ categories. The standalone
+`*` selector keeps wildcard selection. `--exclude-categories` replaces the
+base list with exact category names. The same selector cannot appear in both
+options.
+
+Finite category overrides reject inherited `enabled_tags` selectors other than
+`*`: those tags could enable unlisted categories. For that combination, author
+the category and tag policy in the base config instead.
+
+Use one leading `+` to extend the selected base instead of replacing a list:
+
+```bash
+perfetto/generate-config runtron \
+  --categories +memory,loading --exclude-categories +scheduler
+```
+
+This enables both `memory` and `loading`, excludes `scheduler`, and keeps
+other category choices. Both launchers accept these same options. An added
+enable overrides inherited exclusions and disabled tags for that name. An
+added exclusion removes matching inherited exact enables. Other tags and
+patterns stay unchanged; no global disable fallback is added by append mode.
+
+Append mode accepts exact names, not wildcards or per-name signs such as
+`+memory,-scheduler`. Explicitly enabling and excluding the same name is an
+error. Each flag chooses its mode independently: an unsigned exclusion list
+still replaces the base exclusions, even with `--categories +LIST`. Repeated
+flags keep only their last value; use one comma-separated list per flag.
+To configure unusual names beginning with `+` or `-`, use the base PBtxt.
+
+Buffer size and fill changes apply to the buffer targeted by TrackEvent,
+including any other sources sharing it. The generator checks supported CLI
+combinations, not every Perfetto service constraint.
+
+The command writes PBtxt by default for review. Use binary protobuf when
+another Perfetto tool will read the result:
+
+```bash
+perfetto/generate-config wrapper --base-config perfetto/rinzler.cfg \
+  --format binary > /tmp/rinzler-config.bin
+```
+
+Use the launcher options above for common tuning. To change a data source or
+field that the CLI does not expose, create a PBtxt file and select it with
+`--perfetto-config`.
+

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Run a slow check in the background of a job and report it in a later step.
+#
+#   background-check.sh start NAME -- COMMAND [ARG...]
+#   background-check.sh finish NAME
+#
+# start returns immediately. finish waits for COMMAND, prints its complete log,
+# and exits with COMMAND's status, so a background failure still fails the job.
+# A passing log is collapsed; a failing log is printed expanded, followed by an
+# annotation carrying its last line. Bound COMMAND with timeout(1) so finish
+# cannot wait forever.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+usage() {
+  printf 'usage: %s start NAME -- COMMAND [ARG...] | finish NAME\n' "$0" >&2
+  exit 2
+}
+
+[[ $# -ge 2 ]] || usage
+mode=$1
+name=$2
+shift 2
+[[ "${name}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage
+state_root="${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}}"
+if [[ -n "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" ]]; then
+  # A new runner registration can reuse the same VM and temp directory. Scope
+  # state to this job so a cancelled run's leftovers cannot block its successor.
+  [[ "${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ &&
+    "${GITHUB_JOB:-}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ]] || usage
+  state_root+="/background-checks-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}-${GITHUB_JOB}"
+fi
+state_dir="${state_root}/background-check-${name}"
+
+cleanup() {
+  rm -rf -- "${state_dir}" || printf '::warning::could not remove %s\n' "${state_dir}" >&2
+  if [[ -n "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}" ]]; then
+    # Another named check may still be using this job's root.
+    rmdir -- "${state_root}" 2> /dev/null || true
+  fi
+}
+
+case "${mode}" in
+  start)
+    [[ "${1:-}" == -- && $# -ge 2 ]] || usage
+    shift
+    [[ ! -e "${state_dir}" ]] || {
+      printf 'background check %s already started\n' "${name}" >&2
+      exit 1
+    }
+    mkdir -p -- "${state_root}"
+    # Atomic creation also rejects concurrent duplicate starts within a job.
+    mkdir -- "${state_dir}"
+    date +%s > "${state_dir}/started"
+    (
+      status=0
+      "$@" > "${state_dir}/log" 2>&1 < /dev/null || status=$?
+      date +%s > "${state_dir}/finished"
+      printf '%s\n' "${status}" > "${state_dir}/status.tmp"
+      mv "${state_dir}/status.tmp" "${state_dir}/status"
+    ) < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1 &
+    # Detached from the step's output: the runner keeps a step open while
+    # anything holds its stdout or stderr.
+    printf '%s\n' "$!" > "${state_dir}/pid"
+    printf 'Started %s in the background; its result and log appear in the step that finishes it.\n' "${name}"
+    ;;
+  finish)
+    [[ $# -eq 0 ]] || usage
+    [[ -f "${state_dir}/started" ]] || {
+      printf '::error title=%s not started::see the step that should have started it\n' "${name}"
+      exit 1
+    }
+    [[ -f "${state_dir}/status" ]] || printf 'Waiting for %s to finish...\n' "${name}"
+    while [[ ! -f "${state_dir}/status" ]]; do
+      if ! kill -0 "$(< "${state_dir}/pid")" 2> /dev/null; then
+        # It may have written its status just before exiting.
+        [[ -f "${state_dir}/status" ]] && break
+        trap cleanup EXIT
+        printf '==== %s log (background process exited without a status) ====\n' "${name}"
+        cat "${state_dir}/log" 2> /dev/null || true
+        printf '==== end of %s log ====\n' "${name}"
+        printf '::error title=%s failed::background process exited without reporting a status (killed?)\n' "${name}"
+        exit 1
+      fi
+      sleep 1
+    done
+    # Only clean up after the writer has finished; an interrupted finish must
+    # not delete state while the background command is still using it.
+    trap cleanup EXIT
+    status=$(< "${state_dir}/status")
+    elapsed=$(($(< "${state_dir}/finished") - $(< "${state_dir}/started")))
+    if [[ "${status}" -eq 0 ]]; then
+      printf '::group::%s log (passed)\n' "${name}"
+      cat "${state_dir}/log"
+      printf '::endgroup::\n'
+      printf '%s passed in %s s.\n' "${name}" "${elapsed}"
+      exit 0
+    fi
+    printf '==== %s log (failed with exit status %s after %s s) ====\n' \
+      "${name}" "${status}" "${elapsed}"
+    cat "${state_dir}/log"
+    printf '==== end of %s log ====\n' "${name}"
+    # The last log line is the check's own failure message.
+    reason=$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$' "${state_dir}/log" | tail -n 1 || true)
+    # timeout(1) exits 124 without output of its own.
+    [[ "${status}" -ne 124 ]] || reason="timed out; last output: ${reason:-none}"
+    printf '::error title=%s failed (exit status %s)::%s\n' \
+      "${name}" "${status}" "${reason:-no output}"
+    exit "${status}"
+    ;;
+  *)
+    usage
+    ;;
+esac

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# A background check's failure must fail the step that finishes it and print
+# everything the check wrote.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+helper="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/background-check.sh"
+BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
+export BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR
+# These tests supply their own state root, independent of the hosting CI job.
+unset GITHUB_RUN_ID GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT GITHUB_JOB
+trap 'rm -rf "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}"' EXIT
+
+fail() {
+  printf '%s\n' "$1" >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+# A reused runner can retain an empty legacy directory or a previous job's
+# unreported result. Neither may block a new run, retry, or sibling job.
+(
+  export RUNNER_TEMP="${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/reused runner"
+  unset BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR
+  mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/background-check-reused"
+  export GITHUB_RUN_ID=100 GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=1 GITHUB_JOB=contracts
+  "${helper}" start reused -- printf 'original-job-output\n'
+  status=0
+  "${helper}" start reused -- printf 'duplicate-output\n' > /dev/null 2>&1 || status=$?
+  [[ "${status}" -eq 1 ]] || fail 'start accepted a duplicate in the same job'
+
+  for identity in '101 1 contracts' '100 2 contracts' '100 1 sibling'; do
+    read -r GITHUB_RUN_ID GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT GITHUB_JOB <<< "${identity}"
+    "${helper}" start reused -- printf 'next-job-output\n' \
+      || fail "prior state blocked job ${identity} on a reused runner"
+    output=$("${helper}" finish reused) || fail "finish rejected job ${identity}"
+    [[ "${output}" == *next-job-output* && "${output}" != *original-job-output* ]] \
+      || fail "job ${identity} reported another job's result: ${output}"
+  done
+
+  export GITHUB_RUN_ID=100 GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=1 GITHUB_JOB=contracts
+  output=$("${helper}" finish reused) || fail 'another job removed the original state'
+  [[ "${output}" == *original-job-output* && "${output}" != *duplicate-output* ]] \
+    || fail "duplicate start overwrote the original result: ${output}"
+  [[ -z "$(find "${RUNNER_TEMP}" -type f -print -quit)" ]] \
+    || fail 'finished jobs left state files behind on the reused runner'
+)
+
+"${helper}" start passing -- bash -c 'sleep 1; echo passing-output'
+"${helper}" start failing -- bash -c 'echo first-line; echo failure-reason; exit 7'
+
+output=$("${helper}" finish passing) || fail 'finish rejected a passing check'
+[[ "${output}" == *passing-output* ]] || fail "finish omitted the log: ${output}"
+[[ ! -e "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/background-check-passing" ]] \
+  || fail 'finish left successful check state behind'
+
+status=0
+output=$("${helper}" finish failing) || status=$?
+[[ "${status}" -eq 7 ]] || fail "finish returned ${status}, expected 7"
+[[ "${output}" != *'::group::'* && "${output}" == *first-line*failure-reason* ]] \
+  || fail "finish hid part of the failing log: ${output}"
+[[ "${output}" == *'::error title=failing failed (exit status 7)::failure-reason'* ]] \
+  || fail "finish did not put the failure reason in the annotation: ${output}"
+[[ ! -e "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/background-check-failing" ]] \
+  || fail 'finish left failed check state behind'
+
+# start must not hold the caller's stdout open while the check runs.
+before=$(date +%s%N)
+output=$("${helper}" start detached -- sleep 3)
+elapsed_ms=$((($(date +%s%N) - before) / 1000000))
+[[ "${elapsed_ms}" -lt 2000 ]] \
+  || fail "start held stdout open for ${elapsed_ms} ms while the check ran"
+"${helper}" finish detached > /dev/null || fail 'finish rejected the detached check'
+
+# finish must fail, not wait forever, when the background process dies.
+# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # expanded by the inner shell
+"${helper}" start killed -- bash -c 'echo "$$" > "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/child"; exec sleep 30'
+until [[ -s "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/child" ]]; do sleep 0.1; done
+kill -KILL "$(< "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/background-check-killed/pid")" \
+  "$(< "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/child")"
+status=0
+output=$(timeout 10 "${helper}" finish killed) || status=$?
+[[ "${status}" -eq 1 && "${output}" == *'exited without reporting a status'* ]] \
+  || fail "finish returned ${status} for a killed check: ${output}"
+[[ ! -e "${BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR}/background-check-killed" ]] \
+  || fail 'finish left killed check state behind'
+
+status=0
+"${helper}" finish never-started > /dev/null || status=$?
+[[ "${status}" -ne 0 ]] || fail 'finish accepted a check that never started'
+
+printf 'background-check tests passed.\n'

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Rebuild the complete lint check from a tracked-source copy with one
+# unformatted Nix file, and require the real lint derivation to reject it with
+# an actionable annotation and summary. The copy's source identity is new, so
+# this is a cold lint run; CI starts it in the background of the machinery job.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+fail() {
+  printf 'Full lint rejection check: %s\n' "$1" >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+command -v nix > /dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'nix is not available'
+
+repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
+fixture_root=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "${fixture_root}"' EXIT
+unformatted_source_root="${fixture_root}/unformatted-source"
+
+mkdir -p "${unformatted_source_root}"
+(
+  cd "${repo_root}"
+  git ls-files -z \
+    | xargs -0 -r cp -a --parents --target-directory="${unformatted_source_root}" --
+)
+python3 - "${unformatted_source_root}/flake.nix" << 'PY'
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+
+
+flake_path = Path(sys.argv[1])
+formatted = '  description = "TRON C++/Python development environment";'
+unformatted = '  description="TRON C++/Python development environment";'
+contents = flake_path.read_text()
+if contents.count(formatted) != 1:
+  raise SystemExit("flake description fixture changed")
+flake_path.write_text(contents.replace(formatted, unformatted))
+PY
+
+unformatted_check_ref="path:${unformatted_source_root}#checks.x86_64-linux.lint-toolchain"
+unformatted_drv_path=$(XDG_DATA_HOME="${fixture_root}/unformatted-xdg-data" \
+  nix eval --raw "${unformatted_check_ref}.drvPath" --no-update-lock-file)
+unformatted_build_log="${fixture_root}/unformatted-lint-build.log"
+unformatted_summary="${fixture_root}/unformatted-lint-summary.md"
+if XDG_DATA_HOME="${fixture_root}/unformatted-xdg-data" \
+  GITHUB_ACTIONS=true GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY="${unformatted_summary}" \
+  bash "${repo_root}/bin/ci/run-lint-checks.sh" "${unformatted_check_ref}" \
+  > "${unformatted_build_log}" 2>&1; then
+  cat "${unformatted_build_log}" >&2
+  fail 'lint check accepted an unformatted Nix source'
+fi
+unformatted_derivation_log="${fixture_root}/unformatted-lint-derivation.log"
+if ! nix log "${unformatted_drv_path}" \
+  > "${unformatted_derivation_log}" 2>&1; then
+  cat "${unformatted_build_log}" >&2
+  fail 'could not read the failed lint derivation log'
+fi
+grep -Fq 'flake.nix: not formatted' "${unformatted_derivation_log}" || {
+  cat "${unformatted_build_log}" >&2
+  cat "${unformatted_derivation_log}" >&2
+  fail 'the lint derivation failed without reporting the planted flake.nix formatting error; if the Lint job also failed, fix that lint error first, since it stops the lint check before nixfmt runs'
+}
+grep -q '^::error ' \
+  "${unformatted_build_log}" || {
+  cat "${unformatted_build_log}" >&2
+  fail 'lint failure did not annotate the failing Nix formatter'
+}
+grep -Fq 'flake.nix: not formatted' "${unformatted_summary}" || {
+  cat "${unformatted_summary}" >&2
+  fail 'lint failure summary omitted the formatter diagnostic'
+}
+
+printf '%s\n' 'Full lint rejection check passed.'

+          result.returncode == 0,
+          nix_status == 0,
+          result.stdout + result.stderr,

+def copy_runtime_tree(source: Path, destination: Path) -> None:
+  """Copy a store tree so that an interrupted copy stays removable."""
+  destination.mkdir()
+  destination.chmod(stat.S_IMODE(source.stat().st_mode) | stat.S_IWUSR)
+  for entry in source.iterdir():
+    if entry.is_dir() and not entry.is_symlink():
+      copy_runtime_tree(entry, destination / entry.name)
+    else:
+      shutil.copy2(entry, destination / entry.name, follow_symlinks=False)
+  metadata = source.stat()
+  os.utime(destination, ns=(metadata.st_atime_ns, metadata.st_mtime_ns))

 # A submission is "placeable" iff every slot it requested is unowned.
 
 
+def _split_system_config(system_config: str) -> list[str]:
+  """Read the std::quoted token grammar used by native SYSTEM_CONFIG."""
+  # Keep this aligned with dice_lsf.split_system_config without adding a
+  # module dependency to the standalone Dice package. Shell quoting differs.
+  tokens: list[str] = []
+  whitespace = " \t\n\r\v\f"
+  i = 0
+  while i < len(system_config):
+    if system_config[i] in whitespace:
+      i += 1
+      continue
+    if system_config[i] != '"':
+      start = i
+      while i < len(system_config) and system_config[i] not in whitespace:
+        i += 1
+      tokens.append(system_config[start:i])
+      continue
+    i += 1
+    token: list[str] = []
+    while i < len(system_config):
+      char = system_config[i]
+      i += 1
+      if char == '"':
+        tokens.append("".join(token))
+        break
+      if char == "\\":
+        if i == len(system_config):
+          raise ValueError(
+            "invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG quoting: trailing escape in double quote"
+          )
+        char = system_config[i]
+        i += 1
+      token.append(char)
+    else:
+      raise ValueError("invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG quoting: unterminated double quote")
+  return tokens
+
+
+def _join_system_config(tokens: list[str]) -> str:
+  # Native SYSTEM_CONFIG uses std::quoted, so emit double quotes and its
+  # backslash escapes rather than POSIX single quotes from shlex.join.
+  return " ".join(
+    token
+    if token and not any(c.isspace() or c in "\\\"'" for c in token)
+    else '"' + token.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
+    for token in tokens
+  )
+

+def split_system_config(system_config: str) -> list[str]:
+  """Read the std::quoted token grammar used by native SYSTEM_CONFIG."""
+  # Quotes only delimit a token when they start it. Outside double quotes,
+  # apostrophes and backslashes are literal, unlike shell/shlex parsing.
+  tokens: list[str] = []
+  whitespace = " \t\n\r\v\f"
+  i = 0
+  while i < len(system_config):
+    if system_config[i] in whitespace:
+      i += 1
+      continue
+    if system_config[i] != '"':
+      start = i
+      while i < len(system_config) and system_config[i] not in whitespace:
+        i += 1
+      tokens.append(system_config[start:i])
+      continue
+    i += 1
+    token: list[str] = []
+    while i < len(system_config):
+      char = system_config[i]
+      i += 1
+      if char == '"':
+        tokens.append("".join(token))
+        break
+      if char == "\\":
+        if i == len(system_config):
+          raise ValueError(
+            "invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG quoting: trailing escape in double quote"
+          )
+        char = system_config[i]
+        i += 1
+      token.append(char)
+    else:
+      raise ValueError("invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG quoting: unterminated double quote")
+  return tokens
+
+
+def join_system_config(tokens: list[str]) -> str:
+  # Native SYSTEM_CONFIG uses std::quoted, so emit double quotes and its
+  # backslash escapes rather than POSIX single quotes from shlex.join.
+  return " ".join(
+    token
+    if token and not any(c.isspace() or c in "\\\"'" for c in token)
+    else '"' + token.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
+    for token in tokens
+  )
+
+
 def shape_env(shape: str) -> dict[str, str]:
   shape = canonical_shape(shape)
   system_config = SHAPE_SYSTEM_CONFIG[shape]
   return {} if system_config is None else {"SYSTEM_CONFIG": system_config}
 
 
+def system_config_instance(system_config: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+  """Read only the placement component; all payload tuning remains opaque."""
+  # Remote reservations compare normalized instance pairs, not the complete
+  # tuning string. Reject duplicate or malformed placement before submission.
+  try:
+    tokens = split_system_config(system_config)
+  except ValueError as exc:
+    raise TopologyError(str(exc)) from exc
+  instance = None
+  i = 0
+  while i < len(tokens):
+    token = tokens[i]
+    if token == "--instance" or token.startswith("--instance="):
+      if instance is not None:
+        raise TopologyError("duplicate --instance in SYSTEM_CONFIG")
+      if token == "--instance":
+        i += 1
+        value = tokens[i] if i < len(tokens) else ""
+      else:
+        value = token.split("=", 1)[1]
+      if re.fullmatch(r"\d+,\d+", value) is None:
+        raise TopologyError(f"SYSTEM_CONFIG --instance expects 'X,Y'; got {value!r}")
+      x, n = map(int, value.split(","))
+      if n <= 0 or x >= n:
+        raise TopologyError(
+          f"SYSTEM_CONFIG --instance expects 0 <= X < Y; got {value!r}"
+        )
+      instance = (x, n)
+    i += 1
+  return instance
+
+
+def shape_system_config(shape: str, system_config: str) -> str:
+  # Fill in an omitted reservation boundary while retaining tuning; an
+  # explicit conflicting boundary must be corrected before OpenLava submission.
+  expected = system_config_instance(shape_env(shape).get("SYSTEM_CONFIG", ""))
+  requested = system_config_instance(system_config)
+  granted = expected or (0, 1)
+  if requested is not None and requested != granted:
+    raise TopologyError(
+      f"SYSTEM_CONFIG --instance requested {requested[0]},{requested[1]} "
+      f"conflicts with shape {shape!r} boundary {granted[0]},{granted[1]}; "
+      "use a matching --shape or --instance"
+    )
+  tokens = split_system_config(system_config)
+  if requested is None and expected is not None:
+    tokens += ["--instance", f"{expected[0]},{expected[1]}"]
+  return join_system_config(tokens)

+def get_node_budgets_mb(root: Path = Path("/"), safety_gb: int = 2) -> dict[int, int]:
+  """Per-NUMA-node budget for test anon memory, in MB.
+
+  budget[n] = node MemTotal − node hugepages − safety_gb / num_nodes
+
+  Returns {} when the kernel exposes no NUMA node directories.
+  """
+  node_root = root / "sys/devices/system/node"
+  nodes: dict[int, Path] = {}
+  for path in node_root.glob("node[0-9]*"):
+    suffix = path.name.removeprefix("node")
+    if suffix.isdigit():
+      nodes[int(suffix)] = path
+  if not nodes:
+    return {}
+  safety_mb = safety_gb * 1024 // len(nodes)
+  budgets: dict[int, int] = {}
+  for node, path in sorted(nodes.items()):
+    try:
+      text = (path / "meminfo").read_text()
+    except OSError:
+      return {}
+    match = re.search(r"MemTotal:\s+(\d+)\s+kB", text)
+    if not match:
+      return {}
+    huge_kb = 0
+    for hp_dir in (path / "hugepages").glob("hugepages-*kB"):
+      size = re.fullmatch(r"hugepages-(\d+)kB", hp_dir.name)
+      try:
+        count = int((hp_dir / "nr_hugepages").read_text().strip())
+      except (OSError, ValueError):
+        continue
+      if size:
+        huge_kb += int(size.group(1)) * count
+    budgets[node] = max(0, (int(match.group(1)) - huge_kb) // 1024 - safety_mb)
+  return budgets
+
+
+class MemoryBudget:
+  """Anon-memory admission control keyed by the NUMA nodes a launch occupies.
+
+  Tron binds an instance whose slots share one NUMA node strictly to that
+  node (numa_alloc_policy() in src/system/system.cpp), so its allocations
+  cannot spill to another node. Such a launch must fit both the system
+  budget and its node's budget. An instance that spans nodes is unbound and
+  is checked against the system budget only; its charge is split evenly
+  across the nodes it covers.
+
+  A launch that is the only work on the box bypasses the system limit, and
+  one that is the only work on its node bypasses that node's limit, but only
+  when no node this run can use could hold the test alone: waiting cannot
+  make it smaller, while waiting for a large enough node avoids an OOM.
+  Occupancy counts running tests, not charged MB, so a test with no RSS
+  estimate still occupies its node.
+  """
+
+  def __init__(self, system_mb: int, node_mb: dict[int, int], numa_of_slot: list[int]):
+    self.system_mb = system_mb
+    self.node_mb = dict(node_mb)
+    self.numa_of_slot = list(numa_of_slot)
+    self.committed_mb = 0
+    self.node_committed: dict[int, int] = {n: 0 for n in self.node_mb}
+    self.active = 0
+    self.node_active: dict[int, int] = {n: 0 for n in self.node_mb}
+    self._charges: dict[object, tuple[int, dict[int, int]]] = {}
+
+  def _nodes(self, abs_slot: int, slices: int) -> set[int]:
+    end = abs_slot + slices
+    if not self.numa_of_slot or end > len(self.numa_of_slot):
+      return set()
+    return set(self.numa_of_slot[abs_slot:end])
+
+  def _bound_node(self, abs_slot: int, slices: int) -> int | None:
+    """The node a launch is strictly bound to, if it has a node budget."""
+    nodes = self._nodes(abs_slot, slices)
+    if len(nodes) != 1:
+      return None
+    (node,) = nodes
+    return node if node in self.node_mb else None
+
+  def fits(
+    self, rss_mb: int, abs_slot: int, slices: int, *, sole_node_escape: bool = True
+  ) -> bool:
+    if not self.system_mb:
+      return True
+    if self.active and self.committed_mb + rss_mb > self.system_mb:
+      return False
+    node = self._bound_node(abs_slot, slices)
+    if node is None:
+      return True
+    if sole_node_escape and not self.node_active[node]:
+      return True
+    return self.node_committed[node] + rss_mb <= self.node_mb[node]
+
+  def first_fit(
+    self,
+    abs_starts: list[int],
+    rss_mb: int,
+    slices: int,
+    eligible_starts: list[int] | None = None,
+  ) -> int | None:
+    """First start in abs_starts that can take the test, or None to wait.
+
+    eligible_starts lists every aligned start this run may use, busy or
+    not. The sole-on-node escape applies only when none of them could hold
+    the test alone.
+    """
+    for start in abs_starts:
+      if self.fits(rss_mb, start, slices, sole_node_escape=False):
+        return start
+    for start in eligible_starts if eligible_starts is not None else abs_starts:
+      node = self._bound_node(start, slices)
+      if node is None or rss_mb <= self.node_mb[node]:
+        return None
+    for start in abs_starts:
+      if self.fits(rss_mb, start, slices):
+        return start
+    return None
+
+  def charge(self, key: object, rss_mb: int, abs_slot: int, slices: int) -> None:
+    per_node: dict[int, int] = {}
+    nodes = [n for n in sorted(self._nodes(abs_slot, slices)) if n in self.node_mb]
+    for node in nodes:
+      per_node[node] = rss_mb // len(nodes)
+      self.node_committed[node] += per_node[node]
+      self.node_active[node] += 1
+    self.committed_mb += rss_mb
+    self.active += 1
+    self._charges[key] = (rss_mb, per_node)
+
+  def release(self, key: object) -> None:
+    if key not in self._charges:
+      return
+    rss_mb, per_node = self._charges.pop(key)
+    self.committed_mb = max(0, self.committed_mb - rss_mb)
+    self.active -= 1
+    for node, mb in per_node.items():
+      self.node_committed[node] = max(0, self.node_committed[node] - mb)
+      self.node_active[node] -= 1
+
+

+"""Tests for Slice's per-NUMA ordinary-memory admission budget.
+
+Tron test binaries bind anonymous memory strictly to their slot's NUMA node
+(`numa_alloc_policy()` in src/system/system.cpp uses HWLOC_MEMBIND_BIND |
+HWLOC_MEMBIND_STRICT), so a node-0 slot cannot spill into node 1. A single
+system-wide budget let Slice co-schedule node-0 tests whose peak RSS exceeded
+node 0's non-hugepage memory; on andoria-02/14 (377 GiB, 140 x 1 GiB hugepages
+per node) the kernel OOM-killed t_generate_host_2-fast with
+CONSTRAINT_MEMORY_POLICY, nodemask=0, and the runner unit's OOMPolicy=stop
+cancelled the job.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from conftest import TRUE, required_executable
+
+GIB_KB = 1024 * 1024
+MIB = 1024
+
+# andoria-14 per-node MemTotal (kB): 395,713,224 kB total across two nodes.
+ANDORIA_NODE_KB = 197_856_612
+GENOA96_NUMA = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1]
+FAST_RSS_MB = 40_172  # t_generate_host_2-fast max_rss_mb
+SLOW_RSS_MB = 13_636  # t_generate_host_2-slow max_rss_mb
+
+
+def _run_args(**overrides):
+  values = {
+    "detach": False,
+    "remote": False,
+    "remote_shape": None,
+    "remote_host": None,
+    "remote_model": None,
+    "remote_sku": None,
+    "slot_mask": None,
+    "filter": "host",
+    "exclude_tag": None,
+    "min_slices": 1,
+    "verbose": False,
+  }
+  values.update(overrides)
+  return SimpleNamespace(**values)
+
+
+def write_node(root: Path, node: int, mem_kb: int, huge_1g: int) -> None:
+  node_dir = root / "sys/devices/system/node" / f"node{node}"
+  (node_dir / "hugepages/hugepages-1048576kB").mkdir(parents=True)
+  (node_dir / "hugepages/hugepages-2048kB").mkdir(parents=True)
+  (node_dir / "meminfo").write_text(
+    f"Node {node} MemTotal:       {mem_kb} kB\nNode {node} MemFree:        1234 kB\n"
+  )
+  (node_dir / "hugepages/hugepages-1048576kB/nr_hugepages").write_text(f"{huge_1g}\n")
+  (node_dir / "hugepages/hugepages-2048kB/nr_hugepages").write_text("0\n")
+
+
+def andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path: Path):
+  write_node(tmp_path, 0, ANDORIA_NODE_KB, 140)
+  write_node(tmp_path, 1, ANDORIA_NODE_KB, 140)
+  node_mb = slice_mod.get_node_budgets_mb(root=tmp_path, safety_gb=2)
+  system_mb = (2 * ANDORIA_NODE_KB) // MIB - 280 * 1024 - 2 * 1024
+  return slice_mod.MemoryBudget(system_mb, node_mb, GENOA96_NUMA)
+
+
+def test_node_budgets_subtract_each_nodes_hugepages(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  write_node(tmp_path, 0, ANDORIA_NODE_KB, 140)
+  write_node(tmp_path, 1, ANDORIA_NODE_KB, 100)
+
+  budgets = slice_mod.get_node_budgets_mb(root=tmp_path, safety_gb=2)
+
+  node_mb = ANDORIA_NODE_KB // MIB
+  assert budgets == {
+    0: node_mb - 140 * 1024 - 1024,
+    1: node_mb - 100 * 1024 - 1024,
+  }
+
+
+def test_node_budgets_empty_without_numa_sysfs(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  assert slice_mod.get_node_budgets_mb(root=tmp_path) == {}
+
+
+def test_node_bound_test_blocked_when_its_node_is_full(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  """The andoria-14 21:24 PDT 23-Sep placement: -slow and -fast both on node 0.
+
+  The system-wide budget (about 95 GiB) admits both; node 0 has about 47 GiB.
+  """
+  budget = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)
+  assert budget.system_mb >= SLOW_RSS_MB + FAST_RSS_MB
+
+  budget.charge("slow", SLOW_RSS_MB, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+
+  assert not budget.fits(FAST_RSS_MB, abs_slot=2, slices=1)
+  assert budget.fits(FAST_RSS_MB, abs_slot=5, slices=1)
+
+
+def test_release_frees_node_capacity(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  budget = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)
+  budget.charge("slow", SLOW_RSS_MB, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+  budget.release("slow")
+
+  assert budget.fits(FAST_RSS_MB, abs_slot=2, slices=1)
+  assert budget.committed_mb == 0
+
+
+def test_sole_test_on_node_admitted_even_if_over_node_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  """Waiting cannot shrink a test that alone exceeds its node; admit it."""
+  budget = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)
+  budget.charge("other-node", SLOW_RSS_MB, abs_slot=5, slices=1)
+
+  assert budget.fits(budget.node_mb[0] + 1024, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+
+
+def test_waits_for_a_node_that_can_hold_the_test(slice_mod):
+  """An idle undersized node must not take a test another node could hold."""
+  budget = slice_mod.MemoryBudget(200_000, {0: 88_000, 1: 48_000}, GENOA96_NUMA)
+  budget.charge("running", 30_000, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+  free = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
+  every = list(range(8))
+
+  assert budget.first_fit(free, 58_500, 1, every) is None
+  assert budget.first_fit(free, 90_000, 1, every) == 4
+
+  budget.release("running")
+  assert budget.first_fit(free, 58_500, 1, every) == 1
+
+
+def test_zero_rss_test_still_occupies_its_node_and_the_box(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  """A running test with no RSS estimate blocks an oversized companion."""
+  budget = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)

+
+  assert not budget.fits(budget.node_mb[0] + 1024, abs_slot=2, slices=1)
+  assert not budget.fits(budget.system_mb + 1024, abs_slot=5, slices=1)

+
+def test_zero_rss_test_waits_beside_an_oversized_test(slice_mod, tmp_path):

+  budget.charge("oversized", budget.system_mb + 1024, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+
+  assert not budget.fits(0, abs_slot=5, slices=1)
+
+
+def test_spanning_test_checks_system_budget_only(slice_mod, tmp_path):
+  """Tron leaves a multi-node instance unbound (SYSTEM_NUMA_ALL)."""
+  budget = andoria_budget(slice_mod, tmp_path)
+  budget.charge("slow", SLOW_RSS_MB, abs_slot=0, slices=1)

+def test_system_budget_applies_with_and_without_numa_data(slice_mod, tmp_path):

+  no_numa = slice_mod.MemoryBudget(100_000, {}, [])
+  no_numa.charge("a", 50_000, abs_slot=0, slices=1)
+  assert no_numa.fits(40_000, abs_slot=2, slices=1)
+  assert not no_numa.fits(60_000, abs_slot=2, slices=1)

+def ingest_moe_router(ingest: dict, name: str) -> str:
+  """Return ingest.moe_router, or 'fpga' if it is absent.
+
+  Raise ValueError for any value other than 'cpu' or 'fpga'.
+  """
+  moe_router = ingest.get("moe_router", "fpga")
+  if moe_router not in ("cpu", "fpga"):
+    raise ValueError(
+      f"{name}: ingest.moe_router must be 'cpu' or 'fpga', got {moe_router!r}"
+    )
+  return moe_router

 class TestBuildModelLocalConfig(unittest.TestCase):
+  # ROUTER_REGISTRY is a local config with two plugins, local_cpu and
+  # local_fpga, one per router policy. REGISTERED_ROUTERS adds two plugins of
+  # the canonical registry: ingested_gpt_oss_20b (cpu) and
+  # ingested_mixtral_8x7b (fpga).
+  ROUTER_REGISTRY = "models:\n" + "".join(
+    f"  - name: local_{policy}\n    hf_id: org/local-{policy}\n"
+    "    support_level: working\n    ingest:\n      source: generated\n"
+    f"      moe_router: {policy}\n"
+    f"    variants:\n      - slug: ingested-local-{policy}\n"
+    f"        executors: [tp1]\n        default_weights: org/local-{policy}\n"
+    for policy in ("cpu", "fpga")
+  )
+  REGISTERED_ROUTERS = (
+    ("local_cpu", "cpu"),
+    ("local_fpga", "fpga"),
+    ("ingested_gpt_oss_20b", "cpu"),
+    ("ingested_mixtral_8x7b", "fpga"),
+  )
+
+  @staticmethod
+  def _ingest_argv(name: str, config: Path, trace_dir: str) -> list[str]:
+    return [
+      "build-model.py",
+      "--model",
+      "fixture-model",
+      "--name",
+      name,
+      "--trace-dir",
+      trace_dir,
+      "--skip-export",
+      "--config",
+      str(config),
+      "--ingest-bin",
+      "/fixture/ingest",
+    ]

+  def test_omitted_router_policy_follows_the_registry(self) -> None:
+    build_model = load_build_model_module()
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+      config = Path(directory) / "models.local.yaml"
+      for name, expected in self.REGISTERED_ROUTERS + (("unregistered", "fpga"),):
+        for no_config in (False, True):
+          with self.subTest(name=name, no_config=no_config):
+            config.write_text(self.ROUTER_REGISTRY)
+            argv = self._ingest_argv(name, config, directory)
+            if no_config:
+              argv.append("--no-config")
+            with (
+              mock.patch.object(sys, "argv", argv),
+              mock.patch.object(build_model.subprocess, "run") as run,
+            ):
+              build_model.main()
+            command = run.call_args.args[0]
+            self.assertEqual(command[command.index("--moe-router") + 1], expected)
+            if no_config:
+              self.assertEqual(config.read_text(), self.ROUTER_REGISTRY)
+            else:
+              # A registered plugin keeps its entry. An unregistered one gains
+              # an entry that records the policy.
+              self.assertTrue(
+                build_model.config_has_plugin(config, "unused-slug", name, expected)
+              )

+  def test_explicit_router_policy_must_match_the_registry(self) -> None:

+      config.write_text(self.ROUTER_REGISTRY)

+          for no_config in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(name=name, policy=policy, no_config=no_config):
+              argv = self._ingest_argv(name, config, directory)

+                argv.append("--no-config")

+                mock.patch.object(sys, "argv", argv),
+                mock.patch.object(build_model.subprocess, "run") as run,
+              ):

+                  build_model.main()
+                  command = run.call_args.args[0]
+                  self.assertEqual(command[command.index("--moe-router") + 1], policy)
+                else:
+                  with self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as error:
+                    build_model.main()
+                  self.assertEqual(error.exception.code, 2)
+                  run.assert_not_called()
+              self.assertEqual(config.read_text(), self.ROUTER_REGISTRY)

+class TestIngestRouterBuildPaths(unittest.TestCase):
+  def test_cmake_rebuilds_when_only_router_policy_changes(self) -> None:
+    cmake = shutil.which("cmake")
+    if cmake is None:
+      self.skipTest("cmake is required")
+    repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+    source = (repo / "ingest/CMakeLists.txt").read_text()
+    macro = (
+      "macro(populate_ingest_model"
+      + source.split("macro(populate_ingest_model", 1)[1].split("endmacro()", 1)[0]
+      + "endmacro()\n"
+    )
+    for generator, tool in (("Ninja", "ninja"), ("Unix Makefiles", "make")):
+      with (
+        self.subTest(generator=generator),
+        tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory,

+### Hugepage sizing
+
+Runtron and Rinzler default to 48 one-GiB hugepages per process when launched
+through Dice wrappers, independent of the number of assigned cards. Other
+payloads and legacy execution keep their existing defaults. Runtron accepts an
+explicit size through either the local or remote wrapper:
+
+```bash
+# Request 64 pages with a local card partition.
+bin/runtron --instance 0,4 --nr_hugepages 64 -m <cached-model> -l 100
+# Request 96 pages on a remote worker.
+bin/runtron --remote --nr_hugepages 96 -m <cached-model> -l 100
+```
+
+Dice also preserves `POS_NR_HUGEPAGES` and `POS_1GB_PER_NUMA`. Existing payload
+precedence is unchanged: `POS_1GB_PER_NUMA` scales by the instance's slice count
+and takes precedence over `POS_NR_HUGEPAGES`, which takes precedence over the
+count in `SYSTEM_CONFIG`, then the command-line count. `--kv-cache-gb` is also
+forwarded; its normal allocator-mode behavior still applies. Dice supplies
+the instance in shared `SYSTEM_CONFIG`
+and preserves its other tuning fields through local and remote serving
+wrappers. Explicit settings remain subject to the native grant checks.
+
+These are allocation requests, not Dice memory reservations. The count must fit
+the worker's available hugepages and be divisible by the instance's slice count;
+the existing memlock cap still applies. Dice does not provision additional pages.
+`--hugepage_file` and `POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH` must resolve to the supported shared
+base path. Equivalent path spellings are accepted; a different allocation or
+cleanup namespace fails with a path-conflict error. The parent directory alone
+is not sufficient because startup also cleans the exact base path.
+
+Workers need the updated `positron-dice` package and rebuilt payload binaries.
+Drain and restart Dice using the normal [upgrade procedure](#worker-requirements);
+updating the checkout alone leaves the running daemon's old restrictions active.

+  // Note [BF16 bits through float]
+  // ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+  // to_bits() returns the stored bits when clang reads them from memory. If the
+  // same code also converts the value to float, or passes it by value to a call
+  // that is not inlined, clang can instead hold the value as float in a register
+  // and narrow it back to BF16 where it needs the 16 bits. It can also rewrite a
+  // bit test such as to_bits() & 0x7fff as fabs of that float. With AVX512-BF16
+  // (-mavx512bf16, as in host builds), clang 19 narrows with VCVTNEPS2BF16, which
+  // flushes subnormals to zero and quiets signaling NaNs; see
+  // https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/221052. Without AVX512-BF16 it
+  // calls __truncsfbf2, which keeps both.
+  //
+  // So code that classifies BF16 values by their bits reads each value where it
+  // is stored, and neither converts that value to float nor passes it by value
+  // to a call that is not inlined.
   TRON(nodiscard, inline, pure)
   constexpr uint16_t to_bits() const noexcept {
     return std::bit_cast<uint16_t>(content);

+// Positional variant of read_exact_fd: reads from `offset` without disturbing
+// the fd's own file offset, so several threads can read disjoint regions of one
+// entry through a single shared fd.
+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+bool read_exact_at_fd(int fd, std::span<char> buf, size_t offset) noexcept {
+  char* cursor = buf.data();
+  size_t bytes = buf.size();
+  auto read_offset = static_cast<off_t>(offset);
+  while (bytes != 0) {
+    size_t const chunk =
+        std::min(bytes, static_cast<size_t>(std::numeric_limits<ssize_t>::max()));
+    ssize_t const n = ::pread(fd, cursor, chunk, read_offset);
+    if (n > 0) {
+      cursor += n;
+      bytes -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
+      read_offset += static_cast<off_t>(n);
+    } else if (n == 0) {
+      return false;
+    } else if (errno != EINTR) {
+      return false;
+    }
+  }
+  return true;
+}

+inline constexpr size_t kParallelPrequantReadStreams = 8;
+
+// At or above this payload size, read_payload_and_submit_regions reads each
+// fetcher region and submits its DMA upload in parallel; smaller payloads use a
+// single serial read, where the thread hand-off costs more than it saves.
+inline constexpr size_t kParallelPrequantReadMinBytes = size_t(2) * 1024 * 1024;
+
+// Read a whole cache payload into `payload` and submit every fetcher region's
+// DMA. Reads and submits are interleaved rather than phased, so a region is in
+// flight while later regions are still being read off disk. `payload` must be
+// the whole tensor (fetcher_bytes * FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE) and must outlive the
+// returned transfers: it is the DMA source. Returns false on a short read, in
+// which case the caller must still wait on whatever was already submitted.
+TRON(nodiscard, inline)
+bool read_payload_and_submit_regions(prequant_cache_reader& reader,
+    std::span<uint8_t> payload,
+    device_map const& map,
+    size_t fetcher_bytes,
+    std::vector<weight_fetcher_transfer>& uploads) noexcept {
+  TRON_ASSERT(fetcher_bytes != 0);
+  TRON_ASSERT_EQ(payload.size(), fetcher_bytes * FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE);
+  if (payload.empty()) return true;
+
+  // The reader fills the payload as char; the region views hand raw bytes to
+  // the DMA ABI. Same buffer, two byte views.
+  std::span<char> const char_payload(
+      reinterpret_cast<char*>(payload.data()), payload.size());
+
+  // A pool with no workers runs nothing: thread_pool::parallel_for enqueues one
+  // task per worker, so with zero of them the body never executes, the latch
+  // releases immediately, and the parallel path below would report success over
+  // an unread payload. The pool is sized app_get_num_cpus() - 1, so a single-CPU
+  // app allocation is exactly that case. Read serially instead -- slower, and
+  // correct.
+  if (payload.size() < kParallelPrequantReadMinBytes || app_pool().num_workers() == 0) {
+    if (!reader.read_payload(char_payload)) return false;
+    for (size_t f = 0; f < FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE; ++f) {
+      submit_weight_region_uploads(
+          map, f, payload.subspan(f * fetcher_bytes, fetcher_bytes), uploads);
+    }
+    return true;
+  }
+
+  // Each worker owns a strided subset of the fetchers and reads its regions
+  // positionally, so the workers share one fd without contending on its
+  // offset. Per-worker upload vectors are merged in fetcher order afterwards,
+  // which keeps `uploads` deterministic regardless of how the workers raced.
+  size_t const workers = std::min(FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE, kParallelPrequantReadStreams);
+  std::array<std::vector<weight_fetcher_transfer>, FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE> region_uploads;
+  std::atomic<bool> ok{true};
+  app_pool().parallel_for(size_t(0), workers, [&](size_t worker) {
+    for (size_t f = worker; f < FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE; f += workers) {
+      if (!ok.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) return;
+      size_t const offset = f * fetcher_bytes;
+      // kPrequantPayloadOffset, not sizeof(header): the payload starts after a
+      // zero-filled gap, and these reads are positional so they do not inherit
+      // the seek open() already did for the serial path.
+      bool const read_ok = read_exact_at_fd(reader.fd,
+          char_payload.subspan(offset, fetcher_bytes), kPrequantPayloadOffset + offset);
+      if (!read_ok) {
+        ok.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        return;
+      }
+      submit_weight_region_uploads(
+          map, f, payload.subspan(offset, fetcher_bytes), region_uploads[f]);
+    }
+  });
+
+  for (auto& region : region_uploads) {
+    uploads.insert(uploads.end(), region.begin(), region.end());
+  }
+  return ok.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+}
+

+#pragma once
+
+/// \file
+/// \brief asynchronous weight-fetcher DMA transfers
+///
+/// A weight transfer is a submit and a later wait. Keeping the two apart lets a
+/// caller put every fetcher of a tensor -- and every device it is replicated to
+/// -- in flight before waiting on any of them, which is the difference between
+/// serializing on DMA latency and being bounded by DMA bandwidth.
+
+#include <cstddef>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <span>
+#include <vector>
+
+#include "common/attributes.hpp"
+#include "libpos.hpp"
+#include "pos/device.hpp"
+#include "tron/hardware/driver.hpp"
+
+namespace tron::hardware {
+
+// One in-flight fetcher upload. The device is carried alongside the transfer
+// state because waiting needs both and nothing else reliably recovers the
+// device from the state.
+struct weight_fetcher_transfer {
+  PosDevice* dev = nullptr;
+  // Which fetcher this upload targets. Carried because the caller merges
+  // per-worker results in fetcher order and nothing else recovers that order
+  // from the transfer state -- an assertion on `dev` alone cannot see it, since
+  // every transfer of one tensor shares a device.
+  size_t fetcher = 0;
+  dma_xfer_state transfer{};
+};
+
+TRON(inline)
+weight_fetcher_transfer submit_hardware_weight_fetcher_ready(PosDevice* dev,
+    hbm_address_t base,
+    size_t fetcher,
+    // NOT noescape. The submit returns before the DMA has read `data`; the
+    // engine sources from it until the matching wait_for_weight_fetcher_transfer.
+    // Promising the compiler it does not escape would license treating the
+    // caller's buffer as dead the moment this returns.
+    uint8_t const* data,
+    size_t len) noexcept {
+  return weight_fetcher_transfer{
+      .dev = dev,
+      .fetcher = fetcher,
+      .transfer = xfer_blocks(dev, dev->load_weight_q, base, fetcher, data, len, false),
+  };
+}
+
+// Compatibility entry point. Both names submit to the load-weight queue;
+// libpos handles descriptor admission without TX/RX matmul-worker readiness.
+TRON(inline)
+weight_fetcher_transfer submit_hardware_weight_fetcher(PosDevice* dev,
+    hbm_address_t base,
+    size_t fetcher,
+    uint8_t const* data,  // NOT noescape -- see the _ready overload
+    size_t len) noexcept {
+  return submit_hardware_weight_fetcher_ready(dev, base, fetcher, data, len);
+}
+
+TRON(inline)
+void wait_for_weight_fetcher_transfer(weight_fetcher_transfer const& upload) noexcept {
+  wait_for_xfer_blocks(upload.dev, upload.transfer);
+}
+
+TRON(inline)
+void wait_for_weight_fetcher_transfers(
+    std::vector<weight_fetcher_transfer> const& uploads) noexcept {
+  for (auto const& upload : uploads) {
+    wait_for_weight_fetcher_transfer(upload);
+  }
+}
+
+// Submit one fetcher's bytes to every device the tensor is replicated to. The
+// source buffer must outlive the returned transfers: it is the DMA source, not
+// a staged copy.
+TRON(inline)
+void submit_weight_region_uploads(device_map const& map,
+    size_t fetcher,
+    std::span<uint8_t const> region,
+    std::vector<weight_fetcher_transfer>& uploads) noexcept {
+  uploads.reserve(uploads.size() + map.mask.count());
+  for (process_device_id dev_idx : map.mask) {
+    PosDevice* dev = get_device(dev_idx);
+    // .data()/.size() cross into the hardware DMA ABI (xfer_blocks).
+    uploads.push_back(submit_hardware_weight_fetcher(
+        dev, map.addresses[dev_idx], fetcher, region.data(), region.size()));
+  }
+}
+

+#pragma once
+
+#include <array>
+#include <bit>
+#include <cmath>
+#include <cstddef>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <immintrin.h>
+#include <limits>
+#include <type_traits>
+
+#include "common/assert.hpp"
+#include "common/numerics/bf16.hpp"
+#include "tron/kernels/expr.hpp"
+#include "tron/simd.hpp"
+#include "tron/simd/aligned.hpp"
+#include "tron/tensor/seq.hpp"
+#include "tron/tensor/view.hpp"
+#include "tron/tensor/views.hpp"
+
+namespace tron {
+
+// Note [BF16 matmul range]
+// ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+// BF16 dot instructions (_mm512_dpbf16_ps) flush subnormal products and partial
+// sums to zero. bf16_dot_operand<K> accepts only BF16 values for which a K-term
+// dot product has no subnormal product or partial sum and cannot overflow. These
+// values form the packed range, so called because weight_matrix packs a weight
+// only when every element is in it. On such operands these instructions never
+// flush a value that FP32 FMA would keep. A value is in the packed range if it
+// is zero or if its exponent e = floor(log2(|x|)) satisfies
+//
+//   -56 <= e <= (125 - ceil(log2(K))) / 2, rounded down.
+//
+// - Lower bound: a BF16 value has 8 significant bits, so a nonzero value is a
+//   multiple of 2^(e - 7). The product of two operands with e >= -56 is then
+//   a multiple of 2^-126, the smallest normal FP32 value. So is every partial
+//   sum, even after FP32 rounding. A nonzero multiple of 2^-126 is never
+//   subnormal.
+// - Upper bound: each product is below 2^(127 - ceil(log2(K))). The sum of
+//   the K absolute products is therefore below 2^127 and cannot overflow.
+//
+// Both operands must be in the packed range. weight_matrix checks the weights
+// before packing them, and matvec_packed checks the activations of a token
+// before running row_dot on them. If one is outside the packed range,
+// matvec_packed runs the token on the FP32 fallback.
+namespace host_matvec_detail {
+template <size_t K>
+struct operand_range {
+  static_assert(K > 0);
+  static constexpr int growth = std::bit_width(K - 1);
+  static constexpr int max_exponent = (125 - growth) / 2;
+  static constexpr uint16_t minimum = (127 - 56) << 7;
+  static constexpr uint16_t maximum = ((127 + max_exponent) << 7) | 0x7f;
+};
+inline constexpr uint32_t nan_flag = 1, range_flag = 2;
+inline constexpr uint16_t bf16_infinity_bits =
+    std::numeric_limits<bf16>::infinity().to_bits();
+
+// Classifies the stored bits of value, as bf16_dot_operand does.
+// See Note [BF16 bits through float] in h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp.
+constexpr bool bf16_is_nan(const bf16& value) noexcept {
+  return (value.to_bits() & 0x7fff) > bf16_infinity_bits;
+}
+}  // namespace host_matvec_detail
+
+// See Note [BF16 matmul range]. Classifies the stored bits of value.
+// See Note [BF16 bits through float] in h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp.
+template <size_t K>
+constexpr bool bf16_dot_operand(const bf16& value) noexcept {
+  using limits = host_matvec_detail::operand_range<K>;
+  const auto magnitude = value.to_bits() & 0x7fff;
+  return magnitude == 0 ||
+         (magnitude >= limits::minimum && magnitude <= limits::maximum);
+}
+
+// An M x K BF16 weight matrix for matvec_packed. Each row is padded with zeros
+// to padded_cols, a multiple of 32, so every row starts on a 64-byte boundary.
+// Callers store only values that satisfy bf16_dot_operand<K>. weight_matrix
+// checks this before packing.
+template <size_t M, size_t K>
+struct bf16_matmul_weights {
+  static_assert(M > 0 && K > 0);
+  using layout = padded_row_major<32, seq<M, K>>;
+  static constexpr size_t padded_cols = seq_head<layout>;  // Row stride.
+  alignas(64) std::array<bf16, M * padded_cols> data{};
+
+  tron::view<bf16, true, false, seq<M, K>, layout> as_view() noexcept {
+    return tron::view<bf16, true, false, seq<M, K>, layout>(data.data());
+  }
+  const_view<bf16, true, false, seq<M, K>, layout> as_view() const noexcept {
+    return const_view<bf16, true, false, seq<M, K>, layout>(data.data());
+  }
+};
+
+namespace host_matvec_detail {
+
+template <typename T>
+inline constexpr bool contiguous_bf16_row = false;
+template <bool aligned, bool dma, size_t K>
+inline constexpr bool
+    contiguous_bf16_row<const_view<bf16, aligned, dma, seq<K>, sseq<1>>> = true;
+template <bool aligned, bool dma, size_t K>
+inline constexpr bool contiguous_bf16_row<view<bf16, aligned, dma, seq<K>, sseq<1>>> =
+    true;
+
+// See Note [BF16 matmul range].
+template <size_t K>
+uint32_t contiguous_operand_flags(const bf16* input) noexcept {
+  using limits = operand_range<K>;
+  uint16x16 largest, smallest_nonzero_minus_one(0xffff);
+  size_t k = 0;
+  for (; k + 16 <= K; k += 16) {
+    const uint16x16 magnitude = uint16x16(mm256_load_si256<false>(
+                                    reinterpret_cast<const bf16x16*>(input + k))) &
+                                uint16x16(0x7fff);
+    largest = max(largest, magnitude);
+    // Subtracting one maps zero to 0xffff, excluding it from the minimum.
+    smallest_nonzero_minus_one =
+        min(smallest_nonzero_minus_one, magnitude - uint16x16(1));
+  }
+  // A NaN loaded above makes an element of largest exceed infinity's bits.
+  const uint16x16 nans = _mm256_cmpgt_epi16(largest, uint16x16(bf16_infinity_bits));
+  const uint16x16 above = _mm256_cmpgt_epi16(largest, uint16x16(limits::maximum));
+  const uint16x16 lower_bound(limits::minimum - 1);
+  const uint16x16 bounded_min = min(smallest_nonzero_minus_one, lower_bound);
+  uint32_t flags =
+      uint32_t(nans != uint16x16{}) * nan_flag |
+      uint32_t(above != uint16x16{} || bounded_min != lower_bound) * range_flag;
+  for (; k < K; ++k)
+    flags |= uint32_t(bf16_is_nan(input[k])) * nan_flag |
+             uint32_t(!bf16_dot_operand<K>(input[k])) * range_flag;
+  return flags;
+}
+
+// See Note [BF16 matmul range].
+template <size_t K, typename Activation>
+uint32_t operand_flags(const Activation& act) noexcept {
+  if constexpr (contiguous_bf16_row<Activation>)
+    return contiguous_operand_flags<K>(act.data);
+  using scalar = std::remove_cvref_t<decltype(act[0])>;
+  uint32_t flags = 0;
+  for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k) {
+    const auto& value = act[k];
+    if constexpr (std::is_same_v<scalar, bf16>) {
+      flags |= uint32_t(bf16_is_nan(value)) * nan_flag |
+               uint32_t(!bf16_dot_operand<K>(value)) * range_flag;
+    } else {
+      flags |= uint32_t(std::isnan(float(value))) * nan_flag;
+    }
+  }
+  return flags;
+}
+
+// Computes result[m] = dot(rows[m], act) in FP32 for M x K rows: the as_view()
+// of packed weights, or FP32 storage. A NaN activation fails an assertion.
+template <size_t M, size_t K, typename Rows, typename Result, typename Activation>
+void fallback(const Rows& rows, Result&& result, const Activation& act) noexcept {
+  TRON_ASSERT(!(operand_flags<K>(act) & nan_flag), "NaN in host matvec activation");
+  for (size_t m = 0; m < M; ++m)
+    result[m] = dot(rows[m], act);
+}
+
+#if defined(TRON_AVX512_ENABLED) && defined(__AVX512BF16__)
+// Adds the 32 elements of both accumulators in FP64 and rounds the total to FP32
+// once. An FP32 merge would round after every addition and could lose small
+// terms.
+// TODO: use #4366's reduce_sum_fp64 once the shared FP64 merge lands.
+inline float reduce_sum_fp64(__m512 a, __m512 b) noexcept {
+  const auto a_lo = _mm512_cvtps_pd(_mm512_castps512_ps256(a));
+  const auto a_hi = _mm512_cvtps_pd(_mm512_extractf32x8_ps(a, 1));
+  const auto b_lo = _mm512_cvtps_pd(_mm512_castps512_ps256(b));
+  const auto b_hi = _mm512_cvtps_pd(_mm512_extractf32x8_ps(b, 1));
+  const auto quarters =
+      _mm512_add_pd(_mm512_add_pd(a_lo, a_hi), _mm512_add_pd(b_lo, b_hi));
+  const auto halves = _mm256_add_pd(
+      _mm512_castpd512_pd256(quarters), _mm512_extractf64x4_pd(quarters, 1));
+  const auto pairs =
+      _mm_add_pd(_mm256_castpd256_pd128(halves), _mm256_extractf128_pd(halves, 1));
+  const auto sum = _mm_add_sd(pairs, _mm_unpackhi_pd(pairs, pairs));
+  return _mm_cvtss_f32(_mm_cvtsd_ss(_mm_setzero_ps(), sum));
+}
+
+template <size_t outputs, size_t M, size_t K, typename Result>
+void row_dot_block(const bf16_matmul_weights<M, K>& weights,
+    Result&& result,
+    const bf16* x,
+    size_t first_output,
+    size_t last_output) noexcept {
+  const auto rows = weights.as_view();
+  for (size_t m = first_output; m < last_output; m += outputs) {
+    const bf16* w[outputs];
+    for (size_t j = 0; j < outputs; ++j)
+      w[j] = rows[m + j].data;
+    __m512 a[outputs]{}, c[outputs]{};
+    size_t k = 0;
+    for (; k + 64 <= K; k += 64) {
+      const auto x0 = (__m512bh)mm512_load_si512<false>(x + k);
+      const auto x1 = (__m512bh)mm512_load_si512<false>(x + k + 32);
+      for (size_t j = 0; j < outputs; ++j) {
+        const auto w0 = (__m512bh)mm512_load_si512<true>(w[j] + k);
+        const auto w1 = (__m512bh)mm512_load_si512<true>(w[j] + k + 32);
+        a[j] = _mm512_dpbf16_ps(a[j], w0, x0);
+        c[j] = _mm512_dpbf16_ps(c[j], w1, x1);
+      }
+    }
+    if (k + 32 <= K) {
+      const auto x0 = (__m512bh)mm512_load_si512<false>(x + k);
+      for (size_t j = 0; j < outputs; ++j)
+        a[j] = _mm512_dpbf16_ps(a[j], (__m512bh)mm512_load_si512<true>(w[j] + k), x0);
+      k += 32;
+    }
+    if constexpr (K % 32) {
+      const auto tail = (__m512bh)_mm512_maskz_loadu_epi16(
+          __mmask32((uint32_t{1} << (K % 32)) - 1), x + k);
+      for (size_t j = 0; j < outputs; ++j) {
+        const auto w_tail = (__m512bh)mm512_load_si512<true>(w[j] + k);
+        if constexpr ((K / 32) % 2)
+          c[j] = _mm512_dpbf16_ps(c[j], w_tail, tail);
+        else
+          a[j] = _mm512_dpbf16_ps(a[j], w_tail, tail);
+      }
+    }
+    for (size_t j = 0; j < outputs; ++j)
+      result[m + j] = reduce_sum_fp64(a[j], c[j]);
+  }
+}
+
+template <size_t M, size_t K, typename Result, typename Activation>
+void row_dot(const bf16_matmul_weights<M, K>& weights,
+    Result&& result,
+    const Activation& act) noexcept {
+  static_assert(contiguous_bf16_row<Activation>);
+  // Pairs of output rows reuse each loaded activation vector. Both block shapes
+  // sum a dot in the same order, so the pairing changes no result.
+  constexpr size_t paired = M / 2 * 2;
+  row_dot_block<2>(weights, result, act.data, 0, paired);
+  row_dot_block<1>(weights, result, act.data, paired, M);
+}
+
+#endif
+
+}  // namespace host_matvec_detail
+
+// Computes result[m] = sum_k w[m][k] * act[k] for one token, where w is the
+// packed weight matrix. On AVX-512 BF16 builds it runs row_dot when act is a
+// contiguous BF16 row whose values satisfy bf16_dot_operand<K>. Otherwise it
+// runs the FP32 fallback. A NaN activation fails an assertion.
+template <size_t M, size_t K, typename Result, typename Activation>
+void matvec_packed(const bf16_matmul_weights<M, K>& weights,
+    Result&& result,
+    const Activation& act) noexcept {
+  static_assert(std::is_same_v<typename std::remove_cvref_t<Result>::dim, seq<M>>);
+  static_assert(std::is_same_v<typename Activation::dim, seq<K>>);
+#if defined(TRON_AVX512_ENABLED) && defined(__AVX512BF16__)
+  // A NaN is outside the packed range, so it reaches the fallback's assertion.
+  if constexpr (host_matvec_detail::contiguous_bf16_row<Activation>)
+    if (!(host_matvec_detail::operand_flags<K>(act) & host_matvec_detail::range_flag))
+      return host_matvec_detail::row_dot(weights, result, act);
+#endif
+  host_matvec_detail::fallback<M, K>(weights.as_view(), result, act);
+}

+// Query-only rotary amplitude scaling. Where rope_scaling reshapes the inverse
+// frequencies (and so applies to queries and keys alike), this scales only the
+// amplitude of the query's rotary table, as a function of absolute position.
+// A rope_cfg carrying this belongs to the query side alone: handing the same
+// cfg to key rotation would scale the keys too, which no model family does.
+enum class rope_query_scaling { none, llama4 };
+
+struct llama4_rope_query_scaling_params {

+  float original_context_length;

+    rope_config_detail::enforce_positive_finite(
+        original_context_length, "Llama4 query scaling original context length");
+  }
+};

+template <rope_query_scaling strategy>
+struct rope_query_scale {
+  static_assert(no<std::integer_sequence<rope_query_scaling, strategy>>,
+      "Unknown rope query scaling strategy");
+};

+template <>
+struct rope_query_scale<rope_query_scaling::none> {
+  static constexpr rope_query_scaling strategy = rope_query_scaling::none;
+
+  rope_query_scale() noexcept {}
+
+  TRON(nodiscard, inline, const)
+  float operator()(uint32_t) const noexcept {
+    return 1.0f;
+  }
+};

+// Llama 4 style query scaling, matching this model family's reference exactly:
+//   1 + beta * log1p(floor(pos / original_context_length))
+//
+// The reference is transformers' ministral3 get_llama_4_attn_scale:
+//
+//   scaling = 1 + beta * torch.log(1 + torch.floor(positions_ids
+//                                                  / max_position_embeddings))
+//
+// Note what that function does NOT do, despite its name: it floors the position
+// directly, with no `+ 1`. Transformers' own Llama 4 computes
+// `log1p(floor((positions + 1) / floor_scale)) * attn_scale + 1`, which steps one
+// position earlier. Copying Llama 4's spelling here is a real off-by-one -- it
+// makes the amplitude wrong at pos == original_context_length - 1 and at every
+// multiple after it -- so match ministral3, not llama4, however the enumerator
+// is spelled.
+//
+// The floor is required: the amplitude is exactly 1.0 across the whole original
+// context and then steps once per multiple of it. Dropping it would ramp
+// smoothly from position 0 and diverge across the entire trained range.
+template <>
+struct rope_query_scale<rope_query_scaling::llama4> {
+  static constexpr rope_query_scaling strategy = rope_query_scaling::llama4;
+  float beta;
+  float original_context_length;
+
+  explicit rope_query_scale(llama4_rope_query_scaling_params params) noexcept
+  : beta(params.beta)
+  , original_context_length(params.original_context_length) {}
+
+  TRON(nodiscard, inline, const)
+  float operator()(uint32_t pos) const noexcept {
+    return 1.0f + beta * std::log1p(std::floor(float(pos) / original_context_length));
+  }
+};

+#pragma once
+
+#include <cstddef>
+
+namespace tron {
+
+// The number of lanes in the aligned lane domain for a pass of n tokens.
+// n_workers counts main and its n_workers - 1 helpers. n_pool is the size of
+// the application pool, which must be the helpers plus the attention workers
+// (see Note [Attention workers are the last pool workers] in
+// h/tron/models/model.hpp).
+// - With no helpers there is one lane, and main runs it.
+// - With more than twice as many tokens as helpers, every pool worker is a
+//   lane: the helpers first, then the attention workers.
+// - Otherwise the helpers are the lanes.
+// See Note [Aligned lane domain] in ingest/src/TronCpp.hs.
+constexpr std::size_t aligned_lanes(
+    std::size_t n, std::size_t n_workers, std::size_t n_pool) noexcept {
+  if (n_workers == 1) {
+    return 1;
+  }
+  const std::size_t n_helpers = n_workers - 1;
+  return n <= 2 * n_helpers ? n_helpers : n_pool;
+}
+
+// Whether the attention workers join the aligned lane domain in a pass of n
+// tokens. They join when there are helpers and aligned_lanes gives more lanes
+// than helpers. Generated run() asserts at least one attention worker, so with
+// helpers this holds exactly when aligned_lanes returns n_pool.
+constexpr bool attention_lanes_join(
+    std::size_t n, std::size_t n_workers, std::size_t n_pool) noexcept {
+  return n_workers > 1 && aligned_lanes(n, n_workers, n_pool) != n_workers - 1;
+}
+

+  // Note [Expert placement without a load profile]
+  // ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+  // With load-aware placement on and no usable profile, a model plans its experts
+  // with uniform loads (Note [Expert placement planning]) if expert replicas are
+  // requested, or if it is tensor-parallel and every expert matmul weight its plugin
+  // visits is one tile. Otherwise experts keep the base placement. The uniform
+  // profile steers placement only: `--expert-routing load` needs a measured profile.
+  //
+  // With `replicas` 0, select_placement's base placement for a tensor-parallel model
+  // rotates tiles among the devices in visit order. Generated plugins visit each
+  // expert weight in its own loop over experts, so when the device count divides
+  // the expert count, rotation can put all of an expert's weights on one device.
+  // The plan puts tensor ID t of an expert t devices past the expert's planned
+  // device instead. Separate gate and up weights (Qwen3 MoE, ingested Mixtral),
+  // whose matmuls are independent, can then run in parallel; GPT-OSS's fused
+  // gate_up and its down then run on different devices.
+  //
+  // The plan gives all tiles of an expert weight the same devices, which would put

+#pragma once
+
+#include <cmath>
+#include <cstddef>
+#include <cstdint>

+#include "common/util.hpp"
+#include "tron/files/safetensors.hpp"
+#include "tron/kernels/expr.hpp"
+#include "tron/kernels/host_matvec.hpp"
+#include "tron/tensor/seq.hpp"
+#include "tron/tensor/tensor.hpp"
+#include "tron/tensor/view.hpp"

+namespace tron {

+// Note [Host MoE router matvec]
+// ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+// weight_matrix<M, K> holds an M x K MoE router projection for host kernels,
+// with M outputs and K inputs per token. It stores the weights in one of two
+// forms:
+//
+// - Packed BF16 (bf16_matmul_weights). Assigning a BF16 view packs it when
+//   every element satisfies bf16_dot_operand<K>, that is, is in the packed
+//   range of Note [BF16 matmul range].
+// - Exact FP32. Every other source takes this storage: a BF16 view with an
+//   element outside the packed range, or any source that is not a BF16 view.
+//   Weights synthesized by --synthesize-missing-tensors arrive as FP32 views
+//   and are stored this way. fp32_reason() says why a matrix has FP32 storage.
+//
+// A NaN weight fails an assertion at assignment.
+//
+// matvec computes one token: out[m] = sum_k w[m][k] * in[k]. A NaN activation
+// fails an assertion with either storage.
+// - With FP32 storage, matvec runs the FP32 fallback, one FP32 dot per output
+//   row. This is slower than packed storage.
+// - With packed storage, matvec calls matvec_packed, which picks its backend
+//   from the token's activations: row_dot on AVX-512 BF16 builds when the
+//   activation row is contiguous BF16 within the packed range, and the FP32
+//   fallback otherwise.
+// A token's result therefore depends only on the weights and its activations,
+// not on the worker that computes it.
+//
+// A plugin's generated finalize_weights() passes each of its host matrices
+// (weight_matrix objects) to an fp32_storage_log. add() logs every host matrix
+// with FP32 storage, and its reason, at trace level. report() then warns once
+// if any host matrix has FP32 storage, naming the first one and its reason.
+//
+// touch reads one 8-byte word from each 64-byte cache line of the storage.
+// This brings the weights into the calling core's cache before its first
+// matvec (see Note [MoE router warm-up] in ingest/src/TronCpp.hs).
+
+enum class weight_storage { empty, packed_bf16, fp32 };
+
+// See Note [Host MoE router matvec].
+template <size_t M, size_t K>
+class weight_matrix {
+  using fp32_matrix = tensor<M, K>;
+  using bf16_matrix = bf16_matmul_weights<M, K>;
+  std::variant<std::unique_ptr<fp32_matrix>, std::unique_ptr<bf16_matrix>> weights_;
+  std::string_view fp32_reason_;
+
+  template <typename B>
+  weight_matrix& assign_fp32(
+      expr<B, M, K> const& source, std::string_view reason) noexcept {
+    auto weights = std::make_unique<fp32_matrix>(source);
+    for (size_t row = 0; row < M; ++row)
+      for (size_t column = 0; column < K; ++column)
+        TRON_ASSERT(!std::isnan((*weights)[row][column]), "NaN in host weights");
+    weights_ = std::move(weights);
+    fp32_reason_ = reason;
+    return *this;
+  }
+
+  // A tensor converts to a view with as_view(). A slice is already a view.
+  template <typename Row>
+  static auto row_view(Row& row) noexcept {
+    if constexpr (requires { row.as_view(); })
+      return row.as_view();
+    else
+      return row;
+  }
+
+public:
+  template <typename T>
+  using view = safetensor_view<T, M, K>;
+
+  weight_matrix() noexcept = default;
+  weight_matrix(uninitialized_t) noexcept {}
+
+  template <typename B>
+  weight_matrix(expr<B, M, K> const& source) noexcept {
+    *this = source.self();
+  }
+
+  template <typename B>
+  weight_matrix& operator=(expr<B, M, K> const& source) noexcept {
+    return assign_fp32(source, "the source is not BF16");
+  }
+
+  template <bool aligned, bool dma, typename Stride>
+  weight_matrix& operator=(
+      const_view<bf16, aligned, dma, seq<M, K>, Stride> const& source) noexcept {
+    // See Note [BF16 matmul range].
+    bool pack = true;
+    for (size_t row = 0; row < M; ++row) {
+      for (size_t column = 0; column < K; ++column) {
+        TRON_ASSERT(!host_matvec_detail::bf16_is_nan(source[row][column]),
+            "NaN in host weights");
+        pack &= bf16_dot_operand<K>(source[row][column]);
+      }
+    }
+    if (!pack) return assign_fp32(source, "a BF16 weight is outside the packed range");
+
+    auto weights = std::make_unique<bf16_matrix>();
+    auto rows = weights->as_view();
+    for (size_t row = 0; row < M; ++row)
+      for (size_t column = 0; column < K; ++column)
+        rows[row][column] = source[row][column];
+    weights_ = std::move(weights);
+    fp32_reason_ = {};
+    return *this;
+  }
+
+  weight_storage storage() const noexcept {
+    if (auto const* rows = std::get_if<0>(&weights_))
+      return *rows ? weight_storage::fp32 : weight_storage::empty;
+    return std::get<1>(weights_) ? weight_storage::packed_bf16 : weight_storage::empty;
+  }
+
+  // The reason the storage is FP32, or empty for any other storage.
+  std::string_view fp32_reason() const noexcept {
+    return fp32_reason_;
+  }
+
+  // One token: out[m] = sum_k w[m][k] * in[k].
+  template <typename Out, typename In>
+  void matvec(Out&& out, In const& in) const noexcept {
+    auto result = row_view(out);
+    auto activation = row_view(in);
+    static_assert(std::is_same_v<typename decltype(result)::dim, seq<M>>);
+    static_assert(std::is_same_v<typename decltype(activation)::dim, seq<K>>);
+    if (auto const* rows = std::get_if<0>(&weights_)) {
+      TRON_ASSERT(*rows, "Host weights have not been loaded");
+      host_matvec_detail::fallback<M, K>(**rows, result, activation);
+      return;
+    }
+    auto const& packed = std::get<1>(weights_);
+    TRON_ASSERT(packed, "Host weights have not been loaded");
+    matvec_packed(*packed, result, activation);
+  }
+
+  // Reads one 8-byte word per 64-byte cache line of the storage.
+  // See Note [MoE router warm-up] in ingest/src/TronCpp.hs.
+  void touch() const noexcept {
+    const unsigned char* bytes = nullptr;
+    size_t size = 0;
+    if (auto const* rows = std::get_if<0>(&weights_)) {
+      TRON_ASSERT(*rows, "Host weights have not been loaded");
+      bytes = reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>((*rows)->data.data());
+      size = sizeof(tensor<K>) * M;
+    } else {
+      auto const& packed = std::get<1>(weights_);
+      TRON_ASSERT(packed, "Host weights have not been loaded");
+      bytes = reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(packed->data.data());
+      size = sizeof(packed->data);
+    }
+    uint64_t sum = 0;
+    for (size_t offset = 0; offset + 8 <= size; offset += 64)
+      sum += *reinterpret_cast<const volatile uint64_t*>(bytes + offset);
+    asm volatile("" : : "r"(sum));
+  }
+};
+
+// Warns once about loaded host matrices with FP32 storage.
+// See Note [Host MoE router matvec].
+class fp32_storage_log {
+  size_t loaded_ = 0;
+  size_t fp32_ = 0;
+  std::string first_;
+  std::string_view reason_;
+
+public:
+  template <size_t M, size_t K>
+  void add(std::string_view key, weight_matrix<M, K> const& weights) noexcept {
+    const auto storage = weights.storage();
+    if (storage == weight_storage::empty) return;
+    ++loaded_;
+    if (storage != weight_storage::fp32) return;
+    spdlog::trace("Host matrix {} has FP32 storage: {}", key, weights.fp32_reason());
+    if (fp32_++ > 0) return;
+    first_ = key;
+    reason_ = weights.fp32_reason();
+  }
+
+  void report() const noexcept {
+    if (fp32_ == 0) return;
+    spdlog::warn("{} of {} host matrices have exact FP32 storage, slower per token "
+                 "than packed BF16; first {}: {}",
+        fp32_, loaded_, first_, reason_);
+  }
+};
+
+}  // namespace tron

+// Use the pool when it has workers, otherwise perform the same iteration on
+// the calling thread. thread_pool::parallel_for deliberately enqueues no work
+// in a worker-less pool; initialization paths that must complete every item use
+// this wrapper rather than treating that no-op as completed work.
+template <typename Ix, typename Body>
+void parallel_for_or_serial(thread_pool& pool, Ix start, Ix end, Body&& f) {
+  if (pool.num_workers() == 0) {
+    for (Ix ix = start; ix < end; ++ix)
+      f(ix);
+    return;
+  }
+  pool.parallel_for(start, end, std::forward<Body>(f));
+}
