 [COVERAGE.md](COVERAGE.md) for Haskell coverage. Use
 [../.agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md](../.agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md)
 to select integration and hardware tests.
+
+## Haskell audit principles
+
+### Total field access
+
+A record selector is partial when some constructors lack its field. Do not
+hide this with `OPTIONS_GHC -Wno-partial-fields`. Extract constructor-specific
+fields into a single-constructor payload record. Use an `Mk` prefix for its
+constructor, as in `Fx.Graph.MkCallFunction` and `TypedFx.MkParameterTensorInfo`.
+Leave unused single fields positional; a field present in every constructor
+can have a total selector.
+When absence is meaningful, expose it with a total accessor returning `Maybe`.
+
+Add an accessor only when it has a caller or a justified public API role.
+`weeder` checks reachability from the roots in `weeder.toml`; adding unused
+helpers or expanding its roots merely to silence a failure defeats that check.
+
+### Semantic types
+
+Use named records and targeted `newtype`s where bare tuples, `Text`, or `Int`
+hide meaning or allow values to be interchanged. For example, `Fx.Graph.Keyword`
+makes a keyword-argument map's keys distinct from arbitrary expression text.
+Derive structural operations where appropriate. Derive `IsString` only when
+arbitrary literals respect the type's invariant; it must not bypass validation.
+Do not wrap an otherwise clear field or list element solely for uniformity.
+
+### Named record fields
+
+For types already declared as records, prefer named construction and patterns
+to positional use. `Con{}` ignores fields; `Con{field}` binds a field by name;
+`Con{field = descriptiveLocal}` gives it a local name. Reordering same-typed
+fields can silently change a positional use's meaning, while adding a field
+usually produces an arity or type error. Single-field non-record constructors
+remain positional.
+
+Use `NamedFieldPuns` for puns and `RecordWildCards` for `{..}`. Wildcards suit
+constructions whose one-use locals already have the field names; do not rename
+descriptive locals used elsewhere just to shorten a construction. Explicit
+field aliases preserve established local names and make the mapping clear.
+Check shadowing under the module's enabled extensions and package warning flags.
+
+### Structural instances
+
+Derive structural `Eq`, `Ord`, `Show`, `Functor`, `Foldable`, and `Traversable`
+instances. For intended component-wise `Semigroup` and `Monoid` operations on
+products, use base's `Generically` with `DerivingVia`; do not add
+`generic-deriving`. `TypedFx.Subst` combines its maps by left-biased union,
+which is distinct from substitution composition.
+
+Keep custom instances when their behavior is intentional, and document that
+behavior. Derivation relies on the component instances' laws and compatibility
+with related instances: a derived `Ord`, for example, may disagree with a
+custom `Eq` that ignores a field. It does not prove a domain-specific contract.
+
+### Instance laws and domain properties
+
+Test handwritten instances with the existing `quickcheck-classes-base` law
+batteries for standard classes and explicit properties for project classes
+such as `Semilattice`. Keep tests beside the behavior they cover. Use Sydtest
+`*Spec.hs` modules exporting `spec :: Spec`, and register them in Cabal as
+described above. Follow the test-local `lawsToSpec` and `group` adapters in
+[KnownSpec](test/KnownSpec.hs) as examples. The pinned higher-kinded batteries
+use production `Eq` and `Show` instances through quantified constraints.
+Keep `Arbitrary` and `Arbitrary1` instances test-local; narrowly suppress
+orphan warnings with `OPTIONS_GHC -Wno-orphans` when needed.
+
+Check superclass coherence such as `(<*>) == ap`, as well as associativity,
+identity, ordering, and project-specific behavior. Generic laws alone can miss
+observable data that a custom equality ignores; `KnownSpec` also tests error
+accumulation explicitly.
+
+`Show` and `IsString` have no universal mutual-inverse law. In this repository,
+`RawName "foo" 2` and `RawName "foo_2" 0` render alike but remain distinct.
+The tested contract is `show (fromString s :: RawName) == s`, together with
+Show/Pretty agreement for newline-free generated names and the collision
+case in `NameSpec`. Do not parse literal suffixes as uniqueness counters
+or restrict a generator to force the false inverse `fromString (show rn) == rn`.

 compatible permuted checkpoint. Run `python3 ingest/build-model.py --help` for

+`--moe-router` sets where a MoE plugin computes the router's gate, the linear
+layer that scores the experts for each token. `ingest.moe_router` sets the same
+policy in the model registry.
+
+- `fpga`, the default, runs the gate as a matrix multiplication on the FPGA.
+- `cpu` computes the gate on the host from BF16 weights. A gate matrix that
+  does not load as BF16, or that has an element outside the range of the BF16
+  dot product, is stored in exact FP32 instead. See
+  `Note [Host MoE router matvec]` in `h/tron/tensor/weight_matrix.hpp`. The
+  gate runs in one per-token kernel, the router kernel, with the preceding
+  RMSNorm and the top-k.
+
+Expert selection runs on the CPU under both policies. GPT-OSS 20B, GPT-OSS
+120B and Qwen3-30B-A3B are registered with `ingest.moe_router: cpu`.
+
+Under `cpu`, the router kernel and the per-token kernels around it on the
+residual stream share one stripe of tokens. Within a pass, the same worker runs
+a given token in each of these kernels. The stripe spans the helper workers. In
+a pass with more than twice as many tokens as helpers, the attention workers
+join it.
+
+Except under `--export-only`, `build-model.py` chooses the policy and checks it
+against the registry:
+
+- Without `--moe-router`, it uses the policy registered for the plugin, matched
+  by `--name` or `--slug`. An unregistered plugin gets `fpga`.
+- An explicit `--moe-router` that contradicts the registry is an error, unless
+  `--no-config` is given.
+- A `--name` and a `--slug` that belong to two different registered plugins
+  are an error. `build-model.py` skips this check only for an explicit
+  `--moe-router` with `--no-config`.
+
+To register both policies as separate plugins, give each its own `--name` and
+`--slug`. Both plugins can use the same exported trace. With `--no-config`,
+which registers nothing, distinct `--name` values alone keep one plugin header
+from overwriting the other.
+
 For local registration, create the configuration file before running the
 orchestrator:

+class Registration(NamedTuple):
+  """A plugin's registry entry, as registered_plugin finds it.
+
+  source names the file that holds the entry. For a canonical entry that the
+  local config overrides, it names both files. moe_router is the entry's
+  ingest.moe_router, 'fpga' if absent. slug_registered says whether the
+  requested slug is one of the entry's variants, as opposed to a match by name
+  alone.
+  """
+
+  source: str
+  moe_router: str
+  slug_registered: bool
+
+
+def registered_plugin(
+  config_path: Path, slug: str, model_name: str
+) -> Optional[Registration]:
+  """Return the registration of the plugin named model_name or with slug.
+
+  A config_path with a schema_version is a full registry. Otherwise the lookup
+  uses config/models.yaml, merged with config_path if it exists. Return None if
+  neither the name nor the slug is registered. Raise ValueError if they belong
+  to different plugins.
+  """
+  config_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "config"
+  canonical_path = config_dir / "models.yaml"
+  sys.path.insert(0, str(config_dir))
+  import model_definitions
+
+  config_exists = config_path.exists()
+  config = (yaml.safe_load(config_path.read_text()) or {}) if config_exists else {}
+  canonical_names = set()
+  if "schema_version" in config:
+    registry = model_definitions.load_registry(str(config_path))
+  else:
+    registry = model_definitions.load_registry(str(canonical_path))
+    canonical_names = {arch["name"] for arch in registry["models"]}
+    if config_exists:
+      registry = model_definitions.merge_local(registry, str(config_path))
+  overridden = set()
+  if isinstance(config, dict):
+    overridden = {entry.get("name") for entry in config.get("overrides") or []}
+
+  def source_of(arch: dict) -> str:
+    if arch["name"] not in canonical_names:
+      return str(config_path)
+    if arch["name"] in overridden:
+      return f"{canonical_path} (overridden in {config_path})"
+    return str(canonical_path)
+
+  by_name = next(
+    (arch for arch in registry["models"] if arch.get("name") == model_name), None
+  )
+  by_slug = next(
+    (
+      arch
+      for arch in registry["models"]
+      if any(v.get("slug") == slug for v in arch.get("variants", []) or [])
+    ),
+    None,
+  )
+  if by_name is not None and by_slug is not None and by_name is not by_slug:
+    raise ValueError(
+      f"{model_name} and {slug} are registered to different plugins: "
+      f"{model_name} in {source_of(by_name)}, {slug} under {by_slug['name']} "
+      f"in {source_of(by_slug)}. Pass the name and slug of one plugin, or a new "
+      "name and slug to register another."
+    )
+  arch = by_name if by_name is not None else by_slug
+  if arch is None:
+    return None
+  return Registration(
+    source=source_of(arch),
+    moe_router=model_definitions.ingest_moe_router(
+      arch.get("ingest", {}), arch["name"]
+    ),
+    slug_registered=by_slug is not None,
+  )
+
+
+def config_has_plugin(
+  config_path: Path, slug: str, model_name: str, moe_router: str
+) -> Optional[Registration]:
+  """Return the plugin's registration, or None if it is unregistered.
+
+  Raise ValueError if the name and slug belong to different plugins, as
+  registered_plugin does, or if the registered ingest.moe_router is not
+  moe_router.
+  """
+  registered = registered_plugin(config_path, slug, model_name)
+  if registered is None:
+    return None
+  if registered.moe_router != moe_router:
+    raise ValueError(
+      f"{model_name} is registered with "
+      f"ingest.moe_router={registered.moe_router!r} in {registered.source}, "
+      f"but --moe-router is {moe_router!r}. "
+      "Omit --moe-router to use the registered policy, update that entry, "
+      "or use distinct --name and --slug values to register another plugin."
+    )
+  return registered
+

+moeMatVecExample :: Module
+moeMatVecExample =

+-- | A two-layer MoE model with attention and host router kernels, shaped
+-- like GPT-OSS. An embedding kernel comes first. Each layer then runs the
+-- QKV matmuls, an attention-input kernel, attention and the o_proj matmul.
+-- The router kernel follows, which fuses the residual add, the router and
+-- the top-k. Then come the expert matmuls with their expert-row kernels, a
+-- blend, and the kernel that adds the blend to the residual. See
+-- Note [Aligned lane domain membership] in LoopyTron/LaneDomain.hs.
+laneDomainExample :: Module
+laneDomainExample =
+  Module
+    { moduleEnv =
+        [ config "dim" "hidden_size" 16
+        , config "n_layers" "num_hidden_layers" 2
+        , config "n_heads" "num_attention_heads" 2
+        , config "n_kv_heads" "num_key_value_heads" 1
+        , config "head_size" "head_dim" 8
+        , config "vocab_size" "vocab_size" 32
+        ]
+          ++ concatMap layerEnv [0, 1]
+          ++ [intermediate "out" QBatchItems 16]
+    , moduleLiteralCpps = []
+    , moduleFunction =
+        Function
+          [(array "input" QBatchItems 16, "input")]
+          ( kernel
+              "embed"
+              QBatchItems
+              [ Unary Copy (at "input") (at "resid_0")
+              , Unary Copy (at "resid_0") (at "qkv_in_0")
+              ]
+              : concatMap layer [0, 1]
+          )
+          "out"
+    , moduleInputTokenRemappings = []
+    , moduleLogitsMunge = Nothing
+    }
+ where
+  config name field value =
+    Config
+      (Variable{name = name, type_ = IntType, semantics = Nothing})
+      [field]
+      (Just (IntLit value))
+      emptyProvenance
+  array name iterSpace width =

+      , type_ = Array RealScalar (Just iterSpace) (Static width)
+      , semantics = Nothing
+      }
+  intermediate name iterSpace width =

+  load name shape loadOp =

+      ( Variable

+          , semantics = Nothing

+      loadOp
+      False
+      emptyProvenance
+  at name = KernelIndexExpr (fromString name) "ix"
+  kernel name iterSpace body =
+    ParKernel
+      name
+      (Variable{name = "ix", type_ = LoopIxType iterSpace, semantics = Nothing})
+      body
+      emptyProvenance
+  named :: String -> Integer -> String
+  named base l = base ++ "_" ++ show l
+  key l what = "model.layers." ++ show l ++ "." ++ what
+  pairs l = QBatchItemsExpertPairs (fromString $ named "routing" l) 2
+  layerEnv l =

+    , load (named "wk" l) [8, 16] (LoadSafetensors $ key l "self_attn.k_proj.weight")
+    , load (named "wv" l) [8, 16] (LoadSafetensors $ key l "self_attn.v_proj.weight")

+    , load (named "gate_w" l) [8, 16] (LoadSafetensors $ key l "mlp.gate.weight")

     actualWidth /= expectedWidth

+-- | Require a static rank-2 weight @[M, K]@, an input row of width @K@ and an
+-- output row of width @M@. See Note [Kernel matrix-vector products] in Ops.hs.
+checkMatVecWidths :: L.KernelExpr -> L.KernelExpr -> L.KernelExpr -> CheckM ()
+checkMatVecWidths weight input output = recover $ do
+  (weightTy, inputTy, outputTy) <-
+    independently3
+      (inferExprType weight)
+      (inferExprType input)
+      (inferExprType output)
+  case weightTy of
+    TopET (L.Weight (Shape [Static rows, Static cols])) -> lift $ do
+      expectWidth "matvec input row (weight columns)" cols inputTy
+      expectWidth "matvec output row (weight rows)" rows outputTy
+    TopET (L.Weight _) ->
+      lift $ emit $ ExprTypeMismatch "matvec weight (static rank 2)" weightTy
+    -- 'expectWeightVal' reports a non-weight operand.
+    _ -> pure ()
+ where
+  expectWidth what width ty = case ty of
+    RowET _ (Static actual) | actual == width -> pure ()
+    _ -> emit $ ExprTypeMismatch (what ++ " (width " ++ show width ++ ")") ty
+

 -- shifted RMSNorm requires a rank-1 weight.

+-- Note [Prepares around the MoE router]
+-- ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+-- Under 'HostRouterPrepares', buffer reuse moves channel prepares away from
+-- two places in a MoE layer where a prepare stalls the main thread.
+-- Everywhere else it places prepares as 'MidpointPrepares' does.
+--
+-- A reused slot holds variables with disjoint lifetimes, one after another.
+-- If the slot has a channel, the main thread runs a channel prepare before
+-- the next occupant is written. The prepare waits until the previous
+-- occupant has been read. 'schedulePrepareTime' puts it midway between the
+-- previous occupant's last read and the next occupant's first write,
+-- counting Loopy statements. Two places are bad for it:
+--
+--   - The router window. It starts after an 'L.MoeRoute' and ends at the
+--     first 'L.MoeMatmul' that reads its routing. The expert launch waits
+--     for the routing, so a prepare inside the window delays the launch.
+--     Just before the MoeRoute, the main thread already waits for the
+--     MoeRoute's inputs. So when 'schedulePrepareTime' puts a buffer prepare
+--     inside the window, and the previous occupant's last read comes before
+--     the MoeRoute, 'hoistOutOfMoeRouterWindows' moves the prepare to just
+--     before the MoeRoute. The condition on the last read keeps the prepare
+--     after that read.
+--
+--   - Before the next layer's attention job. The last readers of a routing
+--     are the moe_blends on every worker, so a prepare of a reused routing
+--     slot there waits for the slowest worker's blend. Instead,
+--     'prepareAtMoeRouter' prepares a routing slot just before its next
+--     write, if that write is an 'L.MoeRoute' with a window. That MoeRoute
+--     runs only after every worker has left the blend and written the top-k
+--     indices that the MoeRoute reads.
+--
+-- LoopyTron selects 'HostRouterPrepares' if any kernel has an 'Ops.MatVec'
+-- ('LoopyTron.preparePlacement'). TypedFxBulk emits MatVec only for a host
+-- router (Note [MoE router placement policy] in TypedFxBulk.hs). A MatVec
+-- kernel in hand-written JSON Loopy also selects it.
+--
+-- Device-router and dense functions keep 'MidpointPrepares'. Device-router
+-- functions also get prepares in these two places. For example, a GPT-OSS
+-- plugin built with @--moe-router fpga@ has one in every router window but
+-- the last. They keep 'MidpointPrepares' because the rules have been
+-- measured only with host routers. 'MidpointPrepares' records no router
+-- windows, so both rules reduce to 'schedulePrepareTime'.
+
+-- | The window of each 'L.MoeRoute'. A MoeRoute whose routing no
+-- 'L.MoeMatmul' reads has no window.
+-- See Note [Prepares around the MoE router].
+moeRouterWindows :: [L.Statement] -> [MoeRouterWindow]
+moeRouterWindows stmts =
+  [ (r, m)
+  | (r, L.MoeRoute routing _ _) : later <- tails (zip [LA.Time 0 ..] stmts)

+prepareAtMoeRouter windows lastRead firstWrite
+  | firstWrite `elem` map fst windows = firstWrite
+  | otherwise = schedulePrepareTime lastRead firstWrite

+{-# LANGUAGE LambdaCase #-}
+
+-- | Membership of the aligned lane domain. See Note [Aligned lane domain] in
+-- TronCpp.hs for how the domain runs.
+module LoopyTron.LaneDomain
+  ( LaneDomain
+  , alignedLaneDomain
+  , inLaneDomain
+  , noLaneDomain
+  )
+where
+
+import Data.Map.Strict qualified as M
+import Data.Maybe (mapMaybe)
+import Data.Set qualified as S
+
+import Loopy qualified as L
+import Loopy.KernelAccess qualified as KernelAccess
+import LoopyTron.LivenessAnalysis qualified as LA
+import Name
+import Ops qualified
+import Size (IterationSpaceF (QBatchItems))
+
+-- Note [Aligned lane domain membership]
+-- ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+-- The aligned lane domain contains each host MoE router kernel and every
+-- token-striped host statement linked to one through CPU-written per-token
+-- rows. Its statements share one stripe. So within a pass, when one of them
+-- writes a row and another reads it, the lane that owns the row's token runs
+-- both accesses. This Note says which statements belong to the domain.
+-- Note [Aligned lane domain] in TronCpp.hs describes its lanes and the code
+-- that TronCpp generates for it.
+--
+-- 'alignedLaneDomain' finds the domain in a graph:
+--
+--   - The nodes, called candidates, are the QBatchItems ParKernels and the
+--     MoeBlends.
+--   - An edge links two candidates when one reads an array ('L.Array') that
+--     the other writes. Only candidates link, so a row written by a matmul,
+--     an attention operation or an expert-pair kernel links nothing.
+--   - The domain is the union of the connected components that contain a
+--     kernel with a MatVec, which is a host MoE router kernel.
+--
+-- The domain is empty when the function has no attention, since then no
+-- attention worker could join it. TronCheck rejects aligned-lane statements
+-- in a module without attention (invariant I6 of Note [Aligned lane domain]
+-- in TronCpp.hs).
+--
+-- For GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-30B-A3B the domain contains the embedding rmsnorm
+-- and, per layer, the router kernel (residual add, rmsnorm, router, top-k and
+-- softmax, fused), the moe_blend and the next residual+rmsnorm. After the
+-- last layer, that residual+rmsnorm is the final norm. Attention-input
+-- kernels read only matmul outputs, and expert-row kernels iterate over
+-- expert pairs, so both keep the helper stripe.
+--
+-- LoopyTron computes the domain before liveness analysis. Liveness gives the
+-- domain's statements LaneP producers and LaneC consumers, and these decide
+-- which variables need channels and which buffers can be reused.
+
+-- | Statement times of the aligned lane domain.
+newtype LaneDomain = LaneDomain (S.Set LA.Time)
+  deriving (Eq, Show)
+
+-- | The empty domain: every host kernel and blend keeps the helper stripe.
+noLaneDomain :: LaneDomain
+noLaneDomain = LaneDomain S.empty
+
+inLaneDomain :: LaneDomain -> LA.Time -> Bool
+inLaneDomain (LaneDomain times) t = t `S.member` times
+
+-- | See Note [Aligned lane domain membership].
+alignedLaneDomain :: LA.KernelAccessSummaries -> L.Module -> LaneDomain
+alignedLaneDomain summaries mod_
+  | not (any isAttention (map snd stmts)) = noLaneDomain
+  | otherwise = LaneDomain $ reach S.empty (S.toList seeds)
+ where
+  stmts = zip [LA.Time 0 ..] $ L.functionStmts $ L.moduleFunction mod_
+  variableTypes = KernelAccess.moduleVariableTypes mod_
+
+  isAttention = \case
+    L.Attention{} -> True
+    _ -> False
+
+  rows = S.filter $ \name -> case M.lookup name variableTypes of
+    Just L.Array{} -> True
+    _ -> False
+
+  -- (rows read, rows written) of each candidate.
+  nodes :: M.Map LA.Time (S.Set (Name Loopy), S.Set (Name Loopy))
+  nodes = M.fromList $ mapMaybe node stmts
+  node (t, L.ParKernel name var _ _)
+    | L.variableIterSpace var == QBatchItems =
+        let access = LA.lookupKernelAccessSummary name t summaries
+         in Just
+              ( t
+              ,
+                ( rows $ KernelAccess.kernelAllReadNames access
+                , rows $ KernelAccess.kernelAllWriteNames access
+                )
+              )
+  node (t, L.MoeBlend output _ weights input _ _) =
+    Just (t, (rows $ S.fromList [weights, input], rows $ S.singleton output))
+  node _ = Nothing
+
+  seeds =
+    S.fromList
+      [ t
+      | (t, L.ParKernel _ var body _) <- stmts
+      , L.variableIterSpace var == QBatchItems
+      , any isMatVec $ flatten body
+      ]
+  isMatVec = \case
+    L.Binary Ops.MatVec _ _ _ -> True
+    _ -> False
+  flatten = concatMap $ \case
+    L.For _ body -> flatten body
+    stmt -> [stmt]
+
+  writersOf =
+    M.fromListWith
+      (<>)
+      [(v, S.singleton t) | (t, (_, ws)) <- M.toList nodes, v <- S.toList ws]
+  readersOf =
+    M.fromListWith
+      (<>)
+      [(v, S.singleton t) | (t, (rs, _)) <- M.toList nodes, v <- S.toList rs]
+  look table v = M.findWithDefault S.empty v table
+  neighbours t = case M.lookup t nodes of
+    Just (rs, ws) ->
+      S.delete t $
+        S.unions $
+          map (look writersOf) (S.toList rs) ++ map (look readersOf) (S.toList ws)
+    Nothing -> S.empty
+
+  reach seen [] = seen
+  reach seen (t : rest)
+    | t `S.member` seen = reach seen rest
+    | otherwise = reach (S.insert t seen) (S.toList (neighbours t) ++ rest)

+-- Note [Kernel matrix-vector products]
+-- ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+-- @Binary MatVec w x@ is a matrix-vector product that runs inside a host
+-- kernel, one input row at a time. For a weight @w :: [M, K]@ and an input
+-- row @x :: [K]@, it writes the output row @y :: [M]@ with
+-- @y[m] = sum_k w[m][k] * x[k]@. By contrast, 'Bulk.Matmul' is a device
+-- matmul.
+--
+-- The op spec of MatVec is @"rc,...c->...r"@ (see 'BulkLoopy.binarySpec').
+-- The weight's axes @r@ and @c@ are its @M@ rows and @K@ columns. The weight
+-- has no @...@ axes, so the loop nest over the input's @...@ axes never
+-- indexes it, and the kernel receives the whole weight. The embedding table
+-- of 'Index' is passed the same way. Inside the Loopy kernel the weight is a
+-- plain variable reference ('Loopy.KernelVarExpr'), not an indexed read.
+--
+-- LoopyTron promotes the weight to the 'Tron.HostMatrix' memory space (see
+-- Note [HostMatrix weights] in Tron.hs). TronCpp emits it as
+-- @weight_matrix<M, K>@. That runtime class stores the weight as packed BF16
+-- or as exact FP32, chosen when the weight loads. For a packed weight, it
+-- chooses BF16 or FP32 arithmetic separately for each token (see
+-- Note [Host MoE router matvec] in h/tron/tensor/weight_matrix.hpp).
+--
+-- TypedFxBulk produces a MatVec only for an MoE router gate under
+-- @--moe-router cpu@ (see Note [MoE router placement policy] in
+-- TypedFxBulk.hs). JSON-Loopy input skips TypedFxBulk, so it contains a
+-- MatVec only where the JSON names the op @"matvec"@.

+-- Note [MoE gate recognition]
+-- ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+-- Equality saturation relabels each mixture-of-experts (MoE) router gate that
+-- it recognizes, from 'RFx.Linear' to 'RFx.MoeGateLinear'. The gate is the
+-- Linear that computes the router logits. The top-k indices of those logits,
+-- or of their softmax, feed the 'RFx.MoeRouter'. 'MoeGateLinear' has exactly
+-- the semantics of 'Linear', so the relabeling is always sound. Equality
+-- saturation only marks the gate. TypedFxBulk decides where the gate runs, on
+-- the FPGA or on the host (see Note [MoE router placement policy] in
+-- TypedFxBulk.hs).
+--
+-- A hegg pattern matches an expression and its operands, never its
+-- consumers. A rule rooted at a Linear therefore cannot tell whether the
+-- Linear feeds a router. Instead, a pre-scan of the input model, 'moeGates',
+-- runs before saturation. From each 'RFx.MoeRouter' it follows the router's
+-- indices back to the gate:
+--
+--   1. The indices are @getattr(t, 1)@, where @t@ is a top-level binding
+--      @t := topk(s, dim=last)@.
+--   2. The scores @s@ are the gate output @g@ or @softmax(g, dim=last)@.
+--   3. The gate output @g@ is @linear(x, w, b)@ or
+--      @matmul(x, transpose(w, 0, 1))@. Here @x@ is the input, @b@ is an
+--      optional bias, and @w@, the gate weight, is a parameter tensor.
+--
+-- At each step the pre-scan replaces a variable that names a top-level
+-- binding with that binding's expression. Such a variable has a one-element
+-- path (see Note [Variable paths in RewriteFx] in RewriteFx.hs).
+--
+-- For each recognized gate weight @w@, 'moeGateRewrites' emits the rule
+-- @linear(?x, w, ?b) := moe_gate_linear(?x, w, ?b)@ in two copies, one with
+-- the bias @?b@ and one without. The rule is rooted at the Linear, so the new
+-- node joins the Linear's own e-class, and nothing is inlined or duplicated.
+-- The rule relabels every Linear whose weight is @w@. It matches the
+-- matmul form after 'matmulTransposeToLinear' rewrites that form to a Linear.
+-- Extraction keeps the marker because 'MoeGateLinear' costs less than
+-- 'Linear'.
+--
+-- The pre-scan does not recognize every gate, and an unrecognized gate stays
+-- a 'Linear'. Examples are a sigmoid gate, a group-limited gate, and a gate
+-- whose top-k is not a top-level binding of its own. Under
+-- @--moe-router fpga@ that is harmless, because TypedFxBulk lowers a
+-- 'MoeGateLinear' exactly like a 'Linear'. Under @--moe-router cpu@,
+-- TypedFxBulk rejects the model. JSON-Loopy input skips equality saturation,
+-- so gate recognition never runs on it.
+
+-- | A recognized MoE router gate. See Note [MoE gate recognition].
+data MoeGate = MoeGate
+  { moeGateOwner :: Name.Name Name.RewriteFx
+  -- ^ Binding that holds the MoeRouter.
+  , moeGateWeight :: Name.Name Name.RewriteFx
+  -- ^ Parameter tensor that holds the gate weight.
+  , moeGateWeightType :: RFx.Type
+  -- ^ Type of the variable that references the gate weight.
+  }
+  deriving (Eq, Show)
+
+-- | One entry per MoeRouter, in binder-name order. The entry is 'Right' the
+-- router's gate, or 'Left' the binding that holds the router when the
+-- pre-scan does not recognize the gate. See Note [MoE gate recognition].
+moeGates :: RFx.Model -> [Either (Name.Name Name.RewriteFx) MoeGate]
+moeGates model =
+  [ maybe (Left owner) Right (gateOf owner indices)
+  | (owner, (_, expr)) <- M.assocs binds
+  , indices <- routerIndices expr
+  ]
+ where
+  binds = RFx.modelBinds model
+  routerIndices (RFx.Expr e) =
+    [indices | RFx.MoeRouter _ indices _ _ _ <- [e]] ++ foldMap routerIndices e
+  resolve expr = case expr of
+    RFx.Expr (RFx.Var _ [name])
+      | Just (_, rhs) <- M.lookup name binds -> resolve rhs
+    _ -> expr
+  lastAxis rank dim = dim == -1 || dim == toInteger rank - 1
+  gateOf owner indices = case resolve indices of
+    RFx.Expr
+      ( RFx.GetAttr
+          _
+          (RFx.Expr (RFx.Var (RFx.TTuple (RFx.TGenTensor _ rank) _) [topk]))
+          1
+        )
+        | Just (_, RFx.Expr (RFx.TopK scores _ dim _ _)) <- M.lookup topk binds
+        , lastAxis rank dim ->
+            linearOf owner $ stripSoftmax rank $ resolve scores
+    _ -> Nothing
+  stripSoftmax rank expr = case expr of
+    RFx.Expr (RFx.Softmax scores dim) | lastAxis rank dim -> resolve scores
+    _ -> expr
+  linearOf owner expr = case expr of
+    RFx.Expr (RFx.Linear _ weight _) -> weightOf owner $ resolve weight
+    RFx.Expr (RFx.Matmul _ transposed)
+      | RFx.Expr (RFx.Transpose weight 0 1) <- resolve transposed ->
+          weightOf owner $ resolve weight
+    _ -> Nothing
+  weightOf owner expr = case expr of
+    RFx.Expr (RFx.Var ty [weight])
+      | Just (_, RFx.ParameterTensor{}) <- M.lookup weight (RFx.modelInputs model) ->
+          Just $ MoeGate owner weight ty
+    _ -> Nothing
+
+-- | The rules that relabel each Linear whose weight is a recognized gate weight
+-- as a 'RFx.MoeGateLinear'. See Note [MoE gate recognition].
+moeGateRewrites :: RFx.Model -> [Rewrite anl RFx.ExprF]
+moeGateRewrites model =
+  concat
+    [ [ pat (RFx.Linear "x" weight Nothing)
+          := pat (RFx.MoeGateLinear "x" weight Nothing)
+      , pat (RFx.Linear "x" weight (Just "b"))
+          := pat (RFx.MoeGateLinear "x" weight (Just "b"))
+      ]
+    | gate <- nubOrdOn moeGateWeight $ rights $ moeGates model
+    , let weight = pat $ RFx.Var (moeGateWeightType gate) [moeGateWeight gate]
+    ]
+

--- Note [SingleHostP Producer]
--- ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
--- ParP marks buffers written by all worker threads in striped fashion
--- (each worker handles its token subset). The channel reset uses
--- n_workers producers so every worker's writes are tracked.
---
--- SingleHostP marks buffers written by a single thread (the main thread).
--- The main use is non-parallelized MoE operations: they run only in run(),
--- not in run_main_help(), so a single thread writes all tokens. But
--- downstream consumers (e.g. the residual add) run in both run() and
--- run_main_help() across all workers.
---
--- Without a channel, helpers read the buffer before the main thread
--- finishes writing (e.g. after zero-init but before accumulation),
--- producing wrong results. SingleHostP forces channel creation with
--- reset(1, n_workers): one producer, all workers as consumers. The
--- main thread signals finish_writing(0) after the write completes,
--- and each worker's start_reading(worker_ix) blocks until then.
---
--- SingleHostP also prevents buffer reuse with ParP buffers in the
--- register allocator (BufferReuse.hs), since their channel
--- requirements differ.
+-- | The stripe of a host-kernel producer: its lanes and iteration space.
+parProducerStripe :: Producer k -> Maybe (KernelLanes, k)
+parProducerStripe (ParP is) = Just (HelperStripe, is)
+parProducerStripe (LaneP is) = Just (AlignedLanes, is)
+parProducerStripe _ = Nothing

+-- Note [HostMatrix weights]
+-- ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+-- A weight lives in the 'HostMatrix' memory space when its only use is as
+-- the weight operand @w@ of a kernel @Binary MatVec w x@ (see
+-- Note [Kernel matrix-vector products] in Ops.hs). Such a weight has shape
+-- @[M, K]@, where K is the width of the input row and M the width of the
+-- output row.
+--
+-- LoopyTron promotes a 'Host' weight to 'HostMatrix' when it translates a
+-- ParKernel that multiplies by it, just as it promotes a matmul weight to
+-- 'Device'. A MatVec weight that is also a matmul operand, or that is
+-- compensated, is an ingest error. The promotion also resets the placement
+-- kind to 'OrdinaryTensor'. LoopyTron gives a router weight the
+-- 'MoeRouterTensor' kind from its safetensors key, and the placer replicates
+-- a tensor of that kind on every device. A 'HostMatrix' weight is never
+-- placed on a device, so the kind does not apply.
+--
+-- LoopyTron records 'HostMatrix' as a memory space for the same reason it
+-- records 'Device': later stages read the decision from the declaration.
+-- TronCpp picks each weight's C++ owner type from its declaration alone,
+-- TronCheck checks the declaration (I1, I3, I4), and the Tron dump prints
+-- it.
+--
+-- The memory space selects the owner type, not the storage format. TronCpp
+-- emits a 'HostMatrix' tensor as @weight_matrix<M, K>@. When the weight
+-- loads, @weight_matrix@ stores it as packed BF16 or as exact FP32. FP32
+-- storage is slower per token, so the generated @finalize_weights()@ warns
+-- once if any 'HostMatrix' tensor has it. Note [Host MoE router matvec] in
+-- h/tron/tensor/weight_matrix.hpp says when each storage applies.
+--
+-- TronCheck enforces:
+--
+--   I1. A MatVec weight is an unpermuted 'HostMatrix' @LoadSafetensors@
+--       tensor with a static @[M, K]@ shape.
+--   I2. A MatVec runs in a QBatchItems kernel. Its input is a real-valued
+--       row of width @K@, and its output one of width @M@.
+--   I3. A 'HostMatrix' tensor has at least one MatVec use and no other use.
+--   I4. No 'Host' or 'HostMatrix' tensor is a matmul operand.
+--   I5. A 'Device' 'MoeRouterTensor' is never a kernel parameter.

+-- | Enforce invariants I1-I5 of Note [HostMatrix weights] in Tron.hs.
+checkHostMatrixTensors :: T.Decls -> [T.Statement] -> Either String ()
+checkHostMatrixTensors decls stmts = do
+  mapM_ checkMatVec matVecs
+  mapM_ checkHostMatrixUse tensors
+  mapM_ checkMatmulOperand matmulOperands
+  mapM_ checkKernelParam kernelParams
+ where
+  tensors = T.getTensors decls
+  tensorInfos = M.fromList tensors
+  kernels = T.getKernels decls
+  buffers = M.fromList $ T.getBuffers decls
+
+  -- (kernel, iteration space, weight, input, output) per MatVec.
+  matVecs =
+    [ (kernel, T.kernelIterSpace info, weight, input, output)
+    | (kernel, info) <- kernels
+    , T.Binary Ops.MatVec weight input output <- flattenKernelStmts (T.kernelBody info)
+    ]
+  matVecWeights = S.fromList [tensor | (_, _, T.KernelParam tensor, _, _) <- matVecs]
+
+  -- Tensors referenced as kernel parameters outside a MatVec weight operand.
+  kernelParams =
+    [ (kernel, tensor)
+    | (kernel, info) <- kernels
+    , stmt <- flattenKernelStmts (T.kernelBody info)
+    , tensor <- nonMatVecWeightParams stmt
+    ]
+
+  otherUses :: M.Map (Name ('Tron 'Tensor)) [String]
+  otherUses =
+    M.fromListWith
+      (++)
+      ( [(tensor, ["kernel " ++ show kernel]) | (kernel, tensor) <- kernelParams]
+          ++ [(tensor, ["matmul " ++ show tensor]) | (_, tensor) <- matmulOperands]
+          ++ [ (T.evTensorName info, ["expert view " ++ show view])
+             | (view, info) <- T.getExpertViews decls
+             ]
+          ++ [ (T.moeScheduleSource info, ["MoE schedule " ++ show schedule])
+             | (schedule, info) <- T.getMoeSchedules decls
+             ]
+          ++ [ (sink, ["attention sink"])
+             | T.AttentionStmt operation <- stmts
+             , Just sink <- [T.attentionSinks (T.attentionConfig operation)]
+             ]
+      )
+
+  matmulOperands =
+    [(i, tensor) | (i, stmt) <- zip [0 :: Int ..] stmts, tensor <- matmulTensors stmt]
+  matmulTensors = \case
+    T.MatmulFillStmt tensor _ _ _ _ -> [tensor]
+    T.MatmulPrepareStmt tensor _ _ -> [tensor]
+    T.MoeMatmulPrepareAndLaunchStmt operation -> [T.moeMatmulTensor operation]
+    _ -> []
+
+  memorySpaceOf tensor = T.memorySpace <$> M.lookup tensor tensorInfos
+
+  -- I1 and I2.
+  checkMatVec (kernel, iterSpace, weight, input, output) = do
+    let context = "MatVec in kernel " ++ show kernel
+    tensor <- case weight of
+      T.KernelParam tensor -> Right tensor
+      _ -> Left $ context ++ " multiplies by a non-tensor " ++ show weight
+    info <-
+      maybe (Left $ context ++ " uses undeclared tensor " ++ show tensor) Right $
+        M.lookup tensor tensorInfos
+    (rows, cols) <- case (T.memorySpace info, T.loadOp info, T.shape info) of
+      ( T.HostMatrix
+        , LoadSafetensors _
+        , [Cpp.LiteralExpr (Cpp.IntLit m), Cpp.LiteralExpr (Cpp.IntLit k)]
+        )
+          | isNothing (T.tensorPermutation info) -> Right (m, k)
+      _ ->
+        Left $
+          context
+            ++ " weight "
+            ++ show tensor
+            ++ " is not an unpermuted static rank-2 HostMatrix safetensors tensor"
+    case iterSpace of
+      QBatchItems -> Right ()
+      _ -> Left $ context ++ " iterates over " ++ show iterSpace ++ ", not QBatchItems"
+    expectRealRow context "input" cols input
+    expectRealRow context "output" rows output
+
+  expectRealRow context role width expr = case realRowWidth expr of
+    Just actual
+      | actual == Cpp.LiteralExpr (Cpp.IntLit width) -> Right ()
+    _ ->
+      Left $
+        context
+          ++ " "
+          ++ role
+          ++ " "
+          ++ show expr
+          ++ " is not a real-valued row of width "
+          ++ show width
+
+  realRowWidth = \case
+    T.KernelIndexExpr (T.KernelBuffer buffer) _ -> do
+      info <- M.lookup buffer buffers
+      if T.bufferScalarType info == RealScalar
+        then Just $ T.bufferWidth info
+        else Nothing
+    T.KernelSliceExpr base _ len -> do
+      _ <- realRowWidth base
+      Just $ Cpp.LiteralExpr $ Cpp.IntLit len
+    _ -> Nothing
+
+  -- I3.
+  checkHostMatrixUse (tensor, info)
+    | T.memorySpace info /= T.HostMatrix = Right ()
+    | tensor `S.notMember` matVecWeights =
+        Left $ "HostMatrix tensor " ++ show tensor ++ " has no MatVec use"
+    | Just uses <- M.lookup tensor otherUses =
+        Left $
+          "HostMatrix tensor "
+            ++ show tensor
+            ++ " is used outside MatVec weights: "
+            ++ show uses
+    | otherwise = Right ()
+
+  -- I4.
+  checkMatmulOperand (i, tensor) = case memorySpaceOf tensor of
+    Just space
+      | space `elem` [T.Host, T.HostMatrix] ->
+          Left $
+            "matmul at statement "
+              ++ show i
+              ++ " uses "
+              ++ show space
+              ++ " tensor "
+              ++ show tensor
+    _ -> Right ()
+
+  -- I5.
+  checkKernelParam (kernel, tensor) = case M.lookup tensor tensorInfos of
+    Just
+      T.TensorInfo
+        { T.memorySpace = T.Device
+        , T.tensorPlacementKind = T.MoeRouterTensor
+        } ->
+        Left $
+          "kernel "
+            ++ show kernel
+            ++ " reads device MoE router tensor "
+            ++ show tensor
+    _ -> Right ()
+
+-- | Enforce the static invariants of Note [Aligned lane domain] in TronCpp.hs.
+-- A lane channel is one with a LaneP producer or an aligned-lane reader (a
+-- 'T.LaneConsumer' domain). Each such side is a lane side.
+--
+--   I6. An aligned-lane kernel or blend iterates over QBatchItems in a module
+--       with attention.
+--   L1. The kernels and blends that access a buffer without a guard channel
+--       all have one stripe, so each of the buffer's rows has one owner in a
+--       pass.
+--   L2. The side opposite a lane side is neither a helper-striped QBatchItems
+--       kernel nor an attention worker domain.
+--   L3. On each lane side, main's start and finish statements alternate,
+--       beginning with a start and ending with a finish. No attention
+--       operation falls between a start and its finish. So each attention
+--       window of Note [Aligned lane domain] finishes every phase it starts.
+checkLaneDomain :: T.Decls -> [T.Statement] -> Either String ()
+checkLaneDomain decls stmts = do
+  mapM_ checkIterationSpace alignedKernels
+  case (alignedKernels, alignedBlends, attentionIndices) of
+    ([], [], _) -> Right ()
+    (_, _, []) -> Left "aligned-lane host statements need an attention operation"
+    _ -> Right ()
+  mapM_ checkOwner $ M.toList bufferStripes
+  mapM_ checkLaneChannel channels
+  mapM_ checkWindows laneSides
+ where
+  kernels = T.getKernels decls
+  channels = T.getChannels decls
+  guarded =
+    M.fromList [(name, T.bufferGuardChannel info) | (name, info) <- T.getBuffers decls]
+  alignedKernels =
+    [(name, info) | (name, info) <- kernels, T.kernelLanes info == T.AlignedLanes]
+  alignedBlends = [i | (i, T.MoeBlendStmt _ _ _ _ _ T.AlignedLanes _) <- indexed]
+  indexed = zip [0 :: Int ..] stmts
+  attentionIndices = [i | (i, T.AttentionStmt _) <- indexed]
+
+  checkIterationSpace (name, info) = case T.kernelIterSpace info of
+    QBatchItems -> Right ()
+    space ->
+      Left $ "aligned-lane kernel " ++ show name ++ " iterates over " ++ show space
+
+  -- Stripes of the host statements that access each unguarded buffer.
+  bufferStripes :: Map (Name ('Tron 'Buffer)) (S.Set T.KernelLanes)
+  bufferStripes =
+    M.filterWithKey (\buffer _ -> M.lookup buffer guarded == Just Nothing) $
+      M.fromListWith (<>) $
+        [ (buffer, S.singleton $ T.kernelLanes info)
+        | (_, info) <- kernels
+        , buffer <- S.toList $ kernelBuffers info
+        ]
+          ++ [ (buffer, S.singleton lanes)
+             | T.MoeBlendStmt _ weights output input _ lanes _ <- stmts
+             , buffer <- [weights, output, input]
+             ]
+  checkOwner (buffer, stripes)
+    | S.size stripes <= 1 = Right ()
+    | otherwise =
+        Left $
+          "buffer "
+            ++ show buffer
+            ++ " has no guard channel but is accessed with stripes "
+            ++ show (S.toList stripes)
+
+  isLaneProducer = \case
+    T.LaneP _ -> True
+    _ -> False
+  hasLaneConsumer consumer =
+    not $ null [() | T.LaneConsumer _ <- NE.toList $ T.consumerDomains consumer]
+
+  checkLaneChannel (name, info) = do
+    let producer = T.channelProducer info
+        consumer = T.channelConsumer info
+        domains = NE.toList $ T.consumerDomains consumer
+        reject what =
+          Left $
+            "lane channel "
+              ++ show name
+              ++ " "
+              ++ what
+              ++ ": "
+              ++ show (producer, consumer)
+    when (isLaneProducer producer) $ do
+      when (T.ParConsumer QBatchItems `elem` domains) $
+        reject "feeds a helper-striped kernel"
+      unless (null [() | T.WorkerConsumer _ <- domains]) $
+        reject "feeds attention workers"
+    when (hasLaneConsumer consumer) $ case producer of
+      T.ParP QBatchItems -> reject "is fed by a helper-striped kernel"
+      T.WorkerP _ -> reject "is fed by attention workers"
+      _ -> Right ()
+
+  -- (channel, direction) pairs synchronized by lane participants.
+  laneSides =
+    [ (name, WriteDir)
+    | (name, info) <- channels
+    , isLaneProducer $ T.channelProducer info
+    ]
+      ++ [ (name, ReadDir)
+         | (name, info) <- channels
+         , hasLaneConsumer $ T.channelConsumer info
+         ]
+
+  checkWindows (channel, dir) = go Nothing indexed
+   where
+    side = case dir of
+      WriteDir -> "write"
+      ReadDir -> "read"
+    context i = "lane channel " ++ show channel ++ ", statement " ++ show i ++ ": "
+    go open [] = case open of
+      Just i -> Left $ context i ++ side ++ " phase is never finished"
+      Nothing -> Right ()
+    go open ((i, stmt) : rest) = case (stmt, open) of
+      (T.AttentionStmt _, Just j) ->
+        Left $
+          context j
+            ++ side
+            ++ " phase spans attention operation at statement "
+            ++ show i
+      _ -> case laneSync stmt of
+        Just True
+          | Just j <- open ->
+              Left $
+                context i
+                  ++ "second "
+                  ++ side
+                  ++ " start while statement "
+                  ++ show j
+                  ++ " is open"
+          | otherwise -> go (Just i) rest
+        Just False
+          | Just _ <- open -> go Nothing rest
+          | otherwise ->
+              Left $ context i ++ side ++ " finish without a start in its window"
+        Nothing -> go open rest
+    -- Just True for a start, Just False for a finish of this side.
+    laneSync = \case
+      T.ChannelStartWritingStmt c T.AllWorkers _
+        | c == channel, dir == WriteDir -> Just True
+      T.ChannelFinishWritingStmt c T.AllWorkers _
+        | c == channel, dir == WriteDir -> Just False
+      T.ChannelStartReadingStmt c T.AllWorkers _
+        | c == channel, dir == ReadDir -> Just True
+      T.ChannelFinishReadingStmt c T.AllWorkers _
+        | c == channel, dir == ReadDir -> Just False
+      _ -> Nothing
+
+-- | Buffers a kernel names in its body or access lists.
+kernelBuffers :: T.KernelInfo -> S.Set (Name ('Tron 'Buffer))
+kernelBuffers info =
+  S.fromList $
+    T.kernelEntryReadBuffers info
+      ++ T.kernelWriteBuffers info
+      ++ concatMap
+        (concatMap exprBuffers . stmtExprs)
+        (flattenKernelStmts $ T.kernelBody info)
+ where
+  stmtExprs = \case
+    T.Unary _ a b -> [a, b]
+    T.Binary _ a b c -> [a, b, c]
+    T.Ternary _ a b c d -> [a, b, c, d]
+    T.Reduce _ a b -> [a, b]
+    T.Nary _ args out -> args ++ [out]
+    T.TopK a b c d e f -> [a, b, c, d, e, f]
+    T.StridedCopy a b c d e -> [a, b, c, d, e]
+    T.BackPermute _ src dst -> [src, dst]
+    T.LogStmt obj _ _ _ _ -> [obj]
+    T.For _ _ body -> concatMap stmtExprs body
+    T.Comment _ -> []
+  exprBuffers = \case
+    T.KernelBuffer buffer -> [buffer]
+    T.KernelIndexExpr obj ix -> exprBuffers obj ++ exprBuffers ix
+    T.KernelSliceExpr base _ _ -> exprBuffers base
+    _ -> []
+
+-- | Kernel statements with nested loop bodies spliced in place.
+flattenKernelStmts :: [T.KernelStmt] -> [T.KernelStmt]
+flattenKernelStmts = concatMap $ \case
+  T.For _ _ body -> flattenKernelStmts body
+  stmt -> [stmt]
+
+-- | Tensors a kernel statement references, except a MatVec weight operand.
+nonMatVecWeightParams :: T.KernelStmt -> [Name ('Tron 'Tensor)]
+nonMatVecWeightParams = \case
+  T.Binary Ops.MatVec _ input output -> concatMap exprParams [input, output]
+  T.Unary _ a b -> concatMap exprParams [a, b]
+  T.Binary _ a b c -> concatMap exprParams [a, b, c]
+  T.Ternary _ a b c d -> concatMap exprParams [a, b, c, d]
+  T.Reduce _ a b -> concatMap exprParams [a, b]
+  T.Nary _ args out -> concatMap exprParams (args ++ [out])
+  T.TopK a b c d e f -> concatMap exprParams [a, b, c, d, e, f]
+  T.StridedCopy a b c d e -> concatMap exprParams [a, b, c, d, e]
+  T.BackPermute _ src dst -> concatMap exprParams [src, dst]
+  T.LogStmt obj _ _ _ _ -> exprParams obj
+  T.For _ _ body -> concatMap nonMatVecWeightParams body
+  T.Comment _ -> []
+ where
+  exprParams = \case
+    T.KernelParam tensor -> [tensor]
+    T.KernelIndexExpr obj ix -> exprParams obj ++ exprParams ix
+    T.KernelSliceExpr base _ _ -> exprParams base
+    _ -> []
+

+-- | Whether any tensor is in the 'HostMatrix' memory space.
+-- See Note [HostMatrix weights] in Tron.hs.
+hasHostMatrixTensors :: Module -> Bool
+hasHostMatrixTensors =
+  any ((== HostMatrix) . memorySpace . snd) . getTensors . modDecls
+
+-- | Whether any host statement runs on the aligned lane domain.
+-- See Note [Aligned lane domain].
+hasAlignedLanes :: Module -> Bool
+hasAlignedLanes Module{modDecls = env, mainKernel = run} =
+  any ((== AlignedLanes) . kernelLanes . snd) (getKernels env)
+    || not (null [() | MoeBlendStmt _ _ _ _ _ AlignedLanes _ <- run])

+-- | The @finalize_weights()@ method. It warns once if any 'HostMatrix' tensor
+-- has FP32 storage. Without a 'HostMatrix' tensor its body is empty.
+-- See Note [HostMatrix weights] in Tron.hs.
+finalizeWeightsDef :: Module -> StructComponent
+finalizeWeightsDef m
+  | null hostMatrices = LiteralDef "void finalize_weights() noexcept { }"
+  | otherwise =
+      MethodDef $

+            , Declare "fp32_storage_log" storageLog Nothing
+            ]

+              ++ [ExprStmt $ MethodCall (Var storageLog) "report" []]
+ where
+  hostMatrices =

+    ]

+-- | One step of an attention worker's window method.
+data LaneStep
+  = -- | Lane-side synchronization of a lane channel.
+    LaneSync Cpp.Statement
+  | -- | A guarded call that runs this worker's lane of an aligned-lane kernel
+    -- or blend.
+    LaneCall Cpp.Statement
+
+-- | The attention workers' steps for each attention window, in main's order.
+-- The windows split main's statements at each attention operation. Window
+-- @Just k@ holds the statements after attention operation @k@, and window
+-- 'Nothing' holds those before the first. A window's steps are the lane-side
+-- synchronizations of lane channels and the calls to aligned-lane kernels and
+-- blends among its statements. See Note [Aligned lane domain].
+laneWindows :: Decls -> [Tron.Statement] -> [(Maybe AttentionOpId, [LaneStep])]
+laneWindows env run = map (fmap (concatMap laneSteps)) $ attentionWindows run
+ where
+  blendNames = moeBlendNames run
+  part = Var "part"
+  laneSteps = \case
+    ChannelStartWritingStmt c Tron.AllWorkers _
+      | laneProducer c -> [LaneSync $ startWriting part c]
+    ChannelFinishWritingStmt c Tron.AllWorkers _
+      | laneProducer c -> [LaneSync $ finishWriting part c]
+    ChannelStartReadingStmt c Tron.AllWorkers _
+      | laneConsumer c ->
+          [LaneSync $ startReading (channelReadParticipant env c part) c]
+    ChannelFinishReadingStmt c Tron.AllWorkers _
+      | laneConsumer c ->
+          [LaneSync $ finishReading (channelReadParticipant env c part) c]
+    HostStmt kernel _
+      | ki <- readDecl kernel env
+      , kernelLanes ki == AlignedLanes ->
+          [laneCall (asCpp kernel) (not $ null $ kernelMatVecWeights $ kernelBody ki)]
+    MoeBlendStmt r w o i b AlignedLanes _ ->
+      [laneCall (blendNames M.! MoeBlendKey r w o i b AlignedLanes) False]
+    _ -> []
+  -- Attention workers pass touch = false to a router kernel's lane method.
+  -- They own tokens only in a pass with more than twice as many tokens as
+  -- helpers, and Note [MoE router warm-up] warms only in a pass with no more
+  -- tokens than helpers.
+  laneCall name router =
+    LaneCall $
+      IfStmt
+        (Var "active")
+        ( Block
+            [ ExprStmt $
+                FunCall (NamedFun $ laneMethodName name) $
+                  [Var "q_batch", Var "lane", Var "n_lanes"]
+                    ++ [LiteralExpr (BoolLit False) | router]
+            ]
+        )
+        Nothing
+  laneProducer c = case channelProducer (readDecl c env) of
+    LaneP _ -> True
+    _ -> False
+  laneConsumer c =
+    not $
+      null
+        [ ()
+        | LaneConsumer _ <-
+            NE.toList $ consumerDomains $ channelConsumer $ readDecl c env
+        ]

+-- | Main's statements split at each attention operation, keyed by the
+-- operation they follow.
+attentionWindows :: [Tron.Statement] -> [(Maybe AttentionOpId, [Tron.Statement])]
+attentionWindows = go Nothing []
+ where
+  go key acc [] = [(key, reverse acc)]
+  go key acc (AttentionStmt operation : rest) =
+    (key, reverse acc) : go (Just $ attentionOpId operation) [] rest
+  go key acc (stmt : rest) = go key (stmt : acc) rest
+
+laneWindowName :: Maybe AttentionOpId -> Name Cpp
+laneWindowName Nothing = "attention_prologue"
+laneWindowName (Just (AttentionOpId k)) = fromString $ "attention_window_" ++ show k

+-- | The method that attention worker @attn_ix@ runs for one attention window.
+-- The worker is lane @n_helpers + attn_ix@ of the aligned lane domain. On
+-- each lane channel it synchronizes, it is participant @n_workers + attn_ix@,
+-- offset by the matrix count on a mixed consumer. It takes part in every
+-- lane-channel phase in the window, whether or not its lane has a token.
+-- It calls the lane method of a kernel or blend only when @active@ holds: the
+-- pass has helpers, the pass's lanes include the attention workers, and this
+-- lane has a token.
+laneWindowMethod :: Name Cpp -> [LaneStep] -> Method
+laneWindowMethod name steps =
+  Method "void" name params [] $
+    Block $
+      [ LitStmt "const size_t n_helpers = app_pool().num_workers() - n_attn_workers;"
+      , LitStmt "const size_t n_workers = n_helpers + 1;"
+      ]
+        ++ [LitStmt "const size_t part = n_workers + attn_ix;" | not $ null syncs]
+        ++ ( if null calls
+               then []
+               else
+                 [ LitStmt "const size_t n = q_batch->items.size();"
+                 , LitStmt $
+                     "const size_t n_lanes = tron::aligned_lanes(n, n_workers, "
+                       ++ "app_pool().num_workers());"
+                 , LitStmt "const size_t lane = n_helpers + attn_ix;"
+                 , LitStmt $
+                     "const bool active = n_workers > 1 && lane < n_lanes && "
+                       ++ "lane < n;"
+                 ]
+           )
+        ++ map stepStatement steps
+ where
+  params =
+    [ Param "plugin_batch*" "q_batch"
+    , Param "size_t" "attn_ix"
+    , Param "size_t" "n_attn_workers"
+    ]
+  syncs = [() | LaneSync _ <- steps]
+  calls = [() | LaneCall _ <- steps]
+  stepStatement (LaneSync stmt) = stmt
+  stepStatement (LaneCall stmt) = stmt

+-- Note [Aligned lane domain]
+-- ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+-- The aligned lane domain is a set of token-striped host kernels and blends
+-- that share one stripe per pass. Its lanes are the helpers and, in passes
+-- with more than twice as many tokens as helpers, the attention workers too.
+-- This Note gives the lane rule, when the attention workers join the domain,
+-- and why every lane channel's participant count matches the threads that
+-- synchronize on it.
+--
+-- Membership. A host MoE router (Note [HostMatrix weights] in Tron.hs) runs
+-- in the router kernel. That kernel fuses the residual add and rmsnorm before
+-- the router with the top-k and softmax after it. The domain
+-- holds the router kernels and the token-striped kernels and blends linked to
+-- them through CPU-written per-token rows. Because they share one stripe, no
+-- such row changes owner within a pass. Note [Aligned lane domain membership]
+-- in LoopyTron/LaneDomain.hs gives the linking rule and the members for
+-- GPT-OSS and Qwen3.
+--
+-- Lane rule. A pass has n tokens. n_workers counts main and the H helpers, so
+-- H = n_workers - 1. A is the number of attention workers, and run() asserts
+-- A >= 1. tron::aligned_lanes gives the number of lanes L(n):
+--
+--   L(n) = 1       if H = 0 (main runs the one lane)
+--   L(n) = H       if H >= 1 and n <= 2H
+--   L(n) = H + A   if H >= 1 and n > 2H
+--
+-- Lane l owns tokens l, l + L(n), l + 2 L(n), ... When H >= 1, main is not a
+-- lane. The helper with worker_ix h (1 <= h <= H) is lane h - 1, and
+-- attention worker j (0 <= j < A) is lane H + j. With n <= 2H an attention
+-- worker would own at most one token, so attention workers join the domain
+-- only in larger passes.
+--
+-- Joining the domain. J is true in a pass whose lanes include the attention
+-- workers, that is, when H >= 1 and n > 2H. reset_channels computes J once
+-- per pass with tron::attention_lanes_join, from n = items.size(), n_workers
+-- and the pool size. reset_channels runs on main before main enqueues any
+-- worker. It stores A if J holds, and 0 otherwise, in
+-- plugin_batch::n_attention_lanes. Enqueuing a worker publishes the value
+-- to it. Attention workers only read it, and main writes it again only
+-- after workers_done.wait(). The helpers take their stripe from
+-- tron::aligned_lanes, and tron::attention_lanes_join calls
+-- tron::aligned_lanes with the same inputs, so J and the helpers' stripe
+-- cannot disagree.
+--
+-- Pool split. When the attention workers join the domain,
+-- tron::aligned_lanes returns the pool size as the lane count H + A. Each
+-- attention worker computes H as the pool size minus A. Both assume that the
+-- helpers and the attention workers together fill the application pool, as
+-- Note [Attention workers are the last pool workers] in model.hpp requires.
+-- reset_channels asserts this split every pass. The aligned program also
+-- asserts that its A equals the n_attention_lanes that reset_channels stored.
+--
+-- Lane channels. A lane channel is a channel with a LaneP producer or an
+-- aligned-lane reader, that is, a LaneConsumer domain in its consumer. Each
+-- such side is a lane side. A lane side has n_workers + n_attention_lanes
+-- participants: main, the H helpers and, when J holds, the A attention
+-- workers. Attention worker j is participant n_workers + j. On a mixed
+-- consumer the lane-side ids are offset by the matrix count
+-- (Note [Mixed parallel and matrix consumers] in Tron.hs). Every side that
+-- is not a lane side keeps its usual count. In GPT-OSS and Qwen3, lane
+-- channels carry five kinds of row. Lane sides read two: the o_proj output
+-- and the moe_blend input. They write three: the top-k indices, the next
+-- layer's QKV input, and the expert input. The expert input is the
+-- normalized row that the router kernel writes and the expert matmuls read.
+--
+-- Attention worker programs. Each pass, run_attention_worker runs one of two
+-- programs:
+--   - Without J, run_attention_worker_helpers_only. It runs the attention jobs
+--     and makes no call on a lane channel.
+--   - With J, run_attention_worker_aligned. It runs the same attention jobs,
+--     plus attention_prologue before the first job and attention_window_k
+--     after job k.
+-- Attention window k holds main's statements after attention operation k, up
+-- to the next attention operation or the end of the pass. The prologue is the
+-- attention window before the first attention operation. A window with no
+-- lane-side work gets no method and no call. A window method runs, in main's
+-- order, the lane side of each lane-channel synchronization in its window.
+-- When the worker's lane owns tokens, it also runs the lane method of each
+-- aligned-lane kernel and blend in the window.
+--
+-- Invariants. TronCheck enforces the static ones ('TronCheck.checkLaneDomain'):
+--   L1. The kernels and blends that access a buffer without a guard channel
+--       all have one stripe, so each of the buffer's rows has one owner in a
+--       pass.
+--   L2. The side opposite a lane side is never a helper-striped QBatchItems
+--       kernel or an attention worker domain.
+--   L3. No attention operation falls between the start and the finish of a
+--       lane-side phase, so each attention window finishes every phase it
+--       starts.
+--   I6. An aligned-lane kernel or blend iterates over QBatchItems, and the
+--       module has an attention operation.
+-- The generated code maintains the rest:
+--   - Aligned lanes need one minibatch. Every generated plugin asserts this
+--     (Note [Ingested Model Mini-batching]).
+--   - In every pass, the participants configured on a lane channel are
+--     exactly the ids that call it: 0 to H, plus n_workers + j for each
+--     attention worker j when J holds. A stray id aborts on the barrier's id
+--     assert. A missing call hangs.
+--   - J depends only on inputs that are constant within a pass. It holds
+--     exactly when there are helpers and their stripe has H + A lanes.
+--   - channel::reset re-sizes every barrier and latch each pass, so no
+--     participant state crosses a pass boundary when J changes.
+--
+-- Deadlock freedom follows from ordering and needs no separate check.
+-- Attention workers make their lane-side calls in main's order. So whenever
+-- main waits on an attention worker, main has already issued every prepare
+-- that the worker needed to reach that point.
+

+-- Note [MoE router warm-up]
+-- ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+-- In a small pass, a helper loads a router kernel's host weights into its
+-- cache before its first row arrives. A pass is small when it has no more
+-- tokens than helpers: n <= H, for n tokens and H helpers. The helper warms
+-- only if it owns a token. Before its first row wait, it calls
+-- 'weight_matrix::touch', which reads one 8-byte word from each 64-byte cache
+-- line.
+--
+-- In a small pass each helper runs at most one router matvec for the kernel.
+-- Without the warm-up, that matvec takes the weights' cache misses after the
+-- helper's o_proj row arrives, on the critical path. With it, the loads
+-- overlap the wait. A larger pass amortizes the misses over several rows, so
+-- its helpers skip the extra read.
+--
+-- On the aligned lane domain (Note [Aligned lane domain]), a helper passes
+-- the same condition to the kernel's lane method as its @touch@ flag. An
+-- attention worker passes false, because it owns tokens only when n > 2H.
+
+-- | The warm-up of Note [MoE router warm-up] for a helper-striped kernel whose
+-- body multiplies by host router weights. It is empty for any other kernel.
+moeRouterWarmUp :: [KernelStmt] -> [Cpp.Statement]
+moeRouterWarmUp body = case kernelMatVecWeights body of
+  [] -> []
+  weights ->
+    [ Cpp.Comment "See Note [MoE router warm-up] in ingest/src/TronCpp.hs."
+    , IfStmt
+        ( ExprLit $
+            "actual_worker_ix < q_batch->items.size() && "
+              ++ "q_batch->items.size() <= n_actual_workers"
+        )
+        (Block $ map touchWeights weights)
+        Nothing
+    ]
+
+-- | The warm-up of an aligned-lane router kernel, gated by its @touch@
+-- parameter. See Note [MoE router warm-up].
+laneWarmUp :: [Name ('Tron 'Tensor)] -> [Cpp.Statement]
+laneWarmUp [] = []
+laneWarmUp weights =
+  [ Cpp.Comment "See Note [MoE router warm-up] in ingest/src/TronCpp.hs."
+  , IfStmt (Var "touch") (Block $ map touchWeights weights) Nothing
+  ]
+
+touchWeights :: Name ('Tron 'Tensor) -> Cpp.Statement
+touchWeights w = ExprStmt $ MethodCall (FieldRef (Var "model") (asCpp w)) "touch" []
+
+-- | Host router weights a kernel body multiplies by.
+kernelMatVecWeights :: [KernelStmt] -> [Name ('Tron 'Tensor)]
+kernelMatVecWeights = concatMap $ \case
+  Binary Ops.MatVec (KernelParam w) _ _ -> [w]
+  For _ _ stmts -> kernelMatVecWeights stmts
+  _ -> []

+-- Note [MoE router placement policy]
+-- ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+-- The @--moe-router@ option selects where each MoE router gate runs, on the
+-- FPGA or on the host. It decides how TypedFxBulk lowers a
+-- 'TFx.MoeGateLinear', the node that marks a recognized gate (see
+-- Note [MoE gate recognition] in RewriteFxRewriteFx/EqSat.hs).
+--
+--   - 'MoeRouterFpga', the default, lowers the gate exactly like a
+--     'TFx.Linear': a device 'B.Matmul', plus a @B.Binary Ops.Add@ when the
+--     gate has a bias.
+--   - 'MoeRouterCpu' lowers the gate to a host @B.Binary Ops.MatVec@ (see
+--     Note [Kernel matrix-vector products] in Ops.hs), plus the same bias
+--     Add. BulkLoopy and kernel fusion then merge the preceding RMSNorm, the
+--     MatVec, the bias Add and the top-k into one per-token host kernel,
+--     called the router kernel.
+--
+-- Under 'MoeRouterCpu', 'requireRecognizedMoeGates' fails ingestion unless
+-- every MoeRouter's indices lead, through the top-k and an optional softmax,
+-- to a 'TFx.MoeGateLinear' whose weight has exactly one use. The error names
+-- the binding that holds the router. This one check catches both ways a gate
+-- can stay a plain 'TFx.Linear': the pre-scan 'moeGates' did not recognize its
+-- structure, or the relabel rule did not fire. Without the check, such a
+-- router would silently stay on the FPGA.
+
+-- | Fail unless every MoeRouter has a recognized gate whose weight has exactly
+-- one use. 'typedFxToBulk' runs this check under 'MoeRouterCpu'. See
+-- Note [MoE router placement policy].
+requireRecognizedMoeGates :: TFx.Model -> ()
+requireRecognizedMoeGates model =
+  foldr
+    seq
+    ()
+    [ checkGate owner indices
+    | (owner, TFx.SomeExpr _ expr) <- M.assocs binds
+    , indices <- moeRouterIndices expr
+    ]
+ where
+  binds = TFx.modelBinds model
+  checkGate owner indices = case gateWeight indices of
+    Nothing ->
+      error $
+        "TypedFxBulk: the MoE router gate in binding "
+          <> show owner
+          <> " is not recognized; ingest with --moe-router fpga or extend "
+          <> "Note [MoE gate recognition]"
+    Just weight
+      | uses <- weightUses weight
+      , uses /= 1 ->
+          error $
+            "TypedFxBulk: the MoE router gate weight "
+              <> show weight
+              <> " in binding "
+              <> show owner
+              <> " has "
+              <> show uses
+              <> " uses; expected 1"
+      | otherwise -> ()
+  weightUses weight =
+    length
+      [ ()
+      | TFx.SomeExpr _ expr <- M.elems binds
+      , name <- varNames expr
+      , name == weight
+      ]
+  -- Follow a chain of variables through top-level bindings to the expression
+  -- it names.
+  withResolved :: TFx.Expr a -> (forall b. TFx.Expr b -> r) -> r
+  withResolved (TFx.Var name) k
+    | Just (TFx.SomeExpr _ bound) <- M.lookup name binds = withResolved bound k
+  withResolved expr k = k expr
+  gateWeight :: TFx.Expr a -> Maybe (Name TypedFx)
+  gateWeight indices = withResolved indices $ \case
+    TFx.GetSnd (TFx.Var topk)
+      | Just (TFx.SomeExpr _ (TFx.TopK scores _ dim _ _)) <- M.lookup topk binds
+      , dim == maxBound ->
+          withResolved scores softmaxInput
+    _ -> Nothing
+  softmaxInput :: TFx.Expr a -> Maybe (Name TypedFx)
+  softmaxInput = \case
+    TFx.Softmax scores dim | dim == maxBound -> withResolved scores gateLinear
+    expr -> gateLinear expr
+  gateLinear :: TFx.Expr a -> Maybe (Name TypedFx)

 panic :: HasCallStack => Doc () -> a
 panic err = error $ show err
 
+-- | Unwrap a 'Maybe', failing loudly with context if it is 'Nothing'. Use
+-- instead of 'Data.Maybe.fromJust' so a broken precondition crashes with a
+-- message and call stack rather than the opaque "Maybe.fromJust: Nothing".
+expectJust :: HasCallStack => Doc () -> Maybe a -> a
+expectJust _ (Just x) = x
+expectJust msg Nothing = panic msg
+
+-- | Total-or-loud list indexing. Fails with context (and a call stack)
+-- instead of the opaque "Prelude.!!: index too large" when out of range.
+-- Use instead of @(!!)@ where an index is expected-valid by an invariant.
+expectIndex :: HasCallStack => Doc () -> Int -> [a] -> a
+expectIndex msg n xs =
+  expectJust (msg <+> parens ("index" <+> pretty n)) (safeIndex n xs)

+            (B.TopK "biased" 2 (-1) True True)
+            emptyProvenance

+  intVar name width =

+-- | BulkLoopy lowers the MatVec to a QBatchItems kernel with one row per
+-- iteration. Kernel fusion then merges it with the RMSNorm before it and the
+-- bias add and top-k after it.
+test_matvec_gate_fuses :: IO ()
+test_matvec_gate_fuses = do

+      fused = L.functionStmts (L.moduleFunction (LoopyLoopy.fuseKernels loopy))
+      gateWeights =
+        [ L.name var
+        | L.Load var (LoadSafetensors "model.gate.weight") _ _ <- L.moduleEnv loopy
+        ]
+      opName = \case
+        L.Unary op _ _ -> Just $ Ops.unOpName op
+        L.Binary op _ _ _ -> Just $ Ops.binOpName op
+        L.Ternary op _ _ _ _ -> Just $ Ops.ternOpName op
+        L.TopK{} -> Just "topk"
+        _ -> Nothing
+  case [(var, body) | L.ParKernel "matvec" var body _ <- stmts] of
+    [ ( var

+{-# LANGUAGE DerivingStrategies #-}
+{-# LANGUAGE StandaloneDeriving #-}
+{-# OPTIONS_GHC -Wno-orphans #-}
+
+-- | Typeclass-law spec for the hand-written 'Semigroup' / 'Monoid' instances
+-- on 'Cost'. 'Cost' is the extraction cost of an e-graph node: a finite
+-- cost adds both rewrite debt and size under '<>', and 'Infinite' is the
+-- absorbing element. 'mempty' is @Cost (FiniteCost 0 0)@. We pin the laws from
+-- "Test.QuickCheck.Classes.Base".
+--
+-- The 'Arbitrary' and 'Show' instances below are orphans kept in the test
+-- module (never shipped in the library) purely to feed the law batteries.
+module CostSpec (spec) where
+
+import Data.Proxy (Proxy (..))
+import Numeric.Natural (Natural)
+import Test.QuickCheck
+import Test.QuickCheck.Classes.Base
+  ( Laws (..)
+  , monoidLaws
+  , semigroupLaws
+  )
+import Test.Syd
+
+import RewriteFxRewriteFx.EqSat (Cost (..), FiniteCost (..))
+
+-- | 'Natural' has no 'Arbitrary' instance we can rely on across QuickCheck
+-- versions, so both fields are generated through a non-negative 'Integer'.
+genNatural :: Gen Natural
+genNatural = fromInteger . getNonNegative <$> arbitrary
+
+shrinkNatural :: Natural -> [Natural]
+shrinkNatural = map fromInteger . filter (>= 0) . shrink . toInteger
+
+instance Arbitrary FiniteCost where
+  arbitrary = FiniteCost <$> genNatural <*> genNatural
+  shrink (FiniteCost debt size) =
+    [FiniteCost debt' size | debt' <- shrinkNatural debt]
+      ++ [FiniteCost debt size' | size' <- shrinkNatural size]
+
+instance Arbitrary Cost where
+  arbitrary =
+    frequency
+      [ (3, Cost <$> arbitrary)
+      , (1, pure Infinite)
+      ]
+  shrink (Cost n) = Infinite : map Cost (shrink n)
+  shrink Infinite = []
+
+deriving stock instance Show FiniteCost
+
+deriving stock instance Show Cost
+
+-- | Run every law in a 'Laws' battery as an individual Sydtest property.
+lawsToSpec :: Laws -> Spec
+lawsToSpec laws =
+  group
+    (lawsTypeclass laws)
+    [it name p | (name, p) <- lawsProperties laws]
+
+spec :: Spec
+spec =
+  group
+    "Cost"
+    [ lawsToSpec (semigroupLaws (Proxy :: Proxy Cost))
+    , lawsToSpec (monoidLaws (Proxy :: Proxy Cost))
+    ]
+
+-- | Group a list of specs in one Sydtest 'describe' block.
+group :: String -> [Spec] -> Spec
+group name = describe name . sequence_

+{-# LANGUAGE AllowAmbiguousTypes #-}
+{-# LANGUAGE DataKinds #-}
+{-# LANGUAGE FlexibleContexts #-}
+{-# LANGUAGE PatternSynonyms #-}
+{-# LANGUAGE ScopedTypeVariables #-}
+{-# LANGUAGE TypeApplications #-}
+
+-- | Round-trip and kind-discrimination spec for the hand-written
+-- 'Declarable' instances in "Tron".
+--
+-- 'Declarable' backs @readDecl@/@modifyDecl@: each 'TronEntity' maps (via the
+-- injective 'InfoType' type family) to a record type, and @wrapInfo@ /
+-- @unwrapInfo@ move between that record and the 'EnvInfo' sum. These
+-- instances are written by hand, one per constructor, so the two laws that
+-- @readDecl@ relies on are not guaranteed by construction and are pinned
+-- here:
+--
+--   * round-trip: @unwrapInfo (wrapInfo info) == Just info@;
+--   * kind discrimination: a wrapper built for kind A, read at a different
+--     kind B, yields 'Nothing'.
+--
+-- Sample 'InfoType' values are constructed by hand (the 'InfoType' family
+-- fixes the record type per kind). These are fixed-input Sydtest cases — the inputs
+-- are fixed, so there is no 'Arbitrary' here.
+module DeclarableSpec (spec) where
+
+import Test.Syd
+
+import Cpp (Expr (LiteralExpr), Literal (IntLit))
+import LoadOp (LoadOp (LoadSafetensors))
+import Name
+  ( TronEntity (Buffer, Channel, Input, Permutation, Tensor)
+  )
+import Provenance (emptyProvenance)
+import ScalarType (ScalarType (RealScalar))
+import Size (IterationSpaceF (QBatchItems))
+import Tron
+  ( BufferInfo (..)

+-- | @unwrapInfo (wrapInfo info) == Just info@ for the given kind.
+roundTrip
+  :: forall k
+   . (Declarable k, Eq (InfoType k), Show (InfoType k))
+  => String
+  -> InfoType k
+  -> Spec
+roundTrip label info =
+  it (label ++ " round-trips through wrap/unwrap") $
+    unwrapInfo @k (wrapInfo @k info) `shouldBe` Just info
+
+-- | A wrapper built for kind @a@, read at the distinct kind @b@, is
+-- 'Nothing'. The wrapped value is supplied for @a@; @b@ only contributes
+-- its @unwrapInfo@.
+discriminates
+  :: forall a b
+   . (Declarable a, Declarable b, Eq (InfoType b), Show (InfoType b))
+  => String
+  -> InfoType a
+  -> Spec
+discriminates label info =
+  it (label ++ ": reading at the wrong kind yields Nothing") $
+    unwrapInfo @b (wrapInfo @a info) `shouldBe` Nothing
+
+spec :: Spec
+spec =
+  group
+    "Declarable"
+    [ group
+        "round-trip (unwrapInfo . wrapInfo == Just)"
+        [ roundTrip @Buffer "Buffer" sampleBuffer
+        , roundTrip @Channel "Channel" sampleChannel
+        , roundTrip @Tensor "Tensor" sampleTensor
+        , roundTrip @Input "Input" sampleInput
+        , roundTrip @Permutation "Permutation" samplePermutation
+        ]
+    , group
+        "kind discrimination (wrong-kind unwrap == Nothing)"
+        [ discriminates @Buffer @Channel "Buffer/Channel" sampleBuffer
+        , discriminates @Channel @Buffer "Channel/Buffer" sampleChannel
+        , discriminates @Tensor @Input "Tensor/Input" sampleTensor
+        , discriminates @Input @Tensor "Input/Tensor" sampleInput
+        , discriminates @Permutation @Buffer
+            "Permutation/Buffer"
+            samplePermutation
+        ]
+    ]

+group :: String -> [Spec] -> Spec
+group name = describe name . sequence_
