+  def test_category_selection_uses_perfetto_default_deny(self):
+    # Perfetto v57.2 enables unmatched C++ categories by default. Its documented
+    # finite allow-list form adds a wildcard deny after the exact enabled names.
+    base_disabled = ["driver-detail", "hwattention-detail", "loading"]
+    cases = (
+      (
+        "finite-base-exclusions",
+        ("--categories", "driver,sys,memory"),
+        ["driver", "sys", "memory"],
+        [*base_disabled, "*"],
+      ),
+      (
+        "wildcard-base-exclusions",
+        ("--categories", "*,memory"),
+        ["*", "memory"],
+        base_disabled,
+      ),
+      (
+        "finite-explicit-exclusions",
+        ("--categories", "driver,sys", "--exclude-categories", "loading"),
+        ["driver", "sys"],
+        ["loading", "*"],
+      ),
+      (
+        "wildcard-explicit-exclusions",
+        ("--categories", "*,memory", "--exclude-categories", "loading"),
+        ["*", "memory"],
+        ["loading"],
+      ),
+    )
+    for name, args, expected_enabled, expected_disabled in cases:
+      with self.subTest(name=name):
+        result = self.run_generator("runtron", *args)
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        categories = track_event(text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig()))[
+          0
+        ].config.track_event_config
+        self.assertCountEqual(categories.enabled_categories, expected_enabled)
+        self.assertCountEqual(categories.disabled_categories, expected_disabled)
+
+  def test_incremental_categories_preserve_base_policy(self):
+    cases = (
+      (
+        ["*"],
+        ["loading"],
+        "+memory,loading",
+        "+scheduler,driver-detail",
+        ["*", "memory", "loading"],
+        ["loading", "scheduler", "driver-detail"],
+      ),
+      (
+        ["model", "model", "scheduler", "scheduler"],
+        ["*", "quiet", "quiet"],
+        "+memory,model,memory",
+        "+scheduler,quiet,loading,scheduler",
+        ["model", "model", "memory"],
+        ["*", "quiet", "quiet", "scheduler", "loading"],
+      ),
+      (
+        [],
+        [],
+        "+model,scheduler",
+        "+loading,driver-detail",
+        ["model", "scheduler"],
+        ["loading", "driver-detail"],
+      ),
+      (
+        ["scheduler"],
+        ["loading"],
+        "model",
+        "+scheduler",
+        ["model"],
+        ["loading", "scheduler", "*"],
+      ),
+      (
+        ["model"],
+        ["*"],
+        "+memory",
+        "loading",
+        ["model", "memory"],
+        ["loading"],
+      ),
+      (
+        ["scheduler"],
+        ["loading"],
+        "model",
+        "scheduler",
+        ["model"],
+        ["scheduler", "*"],
+      ),
+    )
+    path = self.root / "incremental.cfg"
+    for (
+      base_enabled,
+      base_disabled,
+      enabled,
+      disabled,
+      want_enabled,
+      want_disabled,
+    ) in cases:
+      with self.subTest(base=base_enabled, enabled=enabled, disabled=disabled):
+        base = text_format.Parse(
+          "buffers { size_kb: 1024 } duration_ms: 1234\n"
+          'data_sources { config { name: "track_event" } }\n',
+          TraceConfig(),
+        )
+        track = track_event(base)[0].config.track_event_config
+        track.enabled_categories.extend(base_enabled)
+        track.disabled_categories.extend(base_disabled)
+        path.write_text(text_format.MessageToString(base))
+        expected = TraceConfig()
+        expected.CopyFrom(base)
+        track = track_event(expected)[0].config.track_event_config
+        track.enabled_categories[:] = want_enabled
+        track.disabled_categories[:] = want_disabled
+        result = self.run_generator(
+          "runtron",
+          "--base-config",
+          path,
+          "--categories",
+          enabled,
+          "--exclude-categories",
+          disabled,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        self.assertEqual(text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig()), expected)
+
+  def test_finite_categories_reject_non_global_enabled_tags(self):
+    # Perfetto v57.2 TrackEventInternal::IsCategoryEnabled checks exact/prefix
+    # tag enables before the global category deny. Reject this combination
+    # even when other base rules could make a tag enable redundant.
+    base_path = self.root / "tagged.cfg"
+    for tag_fields in (
+      'enabled_tags: "debug"',
+      'enabled_tags: "deb*"',
+      'enabled_tags: "*" enabled_tags: "debug"',
+      'enabled_tags: "debug" disabled_tags: "debug"',
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(tag_fields=tag_fields):
+        base_path.write_text(
+          "buffers { size_kb: 1024 }\n"
+          'data_sources { config { name: "track_event" '
+          f"track_event_config {{ {tag_fields} }} }} }}\n"
+        )
+        for exclusions in ((), ("--exclude-categories", "+loading")):
+          result = self.run_generator(
+            "runtron",
+            "--base-config",
+            base_path,
+            "--categories",
+            "scheduler",
+            *exclusions,
+          )
+          self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2, result.stderr)
+          self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "")
+          self.assertIn("--categories", result.stderr)
+          self.assertIn("enabled_tags", result.stderr)
+
+  def test_other_overrides_preserve_enabled_tags(self):
+    base_path = self.root / "tagged.cfg"
+    base_path.write_text(
+      "buffers { size_kb: 1024 }\n"
+      'data_sources { config { name: "track_event" track_event_config { '
+      'enabled_categories: "driver" disabled_categories: "loading" '
+      'enabled_tags: "debug" disabled_tags: "debug" } } }\n'
+    )
+    base = read_pbtxt(base_path)
+    for args in (
+      (),
+      ("--duration-ms", "77"),
+      ("--categories", "*"),
+      ("--exclude-categories", "memory"),
+      ("--categories", "+memory,loading"),
+      ("--exclude-categories", "+driver,memory"),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(args=args):
+        expected = TraceConfig()
+        expected.CopyFrom(base)
+        track = track_event(expected)[0].config.track_event_config
+        if args == ("--duration-ms", "77"):
+          expected.duration_ms = 77
+        elif args == ("--categories", "*"):
+          track.enabled_categories[:] = ["*"]
+        elif args == ("--exclude-categories", "memory"):
+          track.disabled_categories[:] = ["memory"]
+        elif args == ("--categories", "+memory,loading"):
+          track.enabled_categories.extend(("memory", "loading"))
+        elif args == ("--exclude-categories", "+driver,memory"):
+          del track.enabled_categories[:]
+          track.disabled_categories.extend(("driver", "memory"))
+        result = self.run_generator("runtron", "--base-config", base_path, *args)
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        self.assertEqual(text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig()), expected)

+  def test_track_buffer_follows_target_mapping_in_each_config(self):

+  def test_track_buffer_resolves_named_targets(self):
+    template = (
+      'buffers { name: "system" size_kb: 1 }\n'
+      'buffers { name: "app" size_kb: 2 }\n'
+      'data_sources { config { name: "track_event" ROUTING } }\n'
+    )
+    for name, routing, expected in (
+      ("named", 'target_buffer_name: "app"', [1, 1234]),
+      ("consistent", 'target_buffer: 1 target_buffer_name: "app"', [1, 1234]),
+      ("empty", 'target_buffer_name: ""', [1234, 2]),
+      ("zero-with-name", 'target_buffer: 0 target_buffer_name: "app"', [1, 1234]),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(name=name):
+        base = self.root / f"{name}.cfg"
+        base.write_text(template.replace("ROUTING", routing))
+        result = self.run_generator(
+          "runtron", "--base-config", base, "--buffer-kb", "1234"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        config = text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig())
+        self.assertEqual([buffer.size_kb for buffer in config.buffers], expected)
+
+    invalid = {
+      "missing": ('target_buffer_name: "missing"', "missing"),
+      "duplicate": ('target_buffer_name: "system"', "system"),
+      "out-of-range": ("target_buffer: 2", "2"),
+      "inconsistent": (
+        'target_buffer: 1 target_buffer_name: "system"',
+        "system",
+      ),
+    }
+    for name, (routing, diagnostic) in invalid.items():
+      with self.subTest(name=name):
+        base = self.root / f"{name}.cfg"
+        source = template.replace("ROUTING", routing)
+        if name == "duplicate":
+          source = source.replace('name: "app"', 'name: "system"', 1)
+        base.write_text(source)
+        result = self.run_generator(
+          "runtron", "--base-config", base, "--buffer-kb", "1234"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2)
+        self.assertIn(diagnostic, result.stderr)
+

+  def test_each_tuning_override_preserves_unrequested_fields(self):
+    base_path = self.root / "unicode.cfg"
+    base = read_pbtxt(PERFETTO_DIR / "sigusr1.cfg")
+    base.unique_session_name = "café"
+    base.buffers[0].name = "system"
+    base.buffers[1].name = "app"
+    source = track_event(base)[0].config
+    source.target_buffer = 0
+    source.target_buffer_name = "app"
+    source.track_event_config.enabled_categories.extend(("sys", "sys*"))
+    source.track_event_config.enabled_tags.append("*")
+    base.ClearField("write_into_file")
+    base.ClearField("file_write_period_ms")
+    base_path.write_text(
+      text_format.MessageToString(base, as_utf8=True),
+      encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    self.assertIn("café".encode(), base_path.read_bytes())
+
+    env = os.environ.copy()
+    env.pop("PYTHONIOENCODING", None)
+    env.update(
+      LC_ALL="C",
+      PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE="0",
+      PYTHONUTF8="0",
+    )
+    for option, value in (
+      ("--categories", "driver,sys"),
+      ("--exclude-categories", "loading,driver"),
+      ("--categories", "+driver,memory"),
+      ("--exclude-categories", "+loading,sys"),
+      ("--buffer-kb", "1234"),
+      ("--fill", "discard"),
+      ("--duration-ms", "77"),
+      ("--write-period-ms", "250"),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(option=option, value=value):
+        expected = TraceConfig()
+        expected.CopyFrom(base)
+        track = track_event(expected)[0].config.track_event_config
+        if (option, value) == ("--categories", "+driver,memory"):
+          track.enabled_categories.extend(("driver", "memory"))
+        elif (option, value) == ("--exclude-categories", "+loading,sys"):
+          track.enabled_categories.remove("sys")
+          track.disabled_categories.append("sys")
+        elif option == "--categories":
+          del track.enabled_categories[:]
+          track.enabled_categories.extend(("driver", "sys"))
+          track.disabled_categories.append("*")
+        elif option == "--exclude-categories":
+          del track.disabled_categories[:]
+          track.disabled_categories.extend(("loading", "driver"))
+        elif option == "--buffer-kb":
+          expected.buffers[1].size_kb = 1234
+        elif option == "--fill":
+          expected.buffers[1].fill_policy = TraceConfig.BufferConfig.DISCARD
+        elif option == "--duration-ms":
+          expected.duration_ms = 77
+        elif option == "--write-period-ms":
+          expected.write_into_file = True
+          expected.file_write_period_ms = 250
+
+        result = self.run_generator(
+          "runtron",
+          "--base-config",
+          base_path,
+          option,
+          value,
+          env=env,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        actual = text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig())
+        if option in ("--categories", "--exclude-categories"):
+          actual_track = track_event(actual)[0].config.track_event_config
+          fields = (
+            ("enabled_categories", "disabled_categories")
+            if option == "--categories" or value == "+loading,sys"
+            else ("disabled_categories",)
+          )
+          for field in fields:
+            self.assertCountEqual(getattr(actual_track, field), getattr(track, field))
+            actual_track.ClearField(field)
+            track.ClearField(field)
+        self.assertEqual(actual, expected)
+
+  def test_fill_and_streaming_validation_uses_effective_config(self):
+    streamed = self.run_generator("runtron", "--fill", "discard")
+    self.assertEqual(streamed.returncode, 2)
+    self.assertIn("DISCARD", streamed.stderr)
+
+    stopped = self.run_generator(
+      "runtron",
+      "--exclude-categories",
+      "",
+      "--fill",
+      "discard",
+      "--write-period-ms",
+      "0",
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(stopped.returncode, 0, stopped.stderr)
+    config = text_format.Parse(stopped.stdout, TraceConfig())
+    track = track_event(config)[0].config
+    self.assertEqual(
+      config.buffers[track.target_buffer].fill_policy,
+      TraceConfig.BufferConfig.DISCARD,
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(list(track.track_event_config.disabled_categories), [])
+    self.assertFalse(config.write_into_file)
+    self.assertEqual(config.file_write_period_ms, 0)
+
+    discard = self.root / "discard.cfg"
+    discard.write_text("buffers { size_kb: 1 fill_policy: DISCARD }\n")
+    invalid = self.run_generator(
+      "runtron", "--base-config", discard, "--write-period-ms", "250"
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(invalid.returncode, 2)
+    self.assertIn("DISCARD", invalid.stderr)
+
+    inherited = self.root / "inherited-streaming-discard.cfg"
+    inherited.write_text(
+      "duration_ms: 500\n"
+      "buffers { size_kb: 1 fill_policy: DISCARD }\n"
+      "write_into_file: true\n"
+      "file_write_period_ms: 250\n"
+      'output_path: "service.trace"\n'
+    )
+    preserved = self.run_generator(
+      "runtron", "--base-config", inherited, "--duration-ms", "750"
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(preserved.returncode, 0, preserved.stderr)
+    self.assertIn("DISCARD", preserved.stderr)
+    config = text_format.Parse(preserved.stdout, TraceConfig())
+    expected = read_pbtxt(inherited)
+    expected.duration_ms = 750
+    self.assertEqual(config, expected)
+
+    # Perfetto v57.2 rejects CLI -o when the config retains output_path.
+    stopped = self.run_generator(
+      "runtron", "--base-config", inherited, "--write-period-ms", "0"
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(stopped.returncode, 0, stopped.stderr)
+    config = text_format.Parse(stopped.stdout, TraceConfig())
+    expected = read_pbtxt(inherited)
+    expected.ClearField("write_into_file")
+    expected.ClearField("file_write_period_ms")
+    expected.ClearField("output_path")
+    self.assertEqual(config, expected)
+
+  def test_generator_rejects_invalid_input(self):
+    malformed = self.root / "malformed.cfg"
+    malformed.write_text("buffers { size_kb: }\n")
+    invalid_utf8 = self.root / "invalid-utf8.cfg"
+    invalid_utf8.write_bytes(b"\xff")
+    inherited = self.root / "inherited-enable.cfg"
+    inherited.write_text(
+      "buffers { size_kb: 1024 }\n"
+      'data_sources { config { name: "track_event" track_event_config { '
+      'enabled_categories: "scheduler" } } }\n'
+    )
+    cases = (
+      (("--categories", ""), "--categories"),
+      (("--categories", "alpha,,beta"), "--categories"),
+      (("--categories", "alpha,  ,beta"), "--categories"),
+      (("--exclude-categories", "alpha,,beta"), "--exclude-categories"),
+      (("--categories", "driver*"), "--categories"),
+      (("--exclude-categories", "driver*"), "--exclude-categories"),
+      (("--exclude-categories", "*"), "--exclude-categories"),
+      *(
+        ((f"{option}={value}",), option)
+        for option in ("--categories", "--exclude-categories")
+        for value in (
+          "+",
+          "+*",
+          "+driver*",
+          "+model,+scheduler",
+          "model,+scheduler",
+          "+model,-scheduler",
+          "model,-scheduler",
+          "-scheduler",
+          "+model,,scheduler",
+          " ",
+        )
+      ),
+      *(
+        (args, "--exclude-categories")
+        for enabled, disabled in (
+          ("model", "+model"),
+          ("+model", "model"),
+          ("+model", "+model"),
+        )
+        for args in (
+          ("--categories", enabled, "--exclude-categories", disabled),
+          ("--exclude-categories", disabled, "--categories", enabled),
+        )
+      ),
+      (
+        ("--categories", "+model", "--exclude-categories", "*"),
+        "--exclude-categories",
+      ),
+      (
+        (
+          "--base-config",
+          inherited,
+          "--categories",
+          "+model",
+          "--exclude-categories",
+          "scheduler",
+        ),
+        "--exclude-categories",
+      ),
+      (
+        (
+          "--categories",
+          "driver,sys",
+          "--exclude-categories",
+          "driver",
+        ),
+        "--exclude-categories",
+      ),
+      (("--buffer-kb", "abc"), "--buffer-kb"),
+      (("--buffer-kb", "0"), "4194303"),
+      (("--buffer-kb", "4194304"), "4194303"),
+      (("--duration-ms", "-1"), "--duration-ms"),
+      (("--duration-ms", "٥٠٠"), "--duration-ms"),
+      (("--write-period-ms", "-1"), "--write-period-ms"),
+      (("--write-period-ms", "99"), "100"),
+      (("--fill", "fifo"), "--fill"),
+      (("--duration-ms", "4294967296"), "4294967295"),
+      (("--duration-ms", "604800001"), "604800000"),
+      (("--duration-ms", "9" * 5000), "--duration-ms"),
+      (("--base-config", malformed), str(malformed)),
+      (("--base-config", invalid_utf8), str(invalid_utf8)),
+      (("--os-buffer-kb", "8"), "--os-events"),
+      (
+        ("--os-events", "--os-buffer-kb", "4194304"),
+        "4194303",
+      ),
+      (
+        ("--base-config", malformed, "--os-buffer-kb", "8"),
+        "--os-events",
+      ),
+      (("--format", "json"), "--format"),
+      (("--cat", "driver"), "--cat"),
+      (
+        (
+          "--base-config",
+          PERFETTO_DIR / "runtron.cfg",
+          "--base-config",
+          PERFETTO_DIR / "ring3.cfg",
+        ),
+        "--base-config",
+      ),
+    )
+    for args, diagnostic in cases:
+      with self.subTest(args=args):
+        result = self.run_generator("runtron", *args)
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2)
+        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "")
+        self.assertIn(diagnostic, result.stderr)
+
+  def test_generator_accepts_numeric_boundaries(self):
+    result = self.run_generator(
+      "runtron",
+      "--write-period-ms",
+      "100",
+      "--duration-ms",
+      "604800000",
+      "--buffer-kb",
+      "4194303",
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+    config = text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig())
+    self.assertEqual(config.file_write_period_ms, 100)
+    self.assertEqual(config.duration_ms, 604800000)
+    self.assertEqual(track_event(config)[0].config.target_buffer, 1)
+    self.assertEqual(config.buffers[1].size_kb, 4194303)
+
+    result = self.run_generator("runtron", "--duration-ms", "00000000001")
+    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+    config = text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig())
+    self.assertEqual(config.duration_ms, 1)
+
+    # v57.2 TraceBufferV2::Initialize rounds to 4 KiB before its uint32 check.
+    # TraceBufferV1WithV2Shadow::Create also constructs a V2 buffer.
+    for mode in ("TRACE_BUFFER_V2", "TRACE_BUFFER_V2_SHADOW_MODE"):
+      with self.subTest(mode=mode):
+        base = self.root / f"{mode}.cfg"
+        base.write_text(
+          f"buffers {{ size_kb: 4 experimental_mode: {mode} }}\n"
+          'data_sources { config { name: "track_event" } }\n'
+        )
+        accepted = self.run_generator(
+          "runtron", "--base-config", base, "--buffer-kb", "4194300"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(accepted.returncode, 0, accepted.stderr)
+        expected = read_pbtxt(base)
+        expected.buffers[0].size_kb = 4194300
+        self.assertEqual(text_format.Parse(accepted.stdout, TraceConfig()), expected)
+
+        rejected = self.run_generator(
+          "runtron", "--base-config", base, "--buffer-kb", "4194301"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(rejected.returncode, 2)
+        self.assertEqual(rejected.stdout, "")
+        self.assertIn("size_kb", rejected.stderr)
+

+  def test_buffer_overrides_honor_service_guardrails(self):
+    guarded = self.root / "guarded-buffers.cfg"
+    guarded.write_text(
+      "enable_extra_guardrails: true\n"
+      "buffers { size_kb: 131068 fill_policy: RING_BUFFER }\n"
+      "buffers { size_kb: 4 fill_policy: RING_BUFFER }\n"
+      'data_sources { config { name: "track_event" target_buffer: 1 } }\n'
+    )
+
+    not_multiple = self.run_generator(
+      "runtron", "--base-config", guarded, "--buffer-kb", "5"
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(not_multiple.returncode, 2)
+    self.assertIn("size_kb", not_multiple.stderr)
+    self.assertIn("4", not_multiple.stderr)
+
+    too_large = self.run_generator(
+      "runtron", "--base-config", guarded, "--buffer-kb", "8"
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(too_large.returncode, 2)
+    self.assertIn("131076", too_large.stderr)
+    self.assertIn("131072", too_large.stderr)
+
+    overridden = self.root / "guarded-buffers-override.cfg"
+    overridden.write_text(
+      guarded.read_text()
+      + "guardrail_overrides { max_tracing_buffer_size_kb: 131076 }\n"
+    )
+    accepted = self.run_generator(
+      "runtron", "--base-config", overridden, "--buffer-kb", "8"
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(accepted.returncode, 0, accepted.stderr)
+    config = text_format.Parse(accepted.stdout, TraceConfig())
+    self.assertEqual([buffer.size_kb for buffer in config.buffers], [131068, 8])

+  def test_top_level_overrides_honor_effective_trigger_mode(self):
+    trigger_paths = {}
+    for name, mode, compatibility in (
+      ("start", "START_TRACING", ""),
+      ("stop", "STOP_TRACING", ""),
+      ("clone", "CLONE_SNAPSHOT", ""),
+      ("legacy-clone", "STOP_TRACING", "use_clone_snapshot_if_available: true"),
+    ):
+      path = self.root / f"{name}.cfg"
+      path.write_text(
+        "buffers { size_kb: 1 fill_policy: RING_BUFFER }\n"
+        "trigger_config {\n"
+        f"  trigger_mode: {mode}\n"
+        "  trigger_timeout_ms: 1000\n"
+        '  triggers { name: "test" }\n'
+        f"  {compatibility}\n"
+        "}\n"
+      )
+      trigger_paths[name] = path
+
+      rejected = self.run_generator(
+        "runtron", "--base-config", path, "--duration-ms", "1"
+      )
+      self.assertEqual(rejected.returncode, 2, name)
+      self.assertIn("--duration-ms", rejected.stderr)
+
+      uncapped = self.run_generator(
+        "runtron", "--base-config", path, "--duration-ms", "0"
+      )
+      self.assertEqual(uncapped.returncode, 0, uncapped.stderr)
+      config = text_format.Parse(uncapped.stdout, TraceConfig())
+      self.assertEqual(config.duration_ms, 0)
+
+    for name in ("stop", "clone", "legacy-clone"):
+      rejected = self.run_generator(
+        "runtron",
+        "--base-config",
+        trigger_paths[name],
+        "--write-period-ms",
+        "100",
+      )
+      self.assertEqual(rejected.returncode, 2, name)
+      self.assertIn("--write-period-ms", rejected.stderr)
+
+    streamed = self.run_generator(
+      "runtron",
+      "--base-config",
+      trigger_paths["start"],
+      "--write-period-ms",
+      "100",
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(streamed.returncode, 0, streamed.stderr)
+
+    stop_streamed = self.root / "stop-streamed.cfg"
+    stop_streamed.write_text(
+      trigger_paths["stop"].read_text()
+      + "write_into_file: true\nfile_write_period_ms: 250\n"
+    )
+    cleared = self.run_generator(
+      "runtron", "--base-config", stop_streamed, "--write-period-ms", "0"
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(cleared.returncode, 0, cleared.stderr)
+    config = text_format.Parse(cleared.stdout, TraceConfig())
+    self.assertFalse(config.write_into_file)
+    self.assertEqual(config.file_write_period_ms, 0)
+

+  def test_generator_rejects_unmarked_or_mismatched_schema(self):
+    # The generator checks this release on every run, so the suite needs no
+    # separate sync assertion.
+    real_marker = (
+      Path(os.environ["TRON_PERFETTO_SCHEMA_DIR"]) / "perfetto_schema_release.txt"
+    )

+
+    fake = self.root / "fake-schema"

+    (fake / "perfetto_config_pb2.py").write_text("class TraceConfig:\n  pass\n")
+    env = os.environ.copy()
+    env["TRON_PERFETTO_SCHEMA_DIR"] = str(fake)
+
+    unmarked = self.run_generator("runtron", env=env)
+    self.assertEqual(unmarked.returncode, 1)
+    self.assertIn(str(fake), unmarked.stderr)
+
+    (fake / "perfetto_schema_release.txt").write_text("56.0")
+    mismatched = self.run_generator("runtron", env=env)
+    self.assertEqual(mismatched.returncode, 1)
+    self.assertIn("56.0", mismatched.stderr)
+    self.assertIn(pinned, mismatched.stderr)
+
+    namespace = self.root / "fake-namespace-schema"
+    namespace.mkdir()
+    (namespace / "perfetto_config_pb2.py").write_text("__file__ = None\n")
+    env["TRON_PERFETTO_SCHEMA_DIR"] = str(namespace)
+    no_location = self.run_generator("runtron", env=env)
+    self.assertEqual(no_location.returncode, 1)
+    self.assertIn("TraceConfig", no_location.stderr)

+  def test_os_events_adds_default_sources_and_rejects_option_values(self):
+    result = self.run_generator("runtron", "--os-events")

+        "sched/sched_process_fork",
+        "sched/sched_process_free",
+        "sched/sched_process_hang",
+        "sched/sched_process_wait",
+        "raw_syscalls/sys_enter",
+        "raw_syscalls/sys_exit",

+        "irq/irq_handler_exit",

+        "kmem/mm_page_free",
+        "vmscan/mm_vmscan_direct_reclaim_begin",
+        "vmscan/mm_vmscan_direct_reclaim_end",
+        "oom/oom_score_adj_update",
+        "oom/mark_victim",
+        "block/block_rq_issue",
+        "block/block_rq_complete",
+        "exceptions/page_fault_user",
+        "power/cpu_idle",
+      ],

+        "stat_period_ms": 1000,
+      },

+    self.assertFalse(stats.vmstat_counters)
+    counter_enum = stats.DESCRIPTOR.fields_by_name["stat_counters"].enum_type

+      "runtron",
+      "--base-config",
+      PERFETTO_DIR / "ring3.cfg",

+    self.assertIn("--os-events", non_streamed.stderr)

+  def test_os_sources_target_the_appended_buffer(self):
+    base = self.root / "multi-buffer.cfg"
+    base.write_text(
+      "buffers { size_kb: 7 fill_policy: DISCARD }\n"
+      "buffers: { size_kb: 8 fill_policy: RING_BUFFER }\n"
+      'data_sources { config { name: "linux.sys_stats" target_buffer: 1 } }\n'
+      "write_into_file: true\n"
+      "file_write_period_ms: 777\n"
+    )
+    result = self.run_generator(
+      "runtron",
+      "--base-config",
+      base,
+      "--os-events",
+      "--os-buffer-kb",
+      "4096",
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+    config = TraceConfig()
+    text_format.Parse(result.stdout, config)
+    self.assertEqual(
+      [(buffer.size_kb, buffer.fill_policy) for buffer in config.buffers],
+      [
+        (7, TraceConfig.BufferConfig.DISCARD),
+        (8, TraceConfig.BufferConfig.RING_BUFFER),
+        (4096, TraceConfig.BufferConfig.RING_BUFFER),
+      ],
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(
+      [source.config.target_buffer for source in config.data_sources],
+      [1, 2, 2],
+    )
+    self.assertEqual(
+      [source.config.name for source in config.data_sources].count("linux.sys_stats"),
+      2,
+    )
+    self.assertTrue(config.write_into_file)
+    self.assertEqual(config.file_write_period_ms, 777)
+
+    for name in CONFIGS:
+      with self.subTest(config=name):
+        base = read_pbtxt(PERFETTO_DIR / f"{name}.cfg")
+        result = self.run_generator(
+          "runtron",
+          "--base-config",
+          PERFETTO_DIR / f"{name}.cfg",
+          "--os-events",
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        config = text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig())
+        self.assertEqual(len(config.buffers), len(base.buffers) + 1)
+        self.assertEqual(
+          list(config.data_sources[: len(base.data_sources)]),
+          list(base.data_sources),
+        )
+        appended = config.data_sources[len(base.data_sources) :]
+        self.assertCountEqual(
+          [source.config.name for source in appended],
+          ["linux.ftrace", "linux.sys_stats"],
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(
+          all(source.config.target_buffer == len(base.buffers) for source in appended)
+        )
+        sched_switches = [
+          event
+          for source in config.data_sources
+          if source.config.name == "linux.ftrace"
+          for event in source.config.ftrace_config.ftrace_events
+          if event.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] == "sched_switch"
+        ]
+        expected = (
+          ["sched_switch"] if name in {"rinzler", "ring3"} else ["sched/sched_switch"]
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(sched_switches, expected)
+        appended_ftrace = next(
+          source for source in appended if source.config.name == "linux.ftrace"
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(appended_ftrace.config.ftrace_config.compact_sched.enabled)
+
+  def test_os_events_rejects_invalid_original_buffer_routes(self):
+    # v57.2 TracingServiceImpl::EnableTracing checks names and routes before
+    # assigning any buffers to data sources.
+    one_buffer = 'buffers { size_kb: 1024 name: "first" }\n'
+    two_buffers = one_buffer + 'buffers { size_kb: 2048 name: "second" }\n'
+    for name, buffers, source, routing, diagnostic in (
+      ("track-index", one_buffer, "track_event", "target_buffer: 1", "track_event"),
+      (
+        "other-index",
+        one_buffer,
+        "linux.process_stats",
+        "target_buffer: 1",
+        "linux.process_stats",
+      ),
+      (
+        "missing-name",
+        two_buffers,
+        "linux.process_stats",
+        'target_buffer_name: "missing"',
+        "missing",
+      ),
+      (
+        "conflicting-route",
+        two_buffers,
+        "linux.process_stats",
+        'target_buffer: 1 target_buffer_name: "first"',
+        "linux.process_stats",
+      ),
+      (
+        "unused-duplicate-name",
+        one_buffer + one_buffer,
+        "linux.process_stats",
+        "",
+        "first",
+      ),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(name=name):
+        base = self.root / f"{name}.cfg"
+        base.write_text(
+          buffers + f'data_sources {{ config {{ name: "{source}" {routing} }} }}\n'
+        )
+        unchanged = self.run_generator("runtron", "--base-config", base)
+        self.assertEqual(unchanged.returncode, 0, unchanged.stderr)
+        self.assertEqual(
+          text_format.Parse(unchanged.stdout, TraceConfig()), read_pbtxt(base)
+        )
+        result = self.run_generator("runtron", "--base-config", base, "--os-events")
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2, result.stderr)
+        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "")
+        self.assertIn(diagnostic, result.stderr)
+
+  def test_os_events_preserves_original_numeric_and_named_routes(self):
+    # v57.2 treats an empty name as absent and numeric zero as unspecified
+    # beside a nonempty name, even when that name resolves to another buffer.
+    routes = (
+      ("", 0),
+      ("target_buffer: 0", 0),
+      ('target_buffer_name: ""', 0),
+      ('target_buffer: 1 target_buffer_name: ""', 1),
+      ('target_buffer_name: "app"', 3),
+      ('target_buffer: 0 target_buffer_name: "app"', 3),
+      ('target_buffer: 3 target_buffer_name: "app"', 3),
+    )
+    base = self.root / "valid-os-routes.cfg"
+    base.write_text(
+      "buffers { size_kb: 1024 }\n"
+      'buffers { size_kb: 2048 name: "" }\n'
+      'buffers { size_kb: 3072 name: "system" }\n'
+      'buffers { size_kb: 4096 name: "app" }\n'
+      "duration_ms: 1234 write_into_file: true file_write_period_ms: 777\n"
+      + "".join(
+        'data_sources { config { name: "linux.process_stats" ' + routing + " } }\n"
+        for routing, _index in routes
+      )
+    )
+    original = read_pbtxt(base)
+    result = self.run_generator("runtron", "--base-config", base, "--os-events")
+    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+    config = text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig())
+    self.assertEqual(len(config.buffers), len(original.buffers) + 1)
+    self.assertEqual(list(config.buffers[:4]), list(original.buffers))
+    self.assertEqual(
+      list(config.data_sources[: len(routes)]), list(original.data_sources)
+    )
+    for source, (_routing, expected) in zip(config.data_sources, routes):
+      target = source.config
+      if target.target_buffer_name:
+        self.assertEqual(config.buffers[expected].name, target.target_buffer_name)
+      else:
+        self.assertEqual(target.target_buffer, expected)
+    appended = config.data_sources[len(routes) :]
+    self.assertCountEqual(
+      [source.config.name for source in appended],
+      ["linux.ftrace", "linux.sys_stats"],
+    )
+    self.assertTrue(all(source.config.target_buffer == 4 for source in appended))
+    self.assertEqual(config.duration_ms, original.duration_ms)
+    self.assertEqual(config.write_into_file, original.write_into_file)
+    self.assertEqual(config.file_write_period_ms, original.file_write_period_ms)
+
+  def test_os_events_deduplicates_v57_selectors_and_rejects_unsafe_settings(self):
+    base = self.root / "literal-selectors.cfg"
+    base.write_text(
+      "buffers { size_kb: 1 }\n"
+      'data_sources { config { name: "linux.ftrace" '
+      'ftrace_config { ftrace_events: "sched/*" } } }\n'
+    )
+    result = self.run_generator("runtron", "--base-config", base, "--os-events")
+    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+    config = text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig())
+    appended = next(
+      source.config.ftrace_config
+      for source in config.data_sources
+      if source.config.target_buffer == 1 and source.config.name == "linux.ftrace"
+    )
+    self.assertFalse(
+      any(event.startswith("sched/") for event in appended.ftrace_events)
+    )
+    self.assertIn("raw_syscalls/sys_enter", appended.ftrace_events)
+    self.assertTrue(appended.compact_sched.enabled)
+
+    base.write_text(
+      "buffers { size_kb: 1 }\n"
+      'data_sources { config { name: "linux.ftrace" '
+      'ftrace_config { ftrace_events: "*" '
+      'ftrace_events: "sched/sched_*" } } }\n'
+    )
+    literal = self.run_generator("runtron", "--base-config", base, "--os-events")
+    self.assertEqual(literal.returncode, 0, literal.stderr)
+    config = text_format.Parse(literal.stdout, TraceConfig())
+    appended = next(
+      source.config.ftrace_config
+      for source in config.data_sources
+      if source.config.target_buffer == 1 and source.config.name == "linux.ftrace"
+    )
+    self.assertIn("sched/sched_switch", appended.ftrace_events)
+
+    for name, ftrace, error in (
+      ("atrace", 'atrace_categories: "sched"', "atrace_categories"),
+      ("syscalls", 'syscall_events: "sys_read"', "syscall_events"),
+      ("function-graph", "enable_function_graph: true", "enable_function_graph"),
+      ("tids", "tids_to_trace: 123", "tids_to_trace"),
+      (
+        "tracefs-option",
+        'tracefs_options { name: "event-fork" state: STATE_ENABLED }',
+        "tracefs_options",
+      ),
+      ("cpu-mask", 'tracing_cpumask: "1"', "tracing_cpumask"),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(name=name):
+        ambiguous = self.root / f"{name}.cfg"
+        ambiguous.write_text(
+          "buffers { size_kb: 1 }\n"
+          f'data_sources {{ config {{ name: "linux.ftrace" '
+          f"ftrace_config {{ {ftrace} }} }} }}\n"
+        )
+        rejected = self.run_generator(
+          "runtron", "--base-config", ambiguous, "--os-events"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(rejected.returncode, 2)
+        self.assertIn(error, rejected.stderr)
+
+    filtered = self.root / "filtered-ftrace.cfg"
+    # README.perfetto.md @ c715af28d7: filtered-only event coverage must fail.
+    for field, value in (
+      ("producer_name_filter", "perfetto.traced_probes"),
+      ("producer_name_regex_filter", "^no-such-producer$"),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(filter=field):
+        filtered.write_text(
+          "buffers { size_kb: 1 }\n"
+          f'data_sources {{ {field}: "{value}" '
+          'config { name: "linux.ftrace" '
+          'ftrace_config { ftrace_events: "sched_switch" } } }\n'
+        )
+        rejected = self.run_generator(
+          "runtron", "--base-config", filtered, "--os-events"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(rejected.returncode, 2)
+        self.assertEqual(rejected.stdout, "")
+        self.assertIn("sched/sched_switch", rejected.stderr)
+        self.assertIn(field, rejected.stderr)
+
+  def test_os_events_deduplicates_only_effective_generic_selectors(self):
+    # v57.2 ftrace_config_muxer.cc resolves bare names from event_info.cc.
+    # That table lacks page_fault_user; qualified/group selectors can create
+    # it as a generic event, unless disable_generic_events suppresses it.
+    event = "exceptions/page_fault_user"
+    base = self.root / "generic-ftrace.cfg"
+    for selector, disable_generic, retained in (
+      (event, False, False),
+      (event, True, True),
+      ("exceptions/*", False, False),
+      ("exceptions/*", True, True),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(selector=selector, disable_generic=disable_generic):
+        base.write_text(
+          "buffers { size_kb: 1024 }\n"
+          'data_sources { config { name: "linux.ftrace" ftrace_config { '
+          f'ftrace_events: "{selector}" '
+          f"disable_generic_events: {str(disable_generic).lower()} }} }} }}\n"
+        )
+        original = read_pbtxt(base)
+        result = self.run_generator("runtron", "--base-config", base, "--os-events")
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        config = text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig())
+        self.assertEqual(config.data_sources[0], original.data_sources[0])
+        appended = config.data_sources[1].config.ftrace_config
+        self.assertIn("sched/sched_switch", appended.ftrace_events)
+        self.assertEqual(event in appended.ftrace_events, retained)
+
+    for disable_generic in (False, True):
+      with self.subTest(bare_name=True, disable_generic=disable_generic):
+        base.write_text(
+          "buffers { size_kb: 1024 }\n"
+          'data_sources { config { name: "linux.ftrace" ftrace_config { '
+          'ftrace_events: "page_fault_user" '
+          f"disable_generic_events: {str(disable_generic).lower()} }} }} }}\n"
+        )
+        result = self.run_generator("runtron", "--base-config", base, "--os-events")
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2)
+        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "")
+        self.assertIn("page_fault_user", result.stderr)
+
+  def test_os_events_keeps_compiled_event_aliases_with_generic_events_disabled(self):
+    # Every preset entry except exceptions/page_fault_user appears in
+    # v57.2 src/traced/probes/ftrace/event_info.cc with the same group/name.
+    preset = read_pbtxt(PERFETTO_DIR / "os-events.inc.cfg")
+    compiled = [
+      event
+      for event in preset.data_sources[0].config.ftrace_config.ftrace_events
+      if event != "exceptions/page_fault_user"
+    ]
+    base = self.root / "compiled-ftrace.cfg"
+    for bare in (False, True):
+      with self.subTest(bare=bare):
+        base.write_text(
+          "buffers { size_kb: 1024 }\n"
+          'data_sources { config { name: "linux.ftrace" ftrace_config { '
+          "disable_generic_events: true\n"
+          + "".join(
+            f'ftrace_events: "{event.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] if bare else event}"\n'
+            for event in compiled
+          )
+          + "} } }\n"
+        )
+        result = self.run_generator("runtron", "--base-config", base, "--os-events")
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        config = text_format.Parse(result.stdout, TraceConfig())
+        self.assertEqual(config.data_sources[0], read_pbtxt(base).data_sources[0])
+        self.assertEqual(
+          list(config.data_sources[1].config.ftrace_config.ftrace_events),
+          ["exceptions/page_fault_user"],
+        )
+

+  def test_launchers_require_explicit_executable_binary_set(self):
+    for launcher, run in (
+      ("tronperf", self.run_tronperf),
+      ("wrapper", self.run_wrapper),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(launcher=launcher, lane="help"):
+        env = self.env.copy()
+        env.pop("PERFETTO_BIN_DIR")
+        env.pop("PERFETTO_HOME")
+        result = run("--help", env=env)
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        self.assert_no_launcher_side_effects()
+
+      with self.subTest(launcher=launcher, lane="unconfigured"):
+        env = self.env.copy()
+        env.pop("PERFETTO_BIN_DIR")
+        env.pop("PERFETTO_HOME")
+        result = run(env=env)
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2)
+        self.assertIn("PERFETTO_BIN_DIR", result.stderr)
+        self.assert_no_launcher_side_effects()
+
+      with self.subTest(launcher=launcher, lane="nonexecutable"):
+        traced = self.bin_dir / "traced"
+        traced.chmod(0o644)
+        try:
+          result = run()
+        finally:
+          traced.chmod(0o755)
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2)
+        self.assertIn(str(traced), result.stderr)
+        self.assert_no_launcher_side_effects()

+  def test_launchers_share_tuning_flags_and_os_controls(self):
+    options = (
+      "--categories",
+      "one,two",
+      "--exclude-categories",
+      "quiet",
+      "--buffer-kb",
+      "4096",
+      "--duration-ms",
+      "9000",
+      "--write-period-ms",
+      "250",
+      "--os-buffer-kb",
+      "16384",
+    )
+    for launcher, run in (
+      ("tronperf", self.run_tronperf),
+      ("wrapper", self.run_wrapper),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(launcher=launcher, scenario="all controls"):
+        os_events = "-e" if launcher == "wrapper" else "--os-events"
+        result = run(*options, os_events)
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        config = self.captured_config()
+        track = track_event(config)[0].config
+        self.assertCountEqual(
+          track.track_event_config.enabled_categories, ["one", "two"]
+        )
+        self.assertCountEqual(
+          track.track_event_config.disabled_categories, ["quiet", "*"]
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(config.buffers[track.target_buffer].size_kb, 4096)
+        self.assertEqual(config.buffers[-1].size_kb, 16384)
+        self.assertEqual(config.duration_ms, 9000)
+        self.assertEqual(config.file_write_period_ms, 250)
+        self.assertFalse(self.captured_config_path().exists())
+        self.reset_state()
+
+      with self.subTest(launcher=launcher, scenario="fill"):
+        result = run("--fill", "discard", "--write-period-ms", "0")
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        config = self.captured_config()
+        target = track_event(config)[0].config.target_buffer
+        self.assertEqual(
+          config.buffers[target].fill_policy,
+          TraceConfig.BufferConfig.DISCARD,
+        )
+        self.reset_state()
+
+      with self.subTest(launcher=launcher, scenario="equals syntax"):
+        result = run("--duration-ms=9001", "--os-events", "--os-buffer-kb=8192")
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        config = self.captured_config()
+        self.assertEqual(config.duration_ms, 9001)
+        self.assertEqual(config.buffers[-1].size_kb, 8192)
+        self.reset_state()
+
+      for args in (
+        (
+          "--categories",
+          "+ignored",
+          "--categories",
+          " +memory, loading ",
+          "--exclude-categories",
+          "+ignored",
+          "--exclude-categories",
+          "+scheduler,model",
+        ),
+        (
+          "--categories=+ignored",
+          "--categories=+memory,loading",
+          "--exclude-categories=+ignored",
+          "--exclude-categories=+scheduler,model",
+        ),
+      ):
+        with self.subTest(launcher=launcher, scenario="incremental", args=args):
+          result = run(*args)
+          self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+          default = "runtron" if launcher == "tronperf" else "sigusr1"
+          expected = read_pbtxt(PERFETTO_DIR / f"{default}.cfg")
+          track = track_event(expected)[0].config.track_event_config
+          track.enabled_categories.extend(("memory", "loading"))
+          track.disabled_categories.extend(("scheduler", "model"))
+          self.assertEqual(self.captured_config(), expected)
+          self.assertFalse(self.captured_config_path().exists())
+          self.reset_state()
+
+  def test_launcher_validation_fails_before_starting_capture_processes(self):

+      ),

+        'name: "linux.process_stats" target_buffer: 1',
+        ("--os-events",),
+        "linux.process_stats",
+      ),
+      (
+        'name: "linux.ftrace" ftrace_config { ftrace_events: "page_fault_user" }',
+        ("--os-events",),
+        "page_fault_user",
+      ),
+    ):
+      custom.write_text(
+        f"buffers {{ size_kb: 1024 }}\ndata_sources {{ config {{ {source} }} }}\n"
+      )
+      for run in (self.run_tronperf, self.run_wrapper):
+        with self.subTest(launcher=run.__name__, options=options):
+          result = run("--perfetto-config", custom, *options)
+          self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2, result.stderr)
+          self.assertIn(error, result.stderr)
+          self.assert_no_launcher_side_effects()
+
+    for args in (
+      ("--output", ""),
+      ("--pid", "0"),
+      ("--name", ""),
+      ("-c", ""),
+      ("-c", "rinzler", "--perfetto-config", PERFETTO_DIR / "apponly.cfg"),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(args=args):
+        result = self.run_wrapper(*args)

+    env = self.env.copy()
+    env["TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT"] = "31"

+      result = run(env=env)

+    alternate_tracefs = self.root / "alternate-tracefs"

+  def test_tracefs_repair_is_limited_to_exact_trusted_default(self):
+    sudo = self.tools_dir / "sudo"
+    sudo.write_text(
+      f"#!{shutil.which('bash')}\n"
+      'printf "%s\\n" "$@" >"$FAKE_STATE/sudo.args"\n'
+      '[ -z "${FAKE_SUDO_FAIL:-}" ] || exit 73\n'
+      'chmod u+w "$5/tracing_on"\n'
+    )
+    sudo.chmod(0o755)
+    tracing_on = self.tracefs / "tracing_on"
+    command = [
+      shutil.which("bash"),
+      "-c",
+      'SELF_DIR=$1; . "$SELF_DIR/launcher-common"; '
+      "TRACEFS=$2; DEFAULT_TRACEFS=$2; prepare_tracefs",
+      "tracefs-test",
+      PERFETTO_DIR,
+    ]
+
+    def run(tracefs=self.tracefs, **updates):
+      env = self.env.copy()
+      env.update(USER="trace-user", **updates)
+      return subprocess.run(
+        [*command, tracefs],
+        cwd=REPO,
+        env=env,
+        text=True,
+        capture_output=True,
+      )
+
+    try:
+      tracing_on.chmod(0o444)
+      repaired = run()
+      self.assertEqual(repaired.returncode, 0, repaired.stderr)
+      self.assertEqual(
+        (self.state / "sudo.args").read_text().splitlines(),
+        ["chown", "-R", "--", "trace-user", str(self.tracefs)],
+      )
+      self.assertEqual(tracing_on.read_text(), "1\n")
+
+      (self.state / "sudo.args").unlink()
+      tracing_on.chmod(0o444)
+      failed = run(FAKE_SUDO_FAIL="1")
+      self.assertEqual(failed.returncode, 73, failed.stderr)
+      self.assertTrue((self.state / "sudo.args").exists())
+      self.assertEqual(tracing_on.read_text(), "1\n")
+
+      (self.state / "sudo.args").unlink()
+      not_tracefs = self.root / "not-tracefs"
+      not_tracefs.mkdir()
+      (not_tracefs / "events").mkdir()
+      (not_tracefs / "tracing_on").write_text("unchanged\n")
+      rejected = run(not_tracefs)
+      self.assertEqual(rejected.returncode, 1, rejected.stderr)
+      self.assertIn(str(not_tracefs), rejected.stderr)
+      self.assertFalse((self.state / "sudo.args").exists())
+      self.assertEqual(tracing_on.read_text(), "1\n")
+      self.assertEqual((not_tracefs / "tracing_on").read_text(), "unchanged\n")
+    finally:
+      tracing_on.chmod(0o644)
+

+  def test_wrapper_target_signaling_and_duration_wait(self):
+    env = self.env.copy()
+    env["PATH"] = f"{self.bin_dir}:{env['PATH']}"
+    env["FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT"] = "0"
+    env["FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_MARKER"] = str(self.state / "killall.args")
+    for duration_args in (("--duration-ms", "10000"), ("--duration-ms=10000",)):
+      with self.subTest(duration_args=duration_args):
+        result = self.run_launcher(
+          [
+            self.launcher_dir / "wrapper",
+            "--output",
+            self.root / "duration.trace",
+            *duration_args,
+            "-n",
+            "-rinzler",
+          ],
+          env=env,
+          timeout=3,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        self.assertEqual(
+          (self.state / "killall.args").read_text().splitlines(),
+          ["-SIGUSR1", "--", "-rinzler"],
+        )
+        self.reset_state()
+
+    ready = self.root / "target.ready"
+    received = self.root / "target.received"
+    target = subprocess.Popen(
+      [
+        shutil.which("bash"),
+        "-c",
+        'trap \'touch "$2"; exit 0\' USR1; touch "$1"; while :; do sleep 1; done',
+        "target",
+        ready,
+        received,
+      ],
+      start_new_session=True,
+    )
+    self.addCleanup(self.cleanup_process_group, target)
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 2
+    while not ready.exists() and time.monotonic() < deadline:
+      time.sleep(0.02)
+    self.assertTrue(ready.exists())
+
+    env["FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_MARKER"] = str(received)
+    result = self.run_wrapper("-p", str(target.pid), env=env)
+    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+    target.wait(timeout=2)
+    self.assertTrue(received.exists())

+  def test_launcher_times_out_waiting_for_daemon_readiness(self):
+    # Perfetto v57.2 ServiceMain/ProbesMain notify with "1" then EOF.
+    # Reusing the pipe before EOF can attach the next reader to the old writer.
+    for daemon, hold in (
+      ("traced", "FAKE_TRACED_HOLD_READY_FD"),
+      ("traced_probes", "FAKE_TRACED_PROBES_SKIP_NOTIFY"),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(daemon=daemon):
+        self.reset_state()
+        env = self.env.copy()
+        env.update({hold: "1", "TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT": "1"})
+        result = self.run_tronperf(env=env, timeout=3)
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1, result.stderr)
+        self.assertIn(daemon, result.stderr)
+        self.assertFalse((self.state / "perfetto.pid").exists())
+        self.assertFalse((self.state / "runtron.pid").exists())
+        if daemon == "traced":
+          self.assert_processes_gone("traced")
+        else:
+          self.assert_processes_gone("traced", "traced_probes")
+        self.assertFalse(list(self.tmp_dir.iterdir()))
+

+  def test_launchers_do_not_start_targets_before_perfetto_is_ready(self):
+    # Check the native rejection marker too: a fake cannot catch upstream drift.
+    native = Path(os.environ["PERFETTO_TEST_BIN_DIR"])
+    native_env = self.env.copy()
+    socket_name = f"@perfetto-test-{os.getpid()}-{self.root.name}"
+    native_env.update(
+      PERFETTO_PRODUCER_SOCK_NAME=f"{socket_name}-p",
+      PERFETTO_CONSUMER_SOCK_NAME=f"{socket_name}-c",
+    )
+    config = self.root / "native.cfg"
+    read_fd, write_fd = os.pipe()
+    try:
+      service = subprocess.Popen(
+        [native / "traced"],
+        env={**native_env, "TRACED_NOTIFY_FD": str(write_fd)},
+        pass_fds=(write_fd,),
+        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+        start_new_session=True,
+      )
+      self.addCleanup(self.cleanup_process_group, service)
+      os.close(write_fd)
+      write_fd = None
+      self.assertTrue(select.select([read_fd], [], [], 3)[0], "traced not ready")
+      self.assertEqual(os.read(read_fd, 1), b"1")
+      for buffers in (1, 2):
+        config.write_text(
+          'buffers { size_kb: 4 name: "duplicate" }\n' * buffers + "duration_ms: 100\n"
+        )
+        trace = self.root / f"native-{buffers}.trace"
+        capture = subprocess.run(
+          [native / "perfetto", "--txt", "-c", config, "-o", trace, "--notify-fd", "1"],
+          env=native_env,
+          capture_output=True,
+          timeout=3,
+        )
+        if buffers == 1:
+          self.assertEqual(capture.returncode, 0, capture.stderr)
+          self.assertEqual(capture.stdout, b"\0")
+          self.assertGreater(trace.stat().st_size, 0)
+        # A corrected client may report failure directly. A success byte must
+        # retain the diagnostic the launcher needs to distinguish rejection.
+        elif b"\0" in capture.stdout:
+          self.assertIn(b"Service error:", capture.stderr)
+    finally:
+      os.close(read_fd)
+      if write_fd is not None:
+        os.close(write_fd)
+    self.cleanup_process_group(service)
+
+    cases = (
+      (
+        "successful early exit",
+        {"FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_BEFORE_NOTIFY": "1", "FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT": "0"},
+        1,
+      ),
+      (
+        "readiness failure",
+        {"FAKE_PERFETTO_NOTIFY_STATUS": "1", "FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT": "23"},
+        23,
+      ),
+      (
+        "readiness timeout",
+        {
+          "FAKE_PERFETTO_SKIP_NOTIFY": "1",
+          "FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT": "",
+          "TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT": "1",
+        },
+        1,
+      ),
+    )
+    for name, overrides, expected_status in cases:
+      with self.subTest(name=name):
+        env = self.env.copy()
+        env.update(overrides)
+        env["PATH"] = f"{self.bin_dir}:{env['PATH']}"
+        result = self.run_launcher(
+          [
+            self.launcher_dir / "wrapper",
+            "--output",
+            self.root / "not-ready.trace",
+            "--duration-ms",
+            "10000",
+            "--name",
+            "rinzler",
+          ],
+          env=env,
+          timeout=3,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, expected_status, result.stderr)
+        self.assertIn("perfetto", result.stderr)
+        self.assertFalse((self.state / "killall.args").exists())
+        self.assert_processes_gone("perfetto", "traced", "traced_probes")
+        self.reset_state()
+
+    # The native v57.2 client logs rejection, sends NUL, and exits successfully.
+    # Hold it alive after NUL so this cannot pass through a lucky liveness check.
+    for run, args, target in (
+      (self.run_tronperf, (), "runtron.args"),
+      (self.run_wrapper, ("--name", "rinzler"), "killall.args"),
+    ):
+      with self.subTest(service_rejection=target):
+        self.reset_state()
+        env = self.env.copy()
+        env.update(
+          FAKE_PERFETTO_SERVICE_ERROR="1",
+          PATH=f"{self.bin_dir}:{env['PATH']}",
+        )
+        result = run(*args, env=env)
+        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        self.assertIn("Service error: Duplicate buffer name", result.stderr)
+        self.assertFalse((self.state / target).exists())
+        self.assert_processes_gone("perfetto", "traced", "traced_probes")
+        self.assertFalse(list(self.tmp_dir.iterdir()))
+        self.reset_state()
+
+    env = self.env.copy()
+    env["FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_BEFORE_NOTIFY"] = "1"
+    env["FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT"] = "23"
+    result = self.run_tronperf(env=env)
+    self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 23, result.stderr)
+    self.assertIn("perfetto", result.stderr)
+    self.assertFalse((self.state / "runtron.args").exists())
+    self.assert_processes_gone("perfetto", "traced", "traced_probes")
+
+  def wait_for_waiting_helper(self, process):
+    launcher_children = Path(f"/proc/{process.pid}/task/{process.pid}/children")
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 3
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+      self.assertIsNone(process.poll(), "wrapper exited before manual stop")
+      for pid in launcher_children.read_text().split():
+        proc = Path(f"/proc/{pid}")
+        try:
+          if b"perfetto_waiting" not in proc.joinpath("cmdline").read_bytes():
+            continue
+          # A short-lived failed helper must not pass as a manual-stop target.
+          time.sleep(0.1)
+          self.assertIsNone(process.poll(), "wrapper exited before manual stop")
+          if b"perfetto_waiting" not in proc.joinpath("cmdline").read_bytes():
+            continue
+          children = proc.joinpath(f"task/{pid}/children").read_text().split()
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+          continue
+        # Track the old shell's child too, so termination must prove it is gone.
+        names = ["waiting", *[f"waiting-child-{child}" for child in children]]
+        for name, child in zip(names, [pid, *children]):
+          (self.state / f"{name}.pid").write_text(child)
+        return names
+      time.sleep(0.02)
+    self.fail("wrapper did not start its waiting helper")
+
+  def test_wrapper_manual_stop_succeeds(self):
+    env = self.env.copy()
+    env["PATH"] = f"{self.bin_dir}:{env['PATH']}"
+    env["FAKE_FLUSH_CHECK"] = "1"
+    custom = self.root / "duration.cfg"

+  def test_launchers_flush_before_daemon_cleanup_on_term(self):
+    cases = (
+      (
+        "tronperf",
+        [
+          self.launcher_dir / "tronperf",
+          "--output-file",
+          self.root / "term-tron.trace",
+        ],

+      ),
+      (
+        "wrapper",
+        [
+          self.launcher_dir / "wrapper",
+          "--output",
+          self.root / "term-wrapper.trace",
+        ],
+        {},
+      ),
+    )

+      with self.subTest(launcher=launcher):
+        self.reset_state()
+        env = self.env.copy()
+        env.update(extra_env)
+        env["FAKE_FLUSH_CHECK"] = "1"
+        if launcher == "wrapper":
+          env["PATH"] = f"{self.bin_dir}:{env['PATH']}"
+        process = subprocess.Popen(
+          command,
+          cwd=REPO,
+          env=env,
+          text=True,
+          stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+          stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+          start_new_session=True,
+        )
+        self.addCleanup(self.cleanup_process_group, process)
+        required = ["traced.pid", "traced_probes.pid", "perfetto.pid", "config.path"]
+        helper_names = []
+        if launcher == "tronperf":
+          required.append("runtron.pid")
+        else:
+          helper_names = self.wait_for_waiting_helper(process)
+          required.append("waiting.pid")
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 3
+        while (
+          not all((self.state / name).exists() for name in required)
+          and time.monotonic() < deadline
+        ):
+          time.sleep(0.02)
+        self.assertTrue(all((self.state / name).exists() for name in required))
+        generated = self.captured_config_path()
+        process.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
+        order_path = self.state / "shutdown.order"
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 3
+        while (
+          not order_path.exists()
+          or "perfetto-flush-start" not in order_path.read_text()
+        ) and time.monotonic() < deadline:
+          time.sleep(0.02)
+        self.assertIn("perfetto-flush-start", order_path.read_text())
+        process.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
+        process.wait(timeout=5)
+        names = ["perfetto", "traced", "traced_probes", *helper_names]
+        if launcher == "tronperf":
+          names.append("runtron")
+        self.assert_processes_gone(*names)
+        stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=5)
+        self.assertEqual(process.returncode, 143, stdout + stderr)
+        self.assertFalse(generated.exists())
+        order = (self.state / "shutdown.order").read_text().splitlines()
+        self.assertIn("perfetto-flush-complete", order)
+        if launcher == "tronperf":
+          self.assertIn("runtron-stopped", order)
+          self.assertLess(
+            order.index("runtron-stopped"), order.index("perfetto-flush-start")
+          )
+        for daemon in ("traced", "traced_probes"):
+          self.assertIn(f"{daemon}-stopped", order)
+          self.assertLess(
+            order.index("perfetto-flush-complete"), order.index(f"{daemon}-stopped")
+          )

   #[test]
+  fn strftime_now_takes_local_offset_at_pinned_epoch() {
+    // CI runs under UTC, where a dropped offset, a flipped sign, or the
+    // offset of the wall-clock "now" instead of the pinned epoch all render
+    // the same text. Re-run this test in a child process under a POSIX rule
+    // string, which needs no zoneinfo file: UTC-12 standard time, UTC+14
+    // summer time from day 120 to day 300. TZ is process-global and glibc's
+    // localtime_r reads it only once, so this process never changes it. One
+    // instant per regime makes each of those bugs observable whatever today's
+    // date is.
+    const RULE: &str = "<-12>12<+14>-14,J120,J300";
+    if std::env::var("TZ").as_deref() == Ok(RULE) {
+      let t = build_template("{{ strftime_now('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') }}").unwrap();
+      // 2025-01-15T00:00:00Z and 2025-07-15T00:00:00Z.
+      assert_eq!(
+        t.render("{}", 1_736_899_200).unwrap(),
+        "2025-01-14 12:00"
+      );
+      assert_eq!(
+        t.render("{}", 1_752_537_600).unwrap(),
+        "2025-07-15 14:00"
+      );
+      return;
+    }
+    let name = "tests::strftime_now_takes_local_offset_at_pinned_epoch";
+    let out = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
+      .args(["--exact", name, "--test-threads=1"])
+      .env("TZ", RULE)
+      .output()
+      .unwrap();
+    // libtest exits 0 when the filter matches nothing; require one pass.
+    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);
+    assert!(
+      out.status.success() && stdout.contains("test result: ok. 1 passed"),
+      "child under TZ={RULE}: {}\n{stdout}{}",
+      out.status,
+      String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr)
+    );
+  }

+// ordering property, and ordering is what hardware cannot report. Every fetcher
+// of a tensor is meant to be in flight before the first wait; a regression to

+static void require_lark_terminal_name(std::string_view name) {
+  // Predicate hoisted out of the assert: TRON_ASSERT stringifies its
+  // condition into the fmt format string, where a lambda's braces would
+  // parse as replacement fields.
+  auto terminal_char = [](char c) {
+    return (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '_';
+  };
+  bool lark_terminal_name = !name.empty() && name.front() >= 'A' &&
+                            name.front() <= 'Z' &&
+                            std::all_of(name.begin(), name.end(), terminal_char);
+  TRON_ASSERT(lark_terminal_name,
+      "texts_in_string_terminal: '{}' is not a LARK terminal name", name);
+}
+
+// Appends `text` as a literal for a /-delimited LARK regex.
+static void append_regex_literal(std::string& out, std::string_view text) {
+  for (char c : text) {
+    // Raw newline/CR would split the line-oriented LARK rule mid-regex.
+    if (c == '\n') {
+      out += "\\n";
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (c == '\r') {
+      out += "\\r";
+      continue;
+    }
+    // Other control bytes and DEL mirror escape_lark_string: a raw NUL
+    // truncates the spec at the C-string boundary, and the LARK lexer
+    // forbids raw control bytes; \uXXXX matches the byte's code point.
+    auto byte = static_cast<unsigned char>(c);
+    if (byte < 0x20 || byte == 0x7F) {
+      out += fmt::format("\\u{:04x}", byte);
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (std::string_view("\\^$.|?*+()[]{}/").find(c) != std::string_view::npos) {
+      out += '\\';
+    }
+    out += c;
+  }
+}
+
+std::string texts_in_string_terminal(
+    std::string_view name, std::span<const std::string_view> texts) {
+  require_lark_terminal_name(name);
+  TRON_ASSERT(!texts.empty(), "texts_in_string_terminal({}): no texts", name);
+  std::string out = std::string(name) + ": /.*(";
+  for (size_t i = 0; i < texts.size(); ++i) {
+    // Precondition (see the declaration): callers drop empty entries.
+    TRON_ASSERT(
+        !texts[i].empty(), "texts_in_string_terminal({}): text {} is empty", name, i);
+    if (i > 0) out += '|';
+    append_regex_literal(out, texts[i]);
+  }
+  out += ").*/s\n";
+  return out;
+}
+
+// Appends `text` to `texts` unless already present; returns whether it was
+// appended. Grammar builders use it to keep exclusion alternations
+// duplicate-free in first-seen order (texts_in_string_terminal accepts
+// duplicates; derivre folds equal alternatives, so a duplicate adds grammar
+// bytes against MAX_GRAMMAR_BYTES and construction work, not DFA states).
+static bool push_unique(std::vector<std::string_view>& texts, std::string_view text) {
+  if (std::find(texts.begin(), texts.end(), text) != texts.end()) return false;
+  texts.push_back(text);
+  return true;
+}

+// Normalize explicit CPU requests before comparing them with role resources;
+// malformed lists must fail without reaching the mutating legacy CPU parser.
+static bool dice_cpu_list(const std::string& value, std::set<int>& cpus) {
+  if (value.empty()) return false;
+  std::istringstream input(value);
+  std::string part;
+  while (std::getline(input, part, ',')) {
+    auto dash = part.find('-');
+    auto parse = [](const std::string& text, int& result) {
+      auto parsed = std::from_chars(text.data(), text.data() + text.size(), result);
+      return parsed.ec == std::errc() && parsed.ptr == text.data() + text.size() &&
+             result >= 0 &&
+             result <= hwloc_bitmap_last(hwloc_topology_get_complete_cpuset(topology));
+    };
+    int first, last;
+    if (!parse(part.substr(0, dash), first)) return false;
+    last = first;
+    if (dash != std::string::npos && !parse(part.substr(dash + 1), last)) return false;
+    if (last < first) return false;
+    for (int cpu = first; cpu <= last; ++cpu)
+      cpus.insert(cpu);
+  }
+  return !cpus.empty() && value.back() != ',';
+}
+
+// Include actual SMT siblings, never adjacent logical CPUs. The resource
+// map's peer list may include additional sibling capacity beyond tron_cores.
+static std::set<int> dice_role_cpus(const std::string& base, const std::string& peers) {
+  std::set<int> result, peer_sources;
+  dice_cpu_list(base, result);
+  dice_cpu_list(peers, peer_sources);
+  for (int cpu : peer_sources) {
+    auto pu = hwloc_get_pu_obj_by_os_index(topology, cpu);
+    auto core =
+        pu ? hwloc_get_ancestor_obj_by_type(topology, HWLOC_OBJ_CORE, pu) : nullptr;
+    if (!core) continue;
+    int sibling = -1;
+    while ((sibling = hwloc_bitmap_next(core->cpuset, sibling)) >= 0)
+      if (sibling != cpu) result.insert(sibling);
+  }
+  return result;
+}
+
+// Read either trusted or candidate map data without replacing the active
+// manager. Invalid caller YAML becomes a reported conflict, not an assertion.
+static bool dice_map_resources(
+    const YAML::Node& node, const std::vector<int>& slots, instance_resources& result) {
+  try {
+    auto join = [&](const char* key, bool optional = false) {
+      if (optional && !node[key]) return std::string();
+      std::string value;
+      for (int slot : slots) {
+        auto entry = node[key][slot];
+        if (!entry || !entry.IsScalar())
+          throw YAML::RepresentationException(
+              node.Mark(), std::string("invalid ") + key);
+        if (!value.empty()) value += ',';
+        value += entry.as<std::string>();
+      }
+      return value;
+    };
+    result.devices = join("devices");
+    result.app = join("tron_cores");
+    result.dev = join("dev_cores");
+    result.helper = join("helper_cores", true);
+    result.peer = node["peer_cores"] ? join("peer_cores") : result.app;
+    result.diagnostic =
+        node["platform_cores"] ? node["platform_cores"].as<std::string>() : "0";
+    for (int slot : slots)
+      result.numa.push_back(node["numa_nodes"][slot].as<int>());
+    return !result.devices.empty() && !result.app.empty() && !result.dev.empty();
+  } catch (const YAML::Exception&) {
+    return false;
+  }
+}
+
+// Every placement rejection identifies both sides and the grant so the
+// caller can remove the conflicting override or request a compatible instance.
+static bool dice_conflict(const std::string& flag,
+    const std::string& requested,
+    const std::string& permitted) {
+  const char* id = std::getenv("DICE_GRANT_ID");
+  spdlog::error("Dice grant {}: {} requested '{}'; permitted {}. Remove this override "
+                "or request an instance with compatible resources.",
+      id ? id : "<missing>", flag, requested, permitted);
+  return false;
+}

+// Cleanup first touches the exact base path, so matching only its parent
+// would allow deleting another slice's inactive file. Resolve the complete base.
+bool dice_validate_hugepage_path(const std::string& path, const std::string& flag) {
+  if (!dice_grant_active()) return true;
+  std::error_code requested_error, default_error;
+  const auto requested = std::filesystem::weakly_canonical(path, requested_error);
+  const auto permitted =
+      std::filesystem::weakly_canonical(default_hugepage_file, default_error);
+  if (!path.empty() && !requested_error && !default_error && requested == permitted)
+    return true;
+  return dice_conflict(flag, path,
+      fmt::format("cleanup base '{}' (equivalent canonical "
+                  "paths are supported)",
+          default_hugepage_file));
+}

+// Snapshot the installed map or existing hardcoded fallback before reading
+// any custom map. Preserve this baseline even after live CPU pools are consumed.
+static bool dice_prepare_placement() {
+  if (!dice_grant_env_complete()) {
+    spdlog::error("Incomplete Dice grant environment; launch through Dice again");
+    return false;
+  }
+  std::vector<int> slots;
+  if (!parse_dice_slots(slots))
+    return dice_conflict("DICE_SLOTS", "invalid", "slot IDs");
+  std::sort(slots.begin(), slots.end());
+  const std::string identity = std::getenv("DICE_GRANT_ID");
+  if (dice_placement.identity == identity && dice_placement.slots == slots) return true;
+
+  dice_placement_state next;
+  next.identity = identity;
+  next.slots = slots;
+  server_type.clear();
+  if (resource_map_manager::load_resource_map_exact(
+          std::string("/opt/positron/config/") + default_resource_map_config)) {
+    server_type = get_server_type();
+    if (!server_type.empty()) {
+      resource_map_manager::set_server_type(server_type);
+      next.trusted_server = resource_map_manager::get_server_config();
+    }
+  }
+  const int total = get_total_slices();
+  const int width = slots.size();
+  if (width == 0 || total % width != 0 || slots.front() % width != 0 ||
+      slots.back() >= total ||
+      std::adjacent_find(slots.begin(), slots.end(),
+          [](int left, int right) { return right != left + 1; }) != slots.end())
+    return dice_conflict("DICE_SLOTS", fmt::format("{}", slots),
+        fmt::format("one supported contiguous instance within 0-{}", total - 1));
+  next.id = slots.front() / width;
+  next.count = total / width;
+  if (next.trusted_server) {
+    const auto shapes = resource_map_manager::get_instance_slices();
+    if (next.count > (int)shapes.size() || shapes[next.count - 1] != width ||
+        !dice_map_resources(next.trusted_server, slots, next.permitted))
+      return dice_conflict(
+          "DICE_SLOTS", fmt::format("{}", slots), "trusted map shapes");
+  } else if (!instance_resources_hardcoded(next.id, next.count, next.permitted)) {
+    return dice_conflict(
+        "DICE_SLOTS", fmt::format("{}", slots), "supported fallback shapes");
+  }
+  dice_placement = std::move(next);
+  return true;
+}
+
+// Alternate filenames are supported only for equivalent selected-slice
+// topology. Compare normalized resources against the independently trusted copy.
+static bool dice_equivalent_map(const std::string& path) {
+  try {
+    auto root = YAML::LoadFile(path);
+    const auto& trusted = dice_placement.trusted_server;
+    if (root["server_types"]) {
+      for (auto entry : root["server_types"]) {
+        auto candidate = entry.second;
+        bool same = true;
+        same &= candidate["physical_cores"].as<int>() == get_physical_cores() &&
+                candidate["num_numa_nodes"].as<int>() == get_num_numa_nodes() &&
+                candidate["vendor"].as<std::string>() == get_cpu_vendor();
+        const auto shapes = candidate["instance_slices"].as<std::vector<int>>();
+        if (trusted) {
+          same &= shapes == trusted["instance_slices"].as<std::vector<int>>();
+        } else {
+          // A missing installed map still has an independent hardcoded baseline;
+          // permit an equivalent map without letting it redefine slice geometry.
+          for (size_t i = 0; i < shapes.size(); ++i)
+            same &= shapes[i] == get_slices_per_n_instances_hardcoded(i + 1);
+          same &= shapes.size() >= (size_t)dice_placement.count;
+        }
+        if (!same) continue;
+        for (int slot : dice_placement.slots) {
+          instance_resources wanted, allowed;
+          if (!dice_map_resources(candidate, {slot}, wanted) ||
+              (trusted ? !dice_map_resources(trusted, {slot}, allowed)
+                       : !instance_resources_hardcoded(
+                             slot, get_total_slices(), allowed))) {
+            same = false;
+            break;
+          }
+          auto devices = [](const std::string& text) {
+            auto values = parse_device_list(text);
+            return std::set<device_tuple_t>(values.begin(), values.end());
+          };
+          same &= devices(wanted.devices) == devices(allowed.devices) &&
+                  wanted.numa == allowed.numa;
+          for (auto pair :
+              {std::pair{wanted.app, allowed.app}, std::pair{wanted.dev, allowed.dev},
+                  std::pair{wanted.helper, allowed.helper},
+                  std::pair{wanted.peer, allowed.peer},
+                  std::pair{wanted.diagnostic, allowed.diagnostic}}) {
+            std::set<int> requested, permitted;
+            same &= (pair.first.empty() || dice_cpu_list(pair.first, requested)) &&
+                    (pair.second.empty() || dice_cpu_list(pair.second, permitted)) &&
+                    requested == permitted;
+          }
+        }
+        if (same) return true;
+      }
+    }
+  } catch (const YAML::Exception&) {
+    // A malformed custom map cannot become the authority for its own request.
+  }
+  return dice_conflict("--resource-map", path,
+      fmt::format("a map with the same selected devices, CPU roles and NUMA nodes as "
+                  "{} for slots {}",
+          dice_placement.trusted_server ? resource_map_manager::get_resource_map_path()
+                                        : "the installed hardcoded fallback",
+          dice_placement.slots));
+}

+// These are the native placement settings whose accepted values must be
+// replayed after instance defaults. Ordinary payload arguments remain unexamined.
+static bool dice_placement_option(const std::string& flag) {
+  return flag == "--devices" || flag == "--app-cores" || flag == "--dev-cores" ||
+         flag == "--helper-cores" || flag == "--numa" || flag == "--tracer-core" ||
+         flag == "--hugepage_file";
+}
+
+static bool dice_validate_option(const std::string& flag, const std::string& value) {
+  // Compare every explicit request, including ones a later environment value
+  // would supersede, before applying any binding, device selection or cleanup path.
+  const auto& allowed = dice_placement.permitted;
+  if (flag == "--instance") {
+    if (parse_instance_string(value) ==
+        std::pair{dice_placement.id, dice_placement.count})
+      return true;
+    return dice_conflict(flag, value,
+        fmt::format("--instance {},{} (slots {})", dice_placement.id,
+            dice_placement.count, dice_placement.slots));
+  }
+  if (flag == "--resource-map") return dice_equivalent_map(value);
+  if (flag == "--hugepage_file") return dice_validate_hugepage_path(value, flag);
+  if (flag == "--devices") {
+    const auto wanted = parse_device_list(value);
+    const auto permitted = parse_device_list(allowed.devices);
+    if (!wanted.empty() && value.back() != ',' &&
+        std::all_of(wanted.begin(), wanted.end(), [&](auto device) {
+          return std::find(permitted.begin(), permitted.end(), device) !=
+                 permitted.end();
+        }))
+      return true;
+    return dice_conflict(flag, value, allowed.devices);
+  }
+  if (flag == "--numa") {
+    int node = -2;
+    auto parsed = std::from_chars(value.data(), value.data() + value.size(), node);
+    const std::set<int> permitted(allowed.numa.begin(), allowed.numa.end());
+    bool compatible =
+        parsed.ec == std::errc() && parsed.ptr == value.data() + value.size();
+    if (compatible && node == SYSTEM_NUMA_ALL) {
+      // ALL expands to host nodes; it cannot widen a partial-node grant.
+      int id = -1;
+      const auto nodes = hwloc_topology_get_complete_nodeset(topology);
+      while ((id = hwloc_bitmap_next(nodes, id)) >= 0)
+        compatible &= permitted.contains(id);
+    } else {
+      compatible &= permitted.contains(node);
+    }
+    if (compatible) return true;
+    return dice_conflict(flag, value, fmt::format("NUMA nodes {}", permitted));
+  }
+  if (flag == "--app-cores" || flag == "--dev-cores" || flag == "--helper-cores" ||
+      flag == "--tracer-core") {
+    auto app = dice_role_cpus(allowed.app, allowed.peer);
+    auto dev = dice_role_cpus(allowed.dev, allowed.dev);
+    auto helper =
+        allowed.helper.empty() ? app : dice_role_cpus(allowed.helper, allowed.helper);
+    auto permitted = flag == "--dev-cores"      ? dev
+                     : flag == "--helper-cores" ? helper
+                                                : app;
+    if (flag == "--tracer-core") {
+      // Diagnostics may share the map's platform cores as well as the grant's
+      // own roles; that exception does not widen application or driver placement.
+      permitted.insert(dev.begin(), dev.end());
+      permitted.insert(helper.begin(), helper.end());
+      auto diagnostic = dice_role_cpus(allowed.diagnostic, allowed.diagnostic);
+      permitted.insert(diagnostic.begin(), diagnostic.end());
+      if (value == "-1") return true;  // Existing explicit tracer-disable setting.
+    }
+    std::set<int> wanted;
+    int tracer = -1;
+    const auto parsed =
+        std::from_chars(value.data(), value.data() + value.size(), tracer);
+    const bool tracer_valid =
+        flag != "--tracer-core" ||
+        (parsed.ec == std::errc() && parsed.ptr == value.data() + value.size());
+    bool valid =
+        tracer_valid && dice_cpu_list(value, wanted) &&
+        (flag != "--tracer-core" || wanted.size() == 1) &&
+        std::includes(permitted.begin(), permitted.end(), wanted.begin(), wanted.end());
+    for (int cpu : wanted)
+      valid &= hwloc_get_pu_obj_by_os_index(topology, cpu) != nullptr;
+    // An empty helper list explicitly selects the existing app fallback.
+    if (flag == "--helper-cores" && value.empty()) return true;
+    if (valid) return true;
+    return dice_conflict(flag, value, fmt::format("{} CPUs {}", flag, permitted));
+  }
+  return true;
+}
